teeth-falling.name: teeth falling out
teeth-falling.title: What does it mean to dream about teeth falling out?
teeth-falling.lead: The most common reading of a teeth-falling-out dream isn't that something is wrong with your body. It's a daytime feeling of tension, of not being able to hold on or being afraid of losing something. In dreams, teeth are often tied to speaking, image, and strength, so losing them usually reflects a sense that you've been running out of strength in some matter lately.
teeth-falling.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly link losing teeth to elders or relatives at home. Some read it as quarrels and gossip, or as losing someone you rely on. Another widely repeated reading is that it shows you worry about saying the wrong thing or hurting your image. The versions differ a great deal. Some lean toward family, others toward reputation, and there is no single conclusion. Traditionally, this kind of dream is mostly about relationships and things weighing on your mind. It doesn't mean something will happen in real life.
teeth-falling.plain: This dream often shows up when you've talked a lot during the day, have to speak in front of people or negotiate, or are stuck in a relationship where it's hard to speak up. It can also come when you've been especially conscious of your appearance, performance, or stamina, and worry you can't keep it up. Loose teeth, one tooth lost, or many lost can feel very different: loose teeth feel like "I can't hold on much longer," while losing them all feels like "my whole image has collapsed." It's more like stress acting out "I'm afraid of losing control" for you. It isn't a forecast. If you keep having this kind of dream and aren't sleeping well, it may help to talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of teeth falling out with blood
variants.a: Blood makes the scene more intense. It usually matches something in your day that made you feel hurt or made you "pay a price," such as being criticized or being unable to let go after an argument. The point is the thing that hurt, not the blood itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of teeth falling out without pain
variants.a: No pain is often seen in situations of slow loosening, like a relationship or job that is quietly changing and that you haven't faced directly yet. The dream just magnifies that silent change for you.

variants.q: Dreaming of many teeth falling out
variants.a: Losing many teeth at once usually comes during a time when stress is concentrated and things are piling up, for example when you're juggling work and family at the same time. It reflects the exhaustion of carrying too much at once.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else's teeth falling out
variants.a: Dreaming of someone else losing teeth is often connected to worry about that person or a sense of distance from them. It may also project words you haven't dared to say. Think about whether someone has been on your mind lately.

teeth-falling.ask: If you dreamed about a particular person, or about something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
teeth-falling.askQ: How will the matter I can't let go of develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of teeth falling out mean something will happen to my family?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link lost teeth to family members, but that is an older generation's way of making associations and doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more worthwhile to ask whether you've been especially concerned about a family member lately, or haven't been in touch for a long time.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming of teeth falling out?
faq.a: Start by looking at whether you have long-standing pressure you can't voice during the day, such as frustration at work or in a relationship. Writing down the dream and how you felt that day can help. If it recurs enough to disturb your sleep, you can talk with a doctor.

snake.name: snake
snake.title: What does it mean to dream about a snake?
snake.lead: Dreaming of a snake is mostly tied to a feeling of being a bit afraid but unable to stop paying attention. In dreams, a snake often stands for someone around you who puts you on alert, a problem you haven't dealt with, or an emotion you've been holding down.
snake.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree a lot about snakes. Some say a snake means wealth or a turning point, some say it means a petty person or gossip, and another reading ties it to the body and desire. Versions even contradict each other, and the same kind of snake can mean different things in different editions. Traditionally it's mostly treated as a reminder to pay attention to the people and matters around you. It doesn't mean something will happen in real life.
snake.plain: This dream often appears when something about a certain person feels off to you but you can't say what, or when something at work has never been laid out openly. It may also mean you're suppressing an emotion, such as anger, attraction, or wanting to say no without having spoken up. What the snake does matters: coiled quietly is like "not erupted yet," chasing you is like "pressure closing in," and biting you is like "already stung." It's more like your daytime alertness acted out, not a forecast. If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you aren't sleeping well, it may help to talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of a snake biting you
variants.a: Being bitten usually matches being stung by a remark or event during the day, such as being misunderstood or taken advantage of. The dream magnifies that feeling of not having time to defend yourself. The point is the thing that made you uncomfortable.

variants.q: Dreaming of many snakes
variants.a: A pile of snakes often shows up when you feel there's a lot of trouble and people to deal with from every direction, as if several things are chasing you at once. It reflects a sense of overload, not disaster.

variants.q: Dreaming of a snake in the house
variants.a: A snake in the house is often tied to how much you care about family relationships. A family member may be on your mind, or something at home has never been talked through. Think about the atmosphere at home lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a snake
variants.a: Being chased is a very typical dream, usually matching something you've been trying to avoid or put off. What chases you isn't necessarily bad. It may be a responsibility or a conversation you aren't ready to face yet.

snake.ask: If the snake in your dream reminds you of a particular person, or of something you've kept putting aside, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
snake.askQ: What will happen next with the person around me who puts me on alert?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a snake mean good fortune with money?
faq.a: Some versions link snakes with wealth, but others say a snake is a petty person, so there's no agreed reading. Rather than treating it as a money signal, notice whether you felt fear or curiosity toward the snake in the dream. That's closer to your state during the day.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a snake mean someone wants to harm me?
faq.a: Some people make that association traditionally, but it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more practical reading is that you've been especially sensitive about a certain person or matter, and the dream let your alertness out.

ex-partner.name: ex-partner
ex-partner.title: What does it mean to dream about an ex-partner?
ex-partner.lead: Dreaming of an ex-partner is mostly not a sign that they still think of you. It usually means a relationship in your heart hasn't been fully put away. It could be regret, curiosity, comparison, or just a recent scene that stirred up old memories.
ex-partner.trad: In folk dream readings, dreaming of a former lover is often read as something in your heart being unfinished. Some say it means you'll soon hear news of someone from the past, and another reading takes it as a reminder not to compare the past with the present. The versions vary, some leaning toward emotional ties, others toward meeting people again, with no settled conclusion. Traditionally it's mostly treated as something weighing on your mind. It doesn't mean something will happen in real life.
ex-partner.plain: This kind of dream often shows up when your feelings have been stirred up lately, when life is changing, or when you come across a familiar place. It can also mean something in your current relationship hasn't been said out loud, and part of you is quietly comparing it with the past. It matters whether the ex in the dream is warm or cold, whether you get back together or fight: warm is more like "missing who I was then," and cold is more like "there's still something left unsaid." It's more a way of sorting through old feelings than a sign that the person is coming back. If dreams like this keep returning and weigh on your mood, it can help to talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting back together with an ex
variants.a: Getting-back-together dreams often come when you feel a little unsure about your life now. What you miss is usually not the person, but the simpler time when you felt needed. You can ask yourself what's missing for you right now.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ex ignoring you
variants.a: A cold ex often points to a knot inside you that hasn't come undone, such as something that was never made clear or an apology that was never said. The dream replays that feeling of getting no response.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ex with a new partner
variants.a: Dreams like this are mostly about comparing yourself with others. You may not be happy with how you're doing lately. What matters isn't whether the ex has a new partner, but how you see yourself now.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ex getting married
variants.a: A wedding scene often stands for "something has officially ended." If you've recently let go of a part of your past, this dream may also be your mind putting a full stop on that relationship.

ex-partner.ask: If you dreamed of one particular person, or of something in that relationship you still can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
ex-partner.askQ: What will happen next with the thing I can't let go of about my ex?

faq.q: Does dreaming of my ex mean he or she still thinks of me?
faq.a: The dream is your own and doesn't show what the other person is feeling. Some people link them in the traditional view, but there's no basis for it in real life. What's more worth looking at is whether something recently reminded you of who you were in that relationship.

faq.q: If I dream of my ex, will my current partner get jealous?
faq.a: You don't need to rush to explain the dream to your partner. What matters is how you feel. If the dream shows you something unspoken in your current relationship, that can be a good thread to talk about.

exam.name: exams
exam.title: What does it mean to dream about an exam?
exam.lead: Dreaming of an exam is usually tied to feeling tested. It doesn't have to mean a real exam is coming. Something during the day may have made you feel graded, compared, or afraid of not doing well enough.
exam.trad: In the folk dream books, dreaming of an exam is often read as pressure and a fear of not getting through. Some say an important matter is coming up, and others link it to reputation, grades, or being recognized. The many versions differ: some lean toward anxiety, some toward opportunity, and there is no single conclusion. Traditionally it is mostly taken as a reminder not to be so tense, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.
exam.plain: This dream often comes around performance reviews, interviews, presentations, parent-teacher meetings, or anytime someone will be watching how you do. It may also be that you hold yourself to a high standard and feel even rest is slacking. It matters whether the paper is blank, you can't find the exam room, or you run out of time: blank is like "not ready yet," not finding the room is like "not knowing where the bar is," and running out of time is like "too much to do." It's more a replay of your daytime self-demands than a prediction. If dreams like this keep returning and you're sleeping badly, it can help to talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of not knowing the answers on an exam
variants.a: A blank paper or not knowing how to answer often matches something during the day that you feel unsure or unprepared about, like a new task or a conversation you need to start. The dream magnifies that uneasy feeling.

variants.q: Dreaming of being late for an exam
variants.a: Being-late dreams are mostly about time pressure. Is your schedule packed lately, so that you always feel behind? It reflects a pace that's too tight, not that you'll actually miss something.

variants.q: Dreaming of doing very well on an exam
variants.a: Doing well isn't necessarily an omen. It more often appears when you've just finished something and feel relieved, a continuation of your own self-affirmation.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding the exam room
variants.a: Not finding the exam room often matches feeling unclear about where the rules or standards are, such as in a new environment, with a new boss, or in a new relationship. You can start by figuring out who exactly you're being measured against.

exam.ask: If the exam in your dream made you think of something being put to the test, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
exam.askQ: How will the thing I've been tested on lately go from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of an exam mean I'll fail?
faq.a: Some people connect exam dreams with success or failure in the traditional view, but in real life it doesn't show a result. A more practical reading is that you care a lot about how you perform on something, and the dream played out your tension.

faq.q: I'm not studying, so why dream of an exam?
faq.a: It's very common. The exam in a dream doesn't have to be at school. It can be the feeling of being graded at work, in a relationship, or in your family. You can think about whose opinion has mattered to you especially lately.

pregnancy.name: pregnancy
pregnancy.title: What does it mean to dream about pregnancy?
pregnancy.lead: Dreaming of pregnancy is mostly about something taking shape. It doesn't have to mean you really want a baby. A plan, an idea, or a relationship in you may be slowly growing, or you may simply be curious about changes in the body.
pregnancy.trad: In the folk dream books, dreaming of pregnancy is often read as happy news or a new beginning. Some say a wish is taking shape in you, and others link it to money or family. The many versions differ: some lean toward celebration, some toward worry, and there is no single conclusion. Traditionally it is mostly taken as a symbol, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.
pregnancy.plain: This dream often comes when you're waiting on a result, such as a case, a relationship, or a plan that's still at the stage of not yet taking shape. You may also be especially aware of your body, your age, or your role in the family. It matters whether you're happy, panicked, or don't know who the father is: happy is like looking forward to something, panic is like fearing you can't carry the responsibility, and not knowing is like not yet being clear on what you want. It's more a replay of daytime hopes and unease than a prediction. If dreams like this keep returning and weigh on your mood, it can help to talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of being pregnant
variants.a: Dreaming of being pregnant often matches something in your hands that is still growing, like a new job, relationship, or idea. You can think about what lately makes you both hopeful and a little afraid.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else being pregnant
variants.a: Someone else being pregnant is often tied to how you observe or compare yourself with that person. It may also project a role you want, or one you don't want to take on. What matters is how you felt when you saw it.

variants.q: Dreaming of being pregnant but never giving birth
variants.a: Being pregnant for a long time without giving birth often shows up when something is stuck in the preparation stage. You've put a lot in but haven't seen a result yet, so it's natural to feel anxious.

variants.q: Dreaming of being pregnant and miscarrying
variants.a: These dreams are vivid, and some people traditionally link them to worry, but in real life they don't mean anything will happen. More often it's a fear that something you're working on won't hold. You could start by looking at what you've been looking after lately.

pregnancy.ask: If the pregnancy in your dream reminds you of a person or project that's still taking shape, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
pregnancy.askQ: What will happen next with this thing of mine that's still taking shape?

faq.q: If I dream about being pregnant, will I really become pregnant?
faq.a: Some people make that connection traditionally, but dreams and real life aren't necessarily linked. It's more useful to ask whether you're waiting on a result lately, or are especially aware of your body or your role in your family.

faq.q: What if I dreamed of being pregnant and felt scared?
faq.a: Fear usually points to worry about not being able to carry a responsibility. It isn't necessarily about having a child; it could be a new task or a new relationship. You could start by asking yourself which kind of responsibility you're worried about.

dead-person.name: dead people
dead-person.title: What does it mean to dream about dead people?
dead-person.lead: Dreaming of dead people is mostly not a bad thing, and it isn't an omen. Traditional dream interpretation has many views on these dreams, but in everyday life they more often reflect something on your mind, such as a relationship or a matter you care about, or a period of change in your life.
dead-person.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this about seeing dead people in a dream: some versions read it as "an old matter is finished and a new page is turning," some as "there are words left unsaid," and some say that dreaming of a deceased relative means missing them. The versions differ quite a bit and even contradict each other, which shows there is no single answer for this kind of dream. Tradition also reminds us that dreams of dead people, illness, or teeth falling out don't mean anything will happen in real life.
dead-person.plain: You may dream of dead people after thinking of someone you haven't contacted in a long time, passing a place where you used to live, or sorting through old belongings. You may also be letting go of a relationship or a role and feel a little reluctant. The "dead person" in a dream is often just a figure from your memory, and doesn't mean anything will happen. If the feelings in the dream were strong and you woke up feeling heavy, you could notice whether something has been left unresolved lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a deceased relative coming back
variants.a: This is common when you miss them especially strongly, or when something big is happening in your life and you wish you could talk it over with someone. What happens between you in the dream mostly reflects what you want to say to them, not something they are communicating.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead person coming back to life
variants.a: This often appears when you want to repair a relationship or restart something you set aside. It may also be that you haven't yet accepted a change, and your mind keeps rehearsing it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead person speaking
variants.a: The words you hear in a dream are usually thoughts you already had, just spoken in a different voice. After waking, you can think about whether those words sound like what you've been telling yourself lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of many dead people
variants.a: You may have taken in too much heavy news lately, or be facing a lot of old matters at once. It doesn't mean something will go wrong. It's more like your mind is processing too much at one time.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead person laughing
variants.a: This is mostly about relief, perhaps because something that weighed on you has settled. The laughter in the dream may also simply be a projection of your wish for that person to be well.

dead-person.ask: If the person in your dream is hard to let go of, or something keeps weighing on your mind, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
dead-person.askQ: How will this thing I can't let go of develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of dead people mean something will happen to someone close to me?
faq.a: Some people make that connection traditionally, but it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. These dreams are more often related to missing someone, stress, or changes in life. If you dream of this repeatedly and aren't sleeping well, you could talk to a doctor.

faq.q: A deceased relative spoke to me in my dream. Should I do what they said?
faq.a: The words in a dream are usually your own inner voice. You can take them as a reminder to think about what you've been caring about lately, rather than as an instruction to carry out.

flying.name: flying
flying.title: What does it mean to dream about flying?
flying.lead: Dreaming of flying is mostly about wanting to get free of something, or feeling that you can do it. Traditional dream interpretation has many views on flying, but in real life it often appears when you want to break through or catch your breath.
flying.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this about dreaming of flying: some versions read it as "a wish is fulfilled and things go smoothly," some as "wanting to leave home or escape the current situation," and some say the higher you fly, the more you should be careful not to get carried away. The versions vary, and some are even opposite, so treat them only as a reference.
flying.plain: If you've been feeling stifled at work or in life, you may start flying in your dreams, as if finding yourself an outlet. Or you may have just finished something and feel confident, so the flying feels easy. Whether the flight goes smoothly, or whether you're afraid of heights, often reflects how sure you feel about the change in front of you. This kind of dream doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like a thermometer for your mood.

variants.q: Dreaming of flying very high
variants.a: This often appears when you want to prove yourself or have just taken a step forward. Flying high may also reflect a worry about falling, so notice whether you're putting too much pressure on yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to fly
variants.a: This is mostly about feeling unable to put in effort. Perhaps something is stuck, or you feel you aren't prepared enough. It isn't a bad omen, just your mind saying, "I need a little more time."

variants.q: Dreaming of flying and then falling
variants.a: This is common when expectations are high and you fear they'll come to nothing. Falling in the dream is mostly an extension of the tension you felt during the day, and doesn't mean things will fail.

variants.q: Dreaming of flying with someone else
variants.a: Maybe you've been looking after someone lately, or guiding them, or trying to give someone a hand up. Or maybe you wish someone would walk forward with you.

flying.ask: If the feeling of flying reminds you of something you're trying to break through, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
flying.askQ: Will the thing I've been trying to break through make progress in the days ahead?

faq.q: Does dreaming of flying mean I'm going to make it big?
faq.a: Some people say so in the tradition, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life. Flying dreams are more often tied to confidence, a wish to be free, or stress, so it's more useful to treat the dream as a clue about your mood.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of flying but feel afraid?
faq.a: The fear usually comes from feeling unsure about a change during the day. Think about what lately leaves you both excited and nervous. That feeling is often where the dream comes from.

being-chased.name: being chased
being-chased.title: What does it mean to dream about being chased?
being-chased.lead: Dreaming of being chased is one of the most common dreams. It usually has to do with something you've been avoiding during the day, or with stress that has built up. Traditional dream interpretation has many views, but in real life it's usually not an omen. It's more a nudge from inside to face something.
being-chased.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this about being chased: some editions read it as "quarrels or worries," others as "a turn for the better is coming; if you got away, all is well," and some say being chased means "someone is pressing you from behind." The editions differ a lot, so take them only as a reference, not as something to believe.
being-chased.plain: If something has been dragging on and you haven't dared to face it, or someone is putting pressure on you, you're more likely to be chased in a dream. You may also simply be so tense during the day that even in sleep you're "on standby." Who is chasing you, and whether you outrun them, often reflects how much in control you feel about the matter. This kind of dream doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like stress looking for a way out.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a bad person
variants.a: This often shows up when you feel something is a threat but don't want to face it. The bad person may be your own image of that matter. It doesn't mean someone is really out to harm you.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased but unable to run
variants.a: This is often tied to a sense of powerlessness, perhaps feeling that no matter how hard you try, you're stuck. It isn't a bad sign. It's just your mind saying, "I need a different approach, or someone to help."

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by an animal
variants.a: Animals often stand for a certain emotion or instinct. For example, being chased by a dog may relate to a sense of responsibility or being rushed. Think about what lately makes you feel watched.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased and finally hiding
variants.a: You may be facing something but choosing to step away from it for now. Hiding isn't necessarily bad. Sometimes your mind is just asking for room to breathe.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased and then turning to chase the other person
variants.a: This often appears when you've decided not to give way anymore and want to take back the lead. It may also be that you're finally ready to deal with the matter head-on.

being-chased.ask: If the person or matter chasing you in the dream is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
being-chased.askQ: How will the thing I've been trying to avoid develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being chased mean someone is out to harm me?
faq.a: It doesn't mean that will happen in real life. Being-chased dreams mostly come from stress, procrastination, or tension with people. The one chasing you is often just the stress inside you taking a shape.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming of being chased?
faq.a: Start by thinking about what lately makes you want to run the most. Write it down and break it into smaller pieces. If you keep having nightmares or aren't sleeping well, you can talk to a doctor.

falling.name: falling
falling.title: What does it mean to dream about falling?
falling.lead: Dreaming of falling is often tied to a feeling of losing control, such as things not going to plan or worrying about an outcome. Traditional dream interpretation has many views, but in real life it's usually not an omen. It reflects your mood.
falling.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this about falling from a height: some editions read it as "a change in status or circumstances," others as "unease inside; steady yourself," and some say landing safely after the fall means "a false alarm." The editions don't agree, so take them only as a reference.
falling.plain: If something in your work, relationships, or life feels hard to pin down, you're more likely to fall in a dream. You may also be in a period of change, such as a move or waiting on a result, with things left hanging. The moment of falling often comes with waking up with a start. That's the body being tense and doesn't mean anything will happen. After waking, think about what lately makes you feel there's "no ground under your feet."

variants.q: Dreaming of falling from a height
variants.a: This often appears when you worry you won't be able to hold on to something you've achieved, such as an exam or your work performance. The fall is mostly an extension of daytime tension and doesn't mean the result will be bad.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing a step
variants.a: This may relate to a sudden sense of uncertainty, perhaps something is less certain than you thought. This dream is very common and is usually just stress or light sleep.

variants.q: Dreaming of falling into water
variants.a: Water often stands for emotion, so falling into water may reflect being swamped by some feeling lately. Think about whether something recently has felt like too much to handle.

variants.q: Dreaming of falling endlessly and not being able to stop
variants.a: This is often tied to a sense of losing control, perhaps feeling that things have gone beyond what you can handle. It isn't a bad sign. It's your mind calling out, "I need something to hold on to."

variants.q: Dreaming of falling and landing safely
variants.a: This often appears when you actually feel steady inside but are still tense. Landing safely is more like your confidence in yourself and doesn't mean things will necessarily go smoothly.

falling.ask: If the weightless, falling feeling in the dream reminds you of something that's waiting on a result, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
falling.askQ: How will the thing I've been waiting on turn out from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming about falling mean something bad will happen?
faq.a: Not in real life. Falling dreams are mostly tied to stress and uncertainty. They're very common, and there's no need to worry about them.

faq.q: Why do I suddenly feel like I'm falling just as I'm drifting off to sleep?
faq.a: It's a natural reaction of the body as it falls asleep, and many people have it. If it happens often and affects your sleep, you could talk to a doctor.

flood.name: flood
flood.title: What does it mean to dream about a flood?
flood.lead: Dreaming of a flood is often linked to feeling emotionally overfull, or having too much happen at once. Traditional dream interpretation says various things, but in real life it's usually not an omen. It more often reflects that you've been carrying a lot lately.
flood.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), the common sayings about a flood vary. Some versions read it as money or events being in motion, some as worry in your heart and a need to watch your words, and some say that floodwater receding means a matter will pass. The versions differ a lot, even contradicting each other, so take them only as a reference.
flood.plain: If you've been handling many things at once, or emotions have built up for a long time without being said, big water can easily show up in a dream. You may also be going through a change, such as a shift at work or in a relationship, and feel close to being swamped. Whether the water is clear and whether you got away often reflects how you feel about that pressure. This kind of dream doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like your mind letting off water.

variants.q: Dreaming of a flood rushing over you
variants.a: This often comes up when something feels like it's about to bear down on you and you can't get ready in time. Being overrun doesn't mean something will go wrong. It's more about how that pressure feels to you.

variants.q: Dreaming of a flood but being unharmed
variants.a: There may be real changes around you, but you feel you can hold up. Or you may be watching someone else's situation and feeling tense on their behalf.

variants.q: Dreaming of fleeing a flood
variants.a: This is mostly tied to wanting to avoid some kind of pressure, perhaps wanting to step back from something. Whether you can get away reflects how much room you feel you have.

variants.q: Dreaming of a flood receding
variants.a: This often appears when pressure starts to ease and things take a turn. The receding water is more like a feeling inside that it's almost over. It doesn't mean things will necessarily go smoothly.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming in water
variants.a: You may be working hard to keep your balance under pressure. How smoothly you swim often reflects whether you feel you can cope with what's in front of you.

flood.ask: If the flood in the dream reminds you of something weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
flood.askQ: How will the thing that's been weighing on me lately develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming about a flood mean a disaster is coming?
faq.a: Not in real life. Flood dreams are mostly tied to emotions, stress and changes in life. They're very common, and there's no need to think of disaster.

faq.q: Does dreaming about a flood mean good money luck?
faq.a: Some traditional versions say so, but there's no basis for it in real life. It's more practical to treat the dream as a clue about your mood, not as a way to judge your finances.

dog.name: dog
dog.title: What does it mean to dream about a dog? Common sayings and psychological readings
dog.lead: Dreaming of a dog is mostly tied to themes like loyalty, protection and personal boundaries. Traditional dream interpretation says various things, but in real life it more often reflects how you've been feeling about a relationship or a responsibility.
dog.trad: The common sayings in folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) are not uniform. Some versions see the dog as a symbol of guarding and watching over the home, so a dog means a reliable person is near you. Others say a barking or chasing dog hints at quarrels with someone or words left unsaid. Another view takes the dog as a symbol of a friend, so a dog coming close to you means a bond of friendship or cooperation. The versions differ a lot, and the same dream is explained differently in different regions, so take it as cultural interest.
dog.plain: During the day you may have something that makes you responsible to someone: a favor you promised, a pet you keep, a team you lead, or a relationship that needs your care. A dog in a dream often shows up when you're especially concerned about whether someone can be trusted, or whether you're holding your own boundaries. If the dog is friendly, it may reflect that you've felt supported lately. If you're chased or barked at, it's common that you're holding words back during the day, or feel someone is getting too close. Some people have simply watched dog videos or met a dog on the street, and the dream just replays the picture from the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dog following me everywhere
variants.a: A common reading is that you're concerned with clinginess and responsibility in a relationship. Someone may be leaning on you lately, or you can't let go of something. It may also be that you really did meet a relative's dog that day.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased or bitten by a dog
variants.a: Traditional sayings often link this to quarrels and conflict. In real life it more often matches feelings you haven't talked through during the day, or wariness toward someone. A bite is a scary image, but a dream doesn't mean anything will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of many dogs
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been dealing with many people and many requests at once and feel stretched thin. Some circulating versions lean toward "many people, many voices", which you can take as a bit of fun.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dog dying or being hurt
variants.a: Traditionally this is said to relate to losing support or a change in a relationship, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. More often it shows you're worried about a relationship or about someone you look after.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cute puppy
variants.a: This mostly comes with feelings of ease and being needed. You may want to be looked after lately, or be looking forward to a new beginning. It may also just be a heartwarming scene you saw during the day.

dog.ask: If the dog in the dream reminds you of a specific person, or of something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
dog.askQ: Will things change between me and that person in the coming time?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a dog mean someone around me is working against me?
faq.a: Some folk dream books do link a dog's barking to quarrels, but there are many versions and they contradict each other. What's more worth looking at in real life: are you especially on guard around someone lately, or is there something you haven't said out loud?

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of the same dog?
faq.a: A recurring dream is often tied to a feeling that hasn't been worked through yet. Notice whether the feeling in the dream is calm or tense. If it's keeping you from sleeping well or affecting your days, it can help to talk with a doctor.

cat.name: cat
cat.title: What does it mean to dream about a cat? Common views and a psychological reading
cat.lead: Dreaming of a cat is often linked to independence, intuition, and a relationship that's hard to read. Traditional views differ. In daily life, the dream tends to show up when you can't quite get a read on a person or a situation.
cat.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree quite a bit about cats. Some versions see the cat as a symbol of agility and alertness, so a cat in a dream means someone near you is observant. Others say a cat coming close or meowing hints that someone has a complaint about you or is quietly competing with you. Another version treats the cat as a symbol of the home, so a cat coming into the house means something at home needs attention. The versions vary widely, and the same dream often gets opposite readings, so it's best taken as cultural curiosity.
cat.plain: A cat in a dream often matches that hot-and-cold feeling: a relationship that hasn't been defined, a person whose mind you can't read, or your own wish to keep a little space. If you've been going back and forth over whether to make the first move, or what the other person really means, a cat can easily turn up in your dream. A cat can also stand for your own intuition. A very affectionate cat often appears when you've been feeling relaxed and accepted lately, while a cat that hides or scratches you often shows up when you feel misunderstood or want to protect yourself. Of course, if you have a cat at home or have been scrolling through cat videos, it may simply be leftover material from your day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cat staring at me
variants.a: It may reflect feeling watched or judged lately, or caring a lot about how a certain person sees you. Some traditional versions lean toward "someone is noticing you," which is fine to take as light entertainment.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scratched or bitten by a cat
variants.a: Often this means you felt offended during the day, or you're wary about a certain relationship. Traditional views often link it to small frictions, but a dream doesn't mean anything will happen. What matters is the discomfort you're carrying.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of cats
variants.a: This may match a time when you're handling many relationships at once and feel overloaded with information. It could also be that you saw a lot of cat images during the day and the dream pieced them together.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cat being affectionate and cuddly
variants.a: This usually comes with a feeling of relaxation and acceptance. You may be feeling at ease in some relationship lately, or longing for a bit more gentleness in how people treat you.

variants.q: Dreaming of a black cat
variants.a: Traditional versions don't agree about black cats: some lean toward caution, others toward protection. In real life, what's more common is being especially sensitive about something uncertain. It has nothing to do with good or bad luck.

cat.ask: If the cat in your dream made you think of a particular person, or a relationship that hasn't been made clear, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
cat.askQ: What does he really think of me?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a cat unlucky?
faq.a: Some folk versions do lean toward caution, but the versions contradict each other, and many treat the cat as a symbol of agility and intuition. In real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. What matters is what's been on your mind lately.

faq.q: If I dream a cat scratches me, does it mean I'll argue with someone?
faq.a: Some traditions link them that way, but a dream isn't a forecast. What's more worth looking at is whether you already have feelings about someone during the day, or feel a boundary has been crossed. That's what really needs attention.

fish.name: fish
fish.title: What does it mean to dream about fish?
fish.lead: Dreaming of fish is often connected to opportunity, flow, and ideas that haven't surfaced yet. A fish swimming in water is like a thought or plan taking shape in you, not yet ready to be put clearly into words.
fish.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common views. Fish swimming in water is seen as things moving forward and dealings going smoothly. Catching a fish is often read as effort being rewarded. Fish leaping out of the water is read differently: some versions see an opportunity appearing, while others warn that things may slip beyond your control. Versions also differ on the number and color of the fish. These are only traditional associations and don't mean anything will happen in real life.
fish.plain: Fish often appear when you're waiting for a result, such as a reply, some news, or for something to become clear. How clear the water is and how many fish there are often match how smoothly you've been feeling lately. It could also be a plan you haven't told anyone about, swimming around in your mind. Another common case is feeling a bit stuck in life and wanting more flow and change, and the dream uses fish to show that wish to move.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of fish
variants.a: You may have many ideas or opportunities in motion right now. It feels lively but also a bit messy, and you're not sure which one to grab first.

variants.q: Dreaming of catching fish
variants.a: Traditionally this is said to mean effort will pay off. In real life it more often reflects wanting to secure something left hanging, or being deeply committed to a goal.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead fish
variants.a: There's no need to treat it as a bad omen. This dream often shows up when the momentum behind a plan or relationship feels weaker and you feel a little let down.

variants.q: Dreaming of a fish leaping out of the water
variants.a: You may have come across news or an idea lately that caught your eye, or something may have suddenly started moving, leaving you both hopeful and nervous.

variants.q: Dreaming of murky water
variants.a: This often matches feeling that the current situation is unclear, that you don't have enough information, or that something is bothering you and you haven't found a thread to follow.

fish.ask: If the fish in your dream made you think of something you're waiting on, or a plan you haven't voiced yet, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
fish.askQ: Will I hear news about the thing I've been waiting for?

faq.q: Does dreaming about fish mean money is coming?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link fish with harvest, but in waking life it more often reflects how much you're putting into some goal. Take it as a nudge to keep going rather than a forecast.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about fish swimming in water?
faq.a: It often matches a recent feeling that your mood is moving more freely, or that something is slowly coming along. Clear water usually feels smooth, while muddy water may reflect that you still can't quite see things clearly.

money.name: money
money.title: What does it mean to dream about money? Common sayings and psychological readings
money.lead: Traditionally, dreaming about money is often tied to wealth luck, though versions differ. In waking life it more often reflects how much you've been weighing "is it enough, is it worth it" lately, and it may have nothing to do with your actual income.
money.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. One: finding or receiving money is said to mean income coming in or help from someone. Two: losing money or having it stolen is said to mean watching your spending or your relationships. Three: counting or handing out money is linked to responsibility and sharing things out. Some versions say that having money in a dream is instead a reminder to watch your wallet. The versions differ a lot and even contradict each other, so take it as cultural curiosity.
money.plain: In dreams, money is often not about money but a stand-in for "worth" and "security." Have you been tallying this month's expenses, worrying about job stability, or asking yourself again and again whether what you give is worth it? People who are troubled by money or by a choice during the day are especially likely to dream about it. Receiving money in a dream often shows up when you long to be recognized or repaid; losing money often appears when you feel your effort isn't being seen, or you've lost control over something. It may also be that you just made a transfer or looked at a bill, and the image slipped straight into your dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding money
variants.a: Traditional sayings often link this to an unexpected windfall. In waking life it more often matches a hope for some good news or compensation lately. The dream doesn't mean you'll really find money; the point is that part of you wants some return.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing money or having it stolen
variants.a: This often shows up when you feel your effort isn't paid back, or you worry something is slipping out of control. Some circulating versions lean toward a reminder to watch spending. Treat it as light reference and don't let it make you anxious.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of money or counting money
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been especially focused on income or resources lately, or that you're handling something that needs to be divided up. The numbers in a dream usually have no real meaning.

variants.q: Dreaming of giving money to others
variants.a: This is mostly about responsibility, caring for others, and sharing things out. You may have been giving to others for a while and feel a bit tired. You may also be trying to sort out boundaries in some relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of lending money to someone or borrowing from someone
variants.a: This often shows up when you're sensitive to "who owes whom" in a relationship. It may not be about money at all, but about favors. Some traditional sayings lean toward a warning, but a dream is not a forecast.

money.ask: If the money in your dream brings to mind an expense, a job, or a favor you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring some movement.
money.askQ: Will things go smoothly with this money or this job from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming about money mean I'm going to get rich?
faq.a: Circulating folk versions do often link dreaming about money to wealth luck, but they contradict each other, and some remind you to watch your wallet. In waking life it more often reflects how much you've been thinking about money and security lately.

faq.q: If I dream that my money is gone, will I lose money?
faq.a: Some people say so traditionally, but a dream is not a forecast. What's more worth looking at is whether you've been anxious during the day about an expense or a choice. Dealing with that anxiety helps more than worrying about the dream.

marriage.name: getting married
marriage.title: What does it mean to dream about getting married? Common sayings and psychological readings
marriage.lead: Traditionally, dreaming about getting married is often tied to changes in relationships and life stages, though versions differ. In waking life it more often reflects what you've been thinking lately about commitment, union, and settling down, and may have nothing to do with an actual wedding.
marriage.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. One: marriage is seen as union and a new stage, so dreaming of it means changes in life or closer ties with someone. Two: the person you marry in the dream isn't necessarily your real partner and may stand for a longing for some kind of stability. Three: some versions say that dreaming of a wedding ceremony or a lively scene relates to social obligations and responsibility. Some versions also link it to "a matter being settled." The versions differ a lot, so take it as cultural curiosity.
marriage.plain: Marriage in a dream often symbolizes "settling something": it might be a romantic commitment, but it might also be signing a contract at work, moving, or finally deciding something. If you're stuck during the day on "should I say yes" or "should I keep going," a wedding easily turns up in your dreams. Who the bride or groom is is often more interesting than the scene itself: marrying a stranger may reflect excitement or unease about an unknown stage; marrying an ex often shows up when you're still working through habits left over from that relationship. A lively wedding may also simply mean you recently attended a banquet or watched related videos.

variants.q: Dreaming of marrying a stranger
variants.a: It may reflect that you feel both hopeful and a little uneasy about a new stage, or that you long for a kind of stability you haven't pictured yet. Some traditional sayings lean toward change; treat it as light reference.

variants.q: Dreaming of marrying an ex
variants.a: This often shows up when you're still sorting through feelings or habits left by that relationship. It doesn't mean you want to get back together, and it doesn't mean anything will happen. What matters is whether you felt at ease or reluctant in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming that your own wedding is chaotic or goes wrong
variants.a: This mostly matches being tense lately about a decision, afraid you're not ready. Some traditional sayings lean toward a warning, but a dream is not a forecast. Break what's in front of you into smaller pieces first.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else getting married
variants.a: It may reflect that someone around you is entering a new stage and you're thinking about where you stand. It may also be that you heard a lot of news from friends during the day and the dream strung it together.

variants.q: Dreaming of marrying someone you know, or a friend
variants.a: This often shows up when there's some expectation or pressure of being "closer" between you and this person. It isn't necessarily romance; it could be cooperation or commitment. Look at how the two of you interact during the day.

marriage.ask: If the wedding in your dream brings someone to mind, or a decision that hasn't been settled yet, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring some movement.
marriage.askQ: Will things between him and me settle down from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming about getting married mean I'm going to get married?
faq.a: Folk dream books often link wedding dreams to changes in a relationship, but that's symbolism, not a forecast. What's worth looking at in waking life is whether you've been torn lately over a relationship or a decision.

faq.q: I dreamed I married my ex. Does that mean I haven't moved on?
faq.a: It might. It may also be that the relationship left behind a lot of daily habits, and the dream is replaying them. It doesn't mean you'll get back together, or that anything will happen. What matters is how you feel when you wake up.

getting-lost.name: getting lost
getting-lost.title: What does it mean to dream about getting lost?
getting-lost.lead: Dreaming of getting lost mostly reflects feeling unsure about direction or choices lately. It isn't necessarily predicting anything. Traditional dream readings say a few different things about getting lost, and the versions vary. In real life, it more often shows up alongside the feeling of not knowing what to do next.
getting-lost.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that getting lost has to do with things not yet being settled. Some versions say it means something is weighing on you and you can't find the thread. Others read it as "taking a different road may open a turning point." The versions differ quite a bit. Some lean toward relationships, others toward work, and there is no single conclusion. It's best taken as one way the old books helped people sort through their feelings.
getting-lost.plain: If you're stuck on a decision in the daytime, such as changing jobs, whether to move, or whether to bring something up, you may be more likely to dream of getting lost at night. It can also be that you've had too much information and too many options, and your mind can't put them in order. Whether you were searching for the way or simply stopped often matches your state in waking life: rushing to find an answer, or actually wanting to catch your breath first. This kind of dream is common around times of change. It doesn't mean something will happen. It's more of a nudge that the thing you care about most right now deserves some time to think through.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost in a familiar city
variants.a: The place is familiar, yet you can't find your way out. This is common when life hasn't changed much but something feels slightly off. It may relate to a subtle shift in a relationship or in the rhythm of your work.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost while driving
variants.a: This mostly has to do with the feeling of being in control of your direction, for example finding halfway through a plan that it isn't going as expected. It's common for people with many responsibilities who have to make their own decisions.

variants.q: Dreaming of being lost with no one to ask
variants.a: This often appears in times when you feel there's no one to talk things over with. It may reflect a sense of going it alone lately, and not necessarily anything about your actual relationships.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding the exit after getting lost
variants.a: This kind of dream often comes when part of you already has an answer. It's more like acting out the feeling of "I actually know what to do."

getting-lost.ask: If someone, or something you can't let go of, came to mind while you were lost in the dream, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
getting-lost.askQ: How will this matter I'm stuck on unfold from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of getting lost mean I'll fail?
faq.a: Traditional readings have no direct link like that, and the versions don't agree. In real life, it more often appears during times of hesitation or when you have too many options, and it doesn't necessarily relate to success or failure.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of getting lost?
faq.a: Start by noticing whether there's something you've been putting off deciding during the day. If the dream keeps recurring and affects your sleep, you can talk to a doctor. There's no need to frighten yourself.

being-bitten-by-snake.name: snake bite
being-bitten-by-snake.title: What does it mean to dream about being bitten by a snake?
being-bitten-by-snake.lead: Many people wake up startled after dreaming of a snake bite. Traditional dream readings have many views on snakes, but the versions contradict one another. In real life, this dream often shows up when you feel something has latched onto you and won't let go, such as a relationship or a troublesome matter.
being-bitten-by-snake.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ quite a lot on snakes. Some versions say snakes relate to difficult people or situations around you, and being bitten means being entangled. Others see the snake as a symbol of change drawing near, with the bite as something coming to your door. Still others link snakes to money or romantic entanglements. Because the versions differ, even contradict each other, they aren't a sound basis for judging anything. It's best taken as the old books' way of imagining stress.
being-bitten-by-snake.plain: If something is wearing on you in the daytime, such as a difficult coworker, a long-overdue account, or a feeling you can't let go of, you may be more likely to dream of snakes at night. The moment of the bite often matches the feeling of being suddenly stung in waking life: a remark, a message, a reminder that makes your chest tighten. Some people also have these dreams especially when they're under heavy stress or physically tired. This dream doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like tension from the day that wasn't worked through, played out in another form.

variants.q: Dreaming of a snake biting your hand
variants.a: Hands are often tied to doing and taking control. This may reflect feeling stuck on something lately, or being forced to take it over. It's common during busy stretches at work.

variants.q: Dreaming of a snake biting your foot
variants.a: Feet are tied to moving forward. This dream often appears when you feel progress is being held back, or something makes you afraid to go forward.

variants.q: Dreaming of many snakes
variants.a: A large number usually matches the feeling of everything arriving at once. It may relate to to-dos and messages from people piling up at the same time.

variants.q: Dreaming of being bitten by a snake but not hurt
variants.a: This is common after a false alarm, for example when something you worried about turned out less serious, and the dream plays out that tension.

being-bitten-by-snake.ask: If the snake in your dream reminded you of a specific person or a matter that has dragged on, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
being-bitten-by-snake.askQ: How will this matter that keeps entangling me develop from here?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a snake bite a bad omen?
faq.a: The traditional versions differ. Some speak gravely and some neutrally, and none rests on reliable grounds. In real life, it mostly has to do with stress and the feeling of being tied up by something.

faq.q: Could dreaming of snakes be related to health?
faq.a: Dreams don't foretell illness. If you really feel unwell, or if these dreams recur enough to affect your sleep, it's more practical to talk to a doctor directly.

tiger.name: tiger
tiger.title: What does it mean to dream about a tiger?
tiger.lead: Dreaming of a tiger can feel frightening. Traditional dream readings describe the tiger in different ways, such as authority or pressure, and the versions don't agree. In waking life, it tends to show up when you're facing a forceful person, or something you can't afford to take lightly.
tiger.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several different things. Some versions treat the tiger as a symbol of strength and status, so a tiger means a forceful person has come into your life. Others link the tiger to pressure and quarrels. Still others say a tiger in a dream is a reminder not to meet force with force. The versions differ, some leaning favorable and some leaning risky, and they contradict each other, so none of them is a sound basis for judging anything.
tiger.plain: If you have to deal with someone who has a strong presence, such as a boss, a client, or an elder, or with something much bigger than you, a tiger may show up at night. What you do in the dream, whether you hide, watch, or move closer, often matches your stance in waking life: wanting to avoid it, wanting to observe it, or trying to face it. Some people have this dream when their responsibilities grow heavier or people expect more of them. It doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like the feeling that this matter carries real weight, given the shape of a tiger.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tiger chasing me
variants.a: This often comes up when you feel pushed along by something or someone, perhaps tied to a deadline or to expectations, and the dream acts out that pressure.

variants.q: Dreaming of a gentle tiger
variants.a: This dream is common when you've changed your view of someone who used to feel distant, or when a hard task starts to seem less frightening than you thought.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tiger in a zoo
variants.a: Watching through the bars usually matches a state of knowing there's pressure but feeling you can hold up. It's common when the matter hasn't yet landed right in front of you.

variants.q: Dreaming of killing a tiger
variants.a: This mostly appears right after you've dealt with a tricky matter, or when you've already decided to face something. It's more like sorting through your feelings afterward.

tiger.ask: If the tiger in your dream made you think of a specific person or something that makes you tense, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
tiger.askQ: How will this thing that's putting me under so much pressure develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a tiger mean meeting a helpful person or a troublemaker?
faq.a: The traditional versions differ. Some speak of a helpful person, others of pressure, and there's no settled answer. In waking life, it more often reflects a forceful person or a heavy load you've been facing lately.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a tiger mean I should watch out for something?
faq.a: There's no need to think in terms of misfortune. You can notice whether something in your day has you especially tense. Once you deal with it, the dream often changes too.

lion.name: lion
lion.title: What does it mean to dream about a lion?
lion.lead: Dreaming of a lion is mostly about presence and standing. Traditional dream readings aren't consistent about lions. In waking life, it often appears when you face authority or are expected to perform, and it doesn't have to be an omen of anything.
lion.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say relatively little about lions, and what they say falls into two kinds. One treats the lion as a symbol of prestige and leadership, tied to status and reputation. The other connects it to quarrels and overpowering force. Some versions also say a lion in a dream is a reminder not to push too hard. Since the versions differ and don't agree, take them as a reference only.
lion.plain: If you're in a visible position in the day, such as giving a presentation, leading people, or facing evaluation, you may be more likely to dream of a lion at night. Whether the lion charges at you or stands far off often matches how you feel in waking life: singled out, or simply aware that a standard is there. Some people have this dream while deciding whether to go for a certain position. It doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like the feeling that this matter carries weight and attention, played out as a lion.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lion roaring at me
variants.a: This often comes up when you feel questioned or demanded of, possibly linked to being evaluated or compared lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a quiet lion
variants.a: This dream is common when your tension toward a weighty person or matter has slowly turned into observing, and you feel less rattled.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a lion
variants.a: This mostly matches the feeling that something can't be avoided, such as a decision you have to make, and the dream acts out that urgency.

variants.q: Dreaming of staring at a lion
variants.a: This is common when you're weighing whether to respond to something head-on. Stopping at the stare suggests you're still considering.

lion.ask: If the lion in your dream made you think of a specific person or a position you're pursuing, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
lion.askQ: What movement will there be in the matter I'm pursuing from here?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a lion good or bad?
faq.a: The traditional views split into two camps that don't agree, so there's no reliable conclusion. In waking life, it mostly reflects authority, evaluation, or pressure to perform that you've been dealing with lately.

faq.q: Could dreaming of a lion be related to my career?
faq.a: It may relate to work performance you care about, but it isn't a prediction. You can take it as a reminder to ask whether something lately has made you especially aware of how others see you.

horse.name: horse
horse.title: What does it mean to dream about a horse?
horse.lead: Dreaming of a horse is often tied to the feeling of running ahead or being carried along. Traditional dream readings treat the horse fairly neutrally, though there are many versions. In waking life, it tends to appear when you're rushing to keep up, or want to pick up the pace.
horse.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that horses relate to action, travel, and progress. Some versions read a horse as things being set in motion, others as busyness and fatigue. Some also see riding a horse as someone leading you along, and a horse that can't run as being stuck. The versions differ, some leaning positive and some toward hardship, so take them as the old imagination of life's rhythm.
horse.plain: If you're chasing a deadline, running around to many places, or anxious to push something forward, you may be more likely to dream of a horse at night. Whether the horse is fast or slow, and whether you're riding it or being dragged, often matches your sense of pace in waking life: feeling smooth, feeling tired, or feeling pulled along. Some people have this dream while considering whether to speed up a decision. It doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like the feeling of having been in motion lately, played out as a horse.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding a horse at a gallop
variants.a: It often shows up when things are moving along, or when you've finally made up your mind to push ahead. It's more like the dream acting out that drive.

variants.q: Dreaming of a horse that can't run
variants.a: Most often it matches the feeling of wanting to go fast but not being able to, such as being stuck waiting for a reply or for resources. The dream acts out that urgency.

variants.q: Dreaming of being dragged by a horse
variants.a: Common when you feel pushed along by events with little choice of your own. It may have to do with an overly full schedule.

variants.q: Dreaming of a white horse
variants.a: Circulating versions disagree about white horses. Some link them to things going smoothly, others to change. In waking life, you can ask whether you feel hopeful or nervous about change right now.

horse.ask: If the horse in your dream reminds you of something you're rushing to finish, or something that just won't move forward, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
horse.askQ: Will the matter I've been pushing along make progress in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a horse mean good news is coming?
faq.a: The traditional sayings differ. Some speak of progress, others of running around, and there's no settled answer. In waking life, it more often reflects your recent pace and how busy you've been.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a horse running away?
faq.a: It may relate to a worry about an opportunity slipping away, or it may simply be a leftover from rushing during the day. You might notice whether something lately makes you afraid of running out of time.

cow.name: ox
cow.title: What does it mean to dream about an ox? What does an ox stand for in dreams?
cow.lead: Dreaming of an ox is mostly tied to themes like hard work, responsibility, and harvest. It often appears when you're carrying a heavy load or waiting for a result. It's a dream that sits close to everyday life.
cow.trad: In the common sayings of folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), the ox is mostly seen as a symbol of wealth and a farming harvest. An ox walking into the house, or a strong ox, is often said to relate to household finances and building things up. An ox working in the field is linked to "you reap what you sow." Some versions read the ox as a stubborn, uncomplaining temperament. The versions differ: some stress wealth, others character, and there's no single version.
cow.plain: During the day, you may well be in a state of having lots to do and having to carry it all yourself, such as work deadlines, family matters, or a long-term task that isn't finished. An ox feels slow, steady, and strong, so this dream often comes when you're enduring something or holding on. You may also be thinking a lot about whether your effort will be repaid, and the ox seems to remind you that you've already done plenty. Or someone near you who works quietly and says little may have left an impression. These are all projections of mood and don't mean anything will happen next.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ox chasing me
variants.a: Common when something has been weighing on you during the day and you want to avoid it. Being chased reflects pressure, not that anyone truly means you harm.

variants.q: Dreaming of many oxen
variants.a: It may relate to a feeling of one thing after another. Or you may simply have seen many images of farming, ranches, or food lately that stayed in your mind.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ox walking into the house
variants.a: Traditional sayings often link this to household finances and added wealth. In waking life, it's mostly that you've been weighing income, spending, or home arrangements lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead ox
variants.a: Traditionally it's said to be a symbol related to harvest and labor, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. It mostly reflects a worry that something you've invested in for a long time will go to waste.

variants.q: Dreaming of being hit by an ox
variants.a: Common after you've come up against a forceful person or a rule head-on. The dream simply acts out that feeling of being rammed.

cow.ask: If the ox in your dream reminds you of a certain person, or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
cow.askQ: Will the matter in front of me make progress in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of an ox mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Traditional dream books often link the ox with wealth, but that's only a handed-down saying. In real life, it's more a reflection of how much you've been thinking about income and effort. It's not a guarantee.

faq.q: I keep dreaming of oxen. Is there a hidden message?
faq.a: When the same theme keeps returning, it usually means that matter hasn't settled in your mind. If the dreams are frequent enough to disturb your sleep, you can talk with a doctor.

pig.name: pig
pig.title: What does it mean to dream about a pig? What does a pig stand for in dreams?
pig.lead: The common readings of dreaming of a pig relate to abundance, enjoyment, and building up. It may also reflect how much you've been thinking about money, food, or relaxing. It's a very down-to-earth dream.
pig.trad: In the common sayings of folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), the pig mostly symbolizes goods and food. A fat pig, or a pig coming through the door, is often said to relate to savings and the household's fortunes. Raising pigs is linked to slowly growing something over time. Some versions read the pig as a reminder about traits like laziness or greed. The versions differ quite a bit: some stress wealth, others a reminder to practice restraint, and there's no settled answer.
pig.plain: During the day, you may be thinking things like "Is there enough money?" or "Should I treat myself better?", perhaps right after payday, after a big purchase, or while you're cutting back on spending. In dreams the pig is often tied to eating, comfort, and stockpiling, so this dream is common when you've been more tired lately and want to relax, or the reverse, when you're holding yourself back. Someone near you who's more easygoing may also have left an impression. Whether the pig is fat or thin, clean or dirty usually reflects your pull between wanting satisfaction and practicing restraint, not a forecast of anything.

variants.q: Dreaming of a fat pig
variants.a: Traditional sayings often link this to abundance and building things up. In real life, it's mostly that you've been more aware of your income or living conditions lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a pig running away
variants.a: Common when you worry that some money or opportunity won't last. It reflects concern, not that you'll actually lose anything.

variants.q: Dreaming of raising pigs
variants.a: It may point to something you're slowly building, like saving money, growing a habit, or leading a project that needs time to develop.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dirty pig
variants.a: It often shows up after a place or a relationship has left you feeling "not quite comfortable." The dream projects that feeling.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a pig
variants.a: It usually has to do with something you've been trying to avoid during the day. The dream acts out the feeling of being pushed to deal with it.

pig.ask: If the pig in your dream reminds you of some money, or a decision that's been left sitting, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
pig.askQ: How should I best arrange my money right now?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a pig mean good fortune with money?
faq.a: Traditional dream books often link pigs with wealth and possessions, but that is a handed-down saying. In waking life, it's more likely to reflect how much you've been thinking about money and enjoyment lately.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a big, fat pig?
faq.a: A common reading is that it symbolizes "accumulation." You may be waiting for something to slowly bear fruit, or weighing a larger expense.

chicken.name: Chicken
chicken.title: What does it mean to dream about a chicken? What does a chicken represent in a dream?
chicken.lead: Dreaming of a chicken is often tied to daily routine, reminders, and small matters. A rooster crowing, a flock, a rooster or a hen: the details differ, and so does the mood they bring.
chicken.trad: In the folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), the chicken usually stands for home, daily life, and being alert. A crowing rooster is often said to mean "time to get moving, time to pay attention." A hen with her chicks is linked to family and caregiving. Some editions read the chicken as a warning about quarrels or gossip. The editions differ: some lean toward family, others toward friction between people, and there is no single account.
chicken.plain: During the day you may well be living at a pace where time is chasing you, such as getting up early, rushing to clock in, or racing a deadline, and the sound of a rooster slips easily into a dream. Chickens are also linked with small matters, household chores, and neighbors, so this dream is common when you're handling a lot of odds and ends, or have some small friction with people around you. Another possibility is that you're reminding yourself to pull yourself together, and the rooster in the dream is that alarm clock. All of this reflects the pace of your life right now. It doesn't predict what will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of a rooster crowing
variants.a: Common when time or deadlines have been pushing you along lately. Traditional sayings tie it to being alert; in waking life it's mostly a projection of your routine and stress.

variants.q: Dreaming of a hen with her chicks
variants.a: Often comes after looking after family, training a newcomer, or handling many chores. It reflects the feelings of a caregiver.

variants.q: Dreaming of a chicken flying
variants.a: It may point to wanting to break out of some fixed arrangement lately, or to noticing a small, unexpected thing.

variants.q: Dreaming of killing a chicken
variants.a: Traditional sayings often link it to handling household matters. In waking life, it's mostly that you're getting ready to finish some small matter that has dragged on.

variants.q: Dreaming of many chickens
variants.a: Common when many scattered messages and to-dos surround you at once. The dream acts out that "noisiness."

chicken.ask: If the chickens in your dream remind you of a person, or of some small matter you've never dealt with, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
chicken.askQ: How will my small friction with that person develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a chicken crowing mean something is going to happen?
faq.a: Traditional dream books often link a chicken's crowing with being alert, but that is a handed-down saying. In waking life, it's more likely to reflect your routine and time pressure lately.

faq.q: Is dreaming of a chicken connected to quarrels with people?
faq.a: Some editions read it that way, but there's no settled answer. A reading closer to real life is that you may have had a small friction with someone during the day, and the dream held on to it.

duck.name: Duck
duck.title: What does it mean to dream about a duck? What does a duck represent in a dream?
duck.lead: Dreaming of a duck is often tied to going with the flow, relationships, and everyday calm. The picture of a duck drifting on water mostly reflects wanting to take it easier lately, or adjusting to a new environment.
duck.trad: In the folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), the duck usually stands for harmony, partners, and activity on the water.
