faq.a: Folk sayings often link croaking to gossip, but in waking life it's usually just that you've been more sensitive lately to what others say, or that your surroundings are noisy. Rather than worry, it may help to look at what is making you uneasy.

turtle.name: Turtle
turtle.title: What does it mean to dream about a turtle?
turtle.lead: Dreaming of a turtle is mostly tied to feelings like slowing down, protecting yourself, and lasting for the long haul. Traditionally it's often associated with long life and steadiness, but that doesn't hint at good or bad luck, and a single dream won't change anything in real life.
turtle.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that turtles relate to long life, stability, and the household. Some versions distinguish between them: a turtle coming into your arms symbolizes a child being added to the family, and a turtle entering water symbolizes money flowing. Another line of thought holds that since turtles move slowly, dreaming of one means things will drag on and you need to wait patiently. The versions differ quite a bit, even contradicting each other, so treat this as a cultural association, not a forecast.
turtle.plain: During the day, you may be the kind of person who wants everything faster: quick progress, quick replies, quick decisions. When a turtle appears in a dream, it's common that part of you wants to slow down, or that you've been holding on, enduring, or waiting for the right moment lately. You may also be very focused on protecting yourself, not wanting to be seen through or pushed along, and a shell fits that feeling. Another common case is that you have a long-term matter moving slower than expected, and you care about it but can't rush it. This kind of dream is more a reflection of your sense of pace than a prediction of what will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of a turtle crawling into your home
variants.a: Home is often a place of security. This dream may reflect that you want to bring more stability back into your life lately, or that something at home is on your mind and you're looking for a way to settle it.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of turtles
variants.a: A large number often goes with a feeling of accumulation. You may be looking after many small things at once, or care about something that has to build up slowly and can't be hurried.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead turtle
variants.a: Traditionally some people read this in a negative direction, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. More commonly, you're worried that something stable may loosen, or you have feelings about an ending.

variants.q: Dreaming of catching or keeping a turtle
variants.a: It may reflect a wish to hold on to some kind of steadiness, or that you're caring for something that needs long-term commitment and want to be sure you can manage it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a turtle biting you
variants.a: Being bitten often has to do with boundaries. You may feel that someone or something is getting too close and making you uncomfortable, and part of you is reminding yourself to keep some space.

turtle.ask: If you dreamed of a particular person, or there's something on your mind you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring movement.
turtle.askQ: Will there be movement on the matter I can't let go of?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a turtle mean I'll live a long life?
faq.a: Traditionally the turtle is often associated with long life, but that's a cultural symbol, not a prediction for anyone. Dreams more often reflect your mood in the moment, such as wanting to slow down or wanting stability.

faq.q: I keep dreaming of turtles. Should I be concerned?
faq.a: If it only happens now and then, there's usually no need to worry. If you've been sleeping poorly or dreaming repeatedly lately, talking with a doctor about your sleep would be more practical than looking up dream meanings.

crab.name: Crab
crab.title: What does it mean to dream about a crab?
crab.lead: Dreaming of a crab is often tied to feelings like being stuck, wanting to protect yourself, or leaving things unsaid. Traditionally the crab has the image of walking sideways, with a shell and pincers, but that's only an association and doesn't mean real life will go in any particular direction.
crab.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on crabs. One line says crabs mostly relate to quarrels, disputes, and petty people drawing near, because they have pincers and pinch. Another says that a crab with its shell, walking sideways, symbolizes guarding your own territory, or not going about things in a straight line. Some versions also link crab dreams to money and to matters near the water. The versions differ widely, even in opposite ways, so take it as a cultural saying and nothing more.
crab.plain: During the day, you may be in a state of not wanting to clash head-on: holding back words you want to say, being stuck on something you want to move forward, or feeling that someone's words have thorns so you have to guard yourself first. A crab's shell and pincers often match this feeling of defensiveness. It may also be that you feel hemmed in somewhere lately, with many rules and blocked paths, so you have to work around things. Another common case is that something hasn't been laid out and talked about yet, and on the surface all is fine, but you keep thinking about it. This kind of dream is more a reflection of your recent stance: guard first, then find a way.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crab pinching you
variants.a: Being pinched often goes with the feeling of being stung. A remark or an event may have left you uneasy lately, and while you're still deciding whether to respond, you've already put your guard up.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of crabs
variants.a: A large number may reflect feeling that you have to deal with many small troubles at once, or a setting where it was crowded and noisy and you didn't want to stay long.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating crab
variants.a: Eating often relates to digesting and processing. You may be slowly taking apart something that has been stuck, or trying to swallow an emotion and not say much about it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crab walking sideways
variants.a: It may match a time when you have to take a detour and can't go straight at things. It could also be that someone seems to break the usual rules, and you feel you need to pay closer attention.

variants.q: Dreaming of catching a crab
variants.a: It may reflect wanting to grab hold of a difficult matter and keep it under control, or trying to pull a stuck situation back into your own hands.

crab.ask: If you dreamed of a specific person, or something has been weighing on you and you can't let it go, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which coming days may bring movement.
crab.askQ: Will the standoff between that person and me change in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a crab mean someone wants to harm me?
faq.a: Traditionally, some people read it as gossip or petty people, but that is symbolic, not a warning of what will happen. More often, you felt guarded about certain interactions during the day, and the dream simply magnified it.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a crab have to do with money luck?
faq.a: Some circulating versions link crabs with water and wealth, but accounts differ and have no real basis. Rather than looking for a money sign, consider whether you've been worrying about money or resources lately.

shrimp.name: shrimp
shrimp.title: What does it mean to dream about shrimp?
shrimp.lead: Dreaming of shrimp often goes with feelings like "so many small things, wanting to be noticed, a body that's a bit tired." Traditionally, shrimp give an impression of being small, nimble, living in groups and having shells, but this is only a cultural association and doesn't foretell anything in real life.
shrimp.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about shrimp. One line says many shrimp relate to small gains, small bustle and social contact. Another says the shrimp's curved body and shell symbolize a humble posture and the need to endure for a while. Some versions link dreaming of shrimp with gossip and trivial matters. The versions differ clearly, and some even contradict each other, so treat them as circulating sayings for reference only.
shrimp.plain: During the day you may be chased by many small things: lots of messages, lots of chores, a pile of things to answer or handle. None is big, but together they wear you out. Shrimp often appear in groups, and seeing them in a dream commonly matches this feeling of "a pile of small things." It could also be that you care a lot about being seen lately: you've done plenty, but nobody seems to notice, and that weighs on you. Another common reading is that your body is telling you it's tired, especially the kind of tiredness where you've been busy all day and your mind still can't stop. This kind of dream is more a reflection of your recent load than a prediction.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of shrimp
variants.a: It may reflect feeling that the things on your plate are both many and fragmented, and you don't know which to handle first. It could also be that you've had a heavy volume of social messages lately and feel a bit overwhelmed.

variants.q: Dreaming of catching or scooping up shrimp
variants.a: It may match wanting to gather up scattered small matters one by one, or trying to seize a less obvious opportunity while checking that you haven't missed anything.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating shrimp
variants.a: Eating often relates to digestion. You may be dealing with some scattered feelings or small relationship matters and want to digest them slowly instead of leaving them sitting.

variants.q: Dreaming of dead shrimp
variants.a: Traditionally, some people think of it in a negative way, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. More commonly, you worry that some small matter will fizzle out, or you feel a little let down about a certain connection.

variants.q: Dreaming of shrimp jumping or darting around
variants.a: It may reflect some restlessness: lots of changes, a messy rhythm, and trouble settling down, so you're looking for a way to bring your pace back.

shrimp.ask: If you dreamed of a specific person, or something has been weighing on you and you can't let it go, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which coming days may bring movement.
shrimp.askQ: Will the matter I've been busy with lately make progress?

faq.q: Does dreaming of shrimp mean I'll come into a little money?
faq.a: Some circulating versions link shrimp with small gains, but accounts differ and it isn't a prediction. What's more worth looking at is whether you've been worrying about money or small things lately.

faq.q: Does dreaming of shrimp have to do with love?
faq.a: There's no fixed saying. More commonly, the dream reflects that you've had a lot of social contact and messages lately, or that you care about whether the other person notices you.

dragon.name: dragon
dragon.title: What does it mean to dream about a dragon? What does a dragon in a dream stand for?
dragon.lead: Dreaming of a dragon often goes with "wanting to grow stronger, wanting recognition, a surge of spirit inside." The dragon carries great weight in the culture, so when it appears in a dream, it mostly mirrors your recent expectations of yourself, or a stage where you want to break through.
dragon.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly treat the dragon as a symbol of grandeur, nobility and transformation. A dragon flying in the sky is read as high ambition and room to grow, and a dragon entering water as a turn for the better. Some versions link the dragon with power and elders, and say being chased by a dragon means facing pressure. Other circulating versions say a wounded or falling dragon means a loss of momentum. These sayings differ a lot, and the same dream is often given several meanings.
dragon.plain: During the day you may be in a state of "wanting to be seen, but afraid you can't hold up": there's a chance to shine at work, but pressure comes with it, or you hold great hopes for something and feel both excited and tense. A dragon in a dream is often associated with power and change. It may reflect that you badly want to break out of the present situation and prove yourself, or that your feelings are being pulled by someone or something weighty. It could also be that you have pent-up energy with nowhere to go, and in the dream it becomes a dragon. This kind of dream is more a staging of your daytime ambition and pressure, and doesn't mean anything will happen next.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dragon flying in the sky
variants.a: Dreams of flying often connect with wanting to rise higher and be free. They may reflect hope for the future lately, or a wish to shake off some kind of limit.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a dragon
variants.a: Being chased in a dream often relates to stress. You may be dealing with a person or matter of real weight lately and feel pushed to respond.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dragon entering water or in a river
variants.a: Water is often linked with emotions and surroundings. This dream may reflect a wish to find your footing again in more familiar territory, or a sense that things have taken a new direction.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dragon hurt or falling
variants.a: Some traditional versions lean toward setbacks, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life. More likely you're worried that an expectation will fall through, or that you won't be able to hold up.

variants.q: Dreaming of many dragons
variants.a: Large numbers often suggest facing many expectations and pressures at once. You may also be getting a lot of attention lately and feel a bit overwhelmed.

dragon.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
dragon.askQ: Will the thing I've been trying to break through on lately start to move in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a dragon mean I'll prosper?
faq.a: Folk sayings often link dragons with nobility and advancement, but a dream is not a forecast. A more useful way to see it: it reflects the expectations you hold for yourself lately, and it's a reminder to watch your stress.

faq.q: What's the difference between dreaming of a dragon and dreaming of a snake?
faq.a: Folk sayings often treat them separately: the dragon leans toward grandeur and transformation, the snake toward intuition and shedding an old skin. Still, what a dream means depends on your mood and situation at the time.

phoenix.name: Phoenix
phoenix.title: What does it mean to dream about a phoenix?
phoenix.lead: Dreaming of a phoenix often relates to feelings like wanting a fresh start, wanting to be seen, or having hopes for yourself. Traditionally the phoenix symbolizes rebirth and beauty, but that is only a cultural association. It doesn't mean real life will follow the dream.
phoenix.trad: Folk dream books, such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams, don't agree on the phoenix. One line says it symbolizes happy events, dignity, and being valued by others. Another links the phoenix with fire and rebirth, meaning an old chapter ending and a new one beginning. Some versions note that the phoenix is rarely seen, and suggest checking whether you've set your expectations too high. The versions differ quite a bit, so take them as circulating cultural sayings.
phoenix.plain: In waking life, you may be at a point where you want to change how things look: leave an old state behind, redo something properly, or feel more energized. In the culture, the phoenix is often tied to rebirth and standing out, and in a dream it commonly matches this wish to renew yourself. You may also care a lot about how others see you, wanting approval and recognition while worrying you're not good enough. Another common case is that you've just come out of an uncomfortable stretch and feel that you can finally start over. This kind of dream reflects your recent hopes and sense of transition. It is not a prediction.

variants.q: Dreaming of a phoenix flying away
variants.a: It may reflect worry that an opportunity or a certain state won't last, or that something you want to hold on to is slipping away, leaving you a bit reluctant to let go.

variants.q: Dreaming of a phoenix in fire
variants.a: Fire is often linked with change. You may be going through an ending and a beginning, knowing you need to move forward while still feeling attached to the old.

variants.q: Dreaming of a phoenix perched in a tree
variants.a: It may match a recent wish to settle somewhere and steady yourself, or that you're waiting for the right moment and aren't in a hurry to move.

variants.q: Dreaming of many phoenixes
variants.a: Large numbers may reflect many hopes for the future, or wanting to do several things at once. You feel fired up, but aren't sure where to begin.

variants.q: Dreaming of a phoenix calling to you
variants.a: It may match a recent preoccupation with a certain voice or remark, or a thought in your mind that keeps nudging you, wanting to be noticed.

phoenix.ask: If you dreamed of a particular person, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
phoenix.askQ: Will the fresh start I want to make begin to move in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a phoenix mean a happy event is coming?
faq.a: Traditionally some people think in that direction, but it's symbolic talk, not a forecast. More commonly, you have hopes for something lately, or you want to feel renewed.

faq.q: Is dreaming of a phoenix related to love?
faq.a: There's no fixed saying. It's more worth asking whether you've been caring a lot about being seen and affirmed by someone, or wanting a fresh start in a relationship.

crocodile.name: Crocodile
crocodile.title: What does it mean to dream about a crocodile? A dream interpretation
crocodile.lead: Dreaming of a crocodile is usually not a mysterious warning. It's more that you've been especially aware of some hidden pressure lately. In dreams, a crocodile often stands for a quiet but threatening situation, or someone whose thoughts you can't read. No need to worry. Let's look at what tradition says and what feelings it may match in real life.
crocodile.trad: Folk dream books, such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams, commonly say this about crocodiles: some versions read it as gossip or quarrels with others, since a crocodile bites and won't let go. Others link it to trouble lurking in the dark, a reminder to be careful in what you do. Another line holds that the crocodile belongs to water, so dreaming of it relates to money and deals, and may hint at tug-of-war over finances. The versions differ quite a bit, some stressing relationships, others money, with no single conclusion, so take it as one cultural reference.
crocodile.plain: A crocodile in a dream usually gives the feeling of quietly waiting, then suddenly lunging. This dream often shows up when, in the day, you're in a relationship or situation where you can't quite relax: perhaps a difficult person at work, or something left hanging and unresolved. You don't say it aloud, but inside you're on guard. The crocodile may also match a part of yourself, the wish to lie low, wait for the right time, and avoid head-on conflict. If you were very afraid in the dream, it may reflect uncertainty about how you see someone lately. If you watched it calmly, you may already be working out how to respond. A dream is not a prophecy. It's more like your unspoken wariness from the day, acted out by a crocodile.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crocodile biting me
variants.a: Dreams of being bitten often come when you feel something has already wrapped itself around you, perhaps a responsibility, a social obligation, or a relationship that's hard to handle. The crocodile holding on reflects feeling unable to shake it off, not that you'll really be hurt.

variants.q: Being chased by a crocodile
variants.a: Being chased often matches a feeling of avoidance in daily life: there's something you keep putting off facing, and the longer you wait, the more pressure builds. Whether you can run in the dream often has to do with how confident you feel about handling it.

variants.q: Lots of crocodiles
variants.a: A group of crocodiles may match the frazzled feeling of things coming at you from every direction, or a sense that several people around you need watching at once. A large number usually reflects more than one source of stress.

variants.q: A crocodile in the water
variants.a: A crocodile in the water is hard to see, which often matches unease about a situation where you don't have enough information and can't tell what's underneath. It may also mean you sense that something looks calm on the surface but is stirring below.

variants.q: A dead crocodile
variants.a: Traditionally, some read this as trouble fading away. In waking life, it's more often that you've started to feel a worry is nearly over, or that your fear of it has eased.

crocodile.ask: If the crocodile in your dream brings to mind a specific person or something that's stuck, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
crocodile.askQ: When will the standoff between me and that person start to loosen?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a crocodile a bad omen?
faq.a: Traditional dream books do link it with quarrels and trouble, but those are handed-down cultural sayings, not predictions. In waking life, crocodile dreams more often show up when you're especially on guard about a relationship or situation. What matters is what you're going through lately, not the dream itself.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of crocodiles?
faq.a: Start by asking whether something lately has you seeming fine on the outside but staying guarded inside. Write down that person or situation, and you'll often find the dream fits it. If these dreams keep coming back and cost you sleep, it's fine to talk with a doctor. There's no need to scare yourself.

shark.name: Shark
shark.title: What does it mean to dream about a shark? Shark dream meaning
shark.lead: Dreaming of a shark is often tied to a feeling that there's risk around you but you can't quite see it. In a dream, a shark most often stands for a forceful competitor, or for your wariness toward some environment. It isn't a warning of disaster. It's the tension you've built up during the day showing up in a different form at night.
shark.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say little about sharks, since sharks weren't common animals in the Chinese heartland. Most of what's said was added later by coastal regions or modern dream guides. Two readings are common. One treats the shark as a strong rival or capable opponent, so dreaming of one hints at a formidable person nearby. The other links it to the dangers of open water, a reminder to be careful around the water or when traveling far. Some versions also say a shark stands for a sudden shock. The versions don't agree, so take them as reference only.
shark.plain: A shark gives the impression of something fast, fierce, and appearing from the dark. So this dream often comes when you're in a competitive or comparing environment: maybe a very strong rival at work, or a worry that you're not performing well enough and will be outdone. It may also be that you've recently entered an unfamiliar setting where the rules aren't clear and you need to tread carefully. If the shark is far away in the dream, it usually matches knowing there's pressure but still coping. If it's close, or even attacks, it may reflect a feeling that a threat has closed in. For some people, a shark dream is really an awareness of their own drive or aggression: part of you badly wants to win. A dream isn't a prediction. It's more like your daytime sense of competition and alertness taking the shape of a shark.

variants.q: A shark biting me
variants.a: A dream of being bitten by a shark often matches a feeling that some competition or conflict has already hurt you. It might be criticism, a lost opportunity, or friction in a relationship. It reflects a feeling, not that you'll really be hurt.

variants.q: Being chased by a shark
variants.a: Being chased usually has to do with avoidance: there's a challenge or conversation you keep wanting to dodge. How fast you swim in the dream and whether you have anywhere to hide often reflect how much room you feel you have.

variants.q: Lots of sharks
variants.a: A group of sharks may match a feeling that pressure comes from many sides, such as being chased by several people or tasks at once. It may also be a general distrust of some environment.

variants.q: A shark swimming nearby
variants.a: A shark nearby that doesn't attack often appears when you know there's risk but things are still safe for now, like an observation period in a new environment while you work out who's a rival and who's a companion.

variants.q: A dead or stranded shark
variants.a: This kind of dream is common when a source of pressure has finally eased, or when you care less about a rival. Traditionally some read it as a threat being removed, but in waking life it's mostly a change in mood.

shark.ask: If the shark in your dream brings to mind a specific rival or a particular competition, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
shark.askQ: Do I still have a chance in this?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a shark mean someone around me is working against me?
faq.a: Some circulating versions link sharks with a strong enemy, but that's symbolic language, not a prediction naming anyone. In waking life, this dream more often reflects your wariness toward an environment or a person. What's worth noticing is how you feel, not guessing who the bad guy is.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a shark mean I should be careful around water?
faq.a: Traditional sayings do include warnings about the dangers of water, but that's an older generation's cultural association. There's no need to change your plans because of it. If the dream unsettles you, you might instead ask whether something lately makes you feel you can't touch bottom.

whale.name: Whale
whale.title: What does it mean to dream about a whale? Whale dream meaning
whale.lead: Dreaming of a whale is usually tied to things that are huge, slow, and hard to get a hold of. It may be a big thought in your mind, a deep emotion, or something that makes you feel small. Whale dreams mostly carry no sense of threat, and often come when you're thinking about the direction of your life.
whale.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) are mixed on whales, because traditional texts often lump them in with big fish. Two readings are common. One reads a big fish as wealth or a harvest, so dreaming of one is seen as a sign of income. The other links it to long journeys or travel over water. Some say a big fish stands for a helpful person or someone of standing. Since versions often blur whales, carp, and big fish together, they don't agree, so treat it as cultural color.
whale.plain: A whale in a dream is usually a gentle giant, and it tends to appear when you're facing something much bigger than you: perhaps career planning, family responsibility, a deep relationship, or a problem you can't deal with yet. The image of it slowly gliding past often matches the feeling that this is huge and all you can do is watch it unfold. Some people dream of a whale because lately they've especially wanted quiet, to sink into their own world away from the noise. If you're close to the whale in the dream, or even swimming with it, it may reflect that you're accepting some of your deeper feelings. A dream isn't a prediction. It's more like turning something big and heavy inside you into a moving mountain.

variants.q: A whale leaping out of the sea
variants.a: A whale breaching often gives a feeling of finally coming up for air. It may match something that's been weighing on you finding an outlet, or a wish to breathe and be seen.

variants.q: A whale coming near me
variants.a: A whale that comes close without hurting you often shows up when you're facing an important decision or a deep emotion. Its closeness reflects how much that matter now weighs on you.

variants.q: Dreaming of many whales
variants.a: A pod of whales may match the feeling of several big things pressing on you at once. It may also be your overall sense of a group or an environment, where you feel relatively small.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stranded whale
variants.a: The image of a stranding often comes with a feeling of powerlessness: you see something stuck and can't help. It can also mean you feel a part of yourself is stuck somewhere and can't move.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding a whale
variants.a: This kind of dream is common when you feel you've caught a big trend or attached yourself to an important person. It also appears when you're trying to steer something larger than you are, with some excitement and some unease.

whale.ask: If the whale in your dream reminds you of something very big and heavy, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
whale.askQ: How will the big matter on my mind unfold from here?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a whale a good thing?
faq.a: Traditionally, some people link big fish with gains and helpful people, but that is only a passed-down saying, not a promise. In real life, whale dreams more often come when you're thinking about the big direction of your life or facing a large responsibility. What matters is what the "big thing" in your mind is.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a whale mean a helpful person is coming?
faq.a: Some dream-interpretation books make that connection, but instead of waiting for someone, look at how the whale felt in the dream: reassuring or oppressive? That usually matches how you truly feel about someone "weighty" around you.

dolphin.name: Dolphin
dolphin.title: What does it mean to dream about a dolphin? Dolphin dream meaning
dolphin.lead: Dreaming of a dolphin mostly relates to feeling relaxed, friendly, and wanting company. In dreams, a dolphin often stands for pleasant interactions with others, or the part of you that wants to play and get closer to people. This dream usually comes when you long to unwind, or when your relationships have been going smoothly lately.
dolphin.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say very little about dolphins. Dolphins are not a common animal in traditional dream texts, and most of what is said was added by more recent publications. The usual reading is positive: a dolphin is taken to mean a "friend," "good news," or a "happy meeting," and some link it to "a smooth trip on the water." Another view says a dolphin stands for "agility" and "smooth communication." Because the sources are late and the versions differ, treat these as cultural reference only, not something to take literally.
dolphin.plain: Dolphins come across as smart, playful, and quick to approach people, so this dream often appears when you've had a lot of social contact lately, or really want someone to talk to. You may also be in a situation that calls for cooperation and communication, and the dolphin reflects your wish for things to go more easily. If you swim with the dolphin in the dream, it often matches a relationship that feels comfortable, or finally letting yourself relax. On the other hand, if the dolphin is far away and you can't catch it, you may feel that some kind of happiness or a friendship is a bit out of reach. A dream is not a prophecy. It's more like turning your wish to be close to people and have some fun into a leaping dolphin.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dolphin jumping
variants.a: A dolphin leaping out of the water often goes with a lifted mood and a wish to share. It may match something happy that happened lately, or a pleasant occasion you're looking forward to.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming with a dolphin
variants.a: Swimming together often appears when a relationship feels in tune, or when you're enjoying some kind of teamwork. It reflects a sense of ease, not any special sign.

variants.q: Dreaming of many dolphins
variants.a: A group of dolphins may match a lively circle of people around you, or a time when you're dealing with many people at once and feel a little overwhelmed. It may also be a longing for that kind of group warmth.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dolphin coming close to me
variants.a: A dolphin approaching on its own often reflects a strong wish lately for someone to reach out and care about you, or your sense that someone is showing you goodwill.

variants.q: Dreaming of an injured or stranded dolphin
variants.a: This kind of dream often comes with worry about a relationship or a friend. It may also mean you feel something has interrupted your sense of lightness and enjoyment.

dolphin.ask: If the dolphin in your dream makes you think of a certain person or relationship, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
dolphin.askQ: How will things between that person and me go from here?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a dolphin a good thing?
faq.a: The passed-down sayings are mostly positive, linking dolphins with friendship and good news, but that is symbolic, cultural talk. In real life, this dream more often reflects a recent wish to relax and be close to people. What's worth being glad about is how you're doing, not the dream itself.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a dolphin mean romance is coming?
faq.a: Some more recent publications make that connection, but there is no agreed reading. Rather than asking about romance, look at the distance between you and the dolphin in the dream. Closeness usually matches what you hope for in a relationship, which is closer to real life.

centipede.name: Centipede
centipede.title: What does it mean to dream about a centipede? Centipede dream meaning
centipede.lead: Dreaming of a centipede often relates to the feeling of many small things tangled together and wearing on you. With its many legs and quick movement, a centipede in a dream often stands for petty troubles that won't go away, or your distaste for something. It doesn't predict anything. It's the irritation you built up during the day, showing up in another form.
centipede.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ on centipedes. There are two common kinds of reading. One takes the centipede, or "hundred-legged bug," to mean "gossip and quarrels" or a "petty person," because its many legs give a sense of entanglement. The other links it to "many trivial matters and a troubled mind." Some versions say a centipede dream is a reminder to pay attention to your home environment or hygiene. The versions differ quite a bit, some focusing on relationships and some on everyday trifles, with no single conclusion, so treat them as cultural reference only.
centipede.plain: A centipede in a dream is usually unpleasant, and it often appears when you've been caught up in many small things: a pile of to-dos, messages you can't finish answering, small troubles at home or work that never end. It may also be an unspoken distaste for someone, a sense that they "wriggle in" or "cling on." If the centipede crawls onto you in the dream, it often matches a feeling that some annoying matter is already affecting you. If you only see it on a wall, you may know there's a problem but haven't decided to deal with it yet. Some people who dream of a centipede are actually bothered by a thought of their own that they want to shake off but can't. A dream is not a prophecy. It's more like gathering the scattered irritations of your day into one many-legged creature.

variants.q: Dreaming of a centipede crawling on you
variants.a: A dream of something crawling on you often matches a feeling that an annoying matter has "already stuck to you." It could be someone who keeps coming to you, or a problem dragging on unsolved. It reflects irritation.

variants.q: Dreaming of many centipedes
variants.a: A swarm of centipedes may match a time of far too many small things, with to-do lists, chores, and social odds and ends all flooding in at once. The large number usually reflects a feeling that your energy is being scattered.

variants.q: Dreaming of killing a centipede
variants.a: Dreams of killing something often come after you've finally dealt with an annoying matter, or when you've already decided to face it. Some traditional readings take it as "getting rid of trouble," but in waking life it's usually a shift in mood.

variants.q: Dreaming of a centipede biting me
variants.a: Dreams of being bitten often have to do with feeling stung by something small, maybe a remark or an attitude that left you uneasy. It reflects that you care, not that you will really be hurt.

variants.q: Dreaming of a centipede crawling on a wall or the floor
variants.a: Watching it crawl without it coming near often matches knowing a problem exists but still being a little removed from it, and watching to decide whether to deal with it.

centipede.ask: If the centipede in your dream reminds you of something that has been bothering you for a while, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
centipede.askQ: When will this thing that keeps bothering me be settled?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a centipede unlucky?
faq.a: Traditional dream books do link it with quarrels and petty people, but that is a cultural association handed down, not a prophecy. In waking life, centipede dreams more often show up when you're tied up in small matters and feeling irritable. What matters is your own state.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a centipede mean someone around me wants to harm me?
faq.a: Some versions read it as "petty people," but that is symbolic and doesn't point to anyone by name. Instead of guessing who, think about whether a person or a matter lately feels clingy and irritating. That is usually where the dream comes from.

scorpion.name: scorpion
scorpion.title: What does it mean to dream about a scorpion? Common beliefs and psychological readings
scorpion.lead: Most people wake up a little uneasy after dreaming of a scorpion. Traditional dream readings vary: some link it to guardedness and petty people, others see heightened alertness. In waking life, it more often reflects being especially on guard about something or someone lately.
scorpion.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say scorpions are tied to "defensiveness and hidden trouble," so dreaming of one may be read as a relationship around you that needs attention. Other versions see the scorpion as "dormant power," meaning you sense some pressure approaching. Another line of reading holds that being stung in the dream matches the situation of "being suddenly pricked," such as being hurt by words or an attitude. The versions differ quite a bit. Some lean toward relationships, others toward your own feelings, and there is no single standard version.
scorpion.plain: This dream often appears when, during the day, you've been in a state of "watching out." Maybe a coworker's, friend's, or family member's words left you uneasy, maybe you're waiting for a result and afraid of a mistake, or maybe you've started to feel unsure about a relationship. A scorpion feels "small, quiet, but able to sting," so when it appears in a dream, it often matches that sense of not knowing when you might get jabbed. Some people have simply seen related videos or pictures lately, or it's hot or they're sleeping badly, and the dream picks it up. You might ask yourself: is there something you say is fine while a thorn stays in your heart? That thorn is usually worth more attention than the scorpion itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of a scorpion biting or stinging me
variants.a: Often matches a feeling of being "stung" during the day, such as being criticized, ignored, or misunderstood. The clearer the pain in the dream, the more likely some remark or attitude is still sitting with you, undigested.

variants.q: Dreaming of many scorpions
variants.a: Common when a lot of pressure arrives at once, like handling several matters or several people at the same time. A large number doesn't necessarily mean things are serious. It's that you feel you have to be careful everywhere.

variants.q: Dreaming of killing a scorpion
variants.a: It may reflect that you badly want to get rid of a trouble lately, or have already made up your mind to face it. Solving it in the dream usually brings relief on waking, but in real life it still depends on what you do.

variants.q: Dreaming of a scorpion crawling on my body
variants.a: Often linked to worries you can't shake, perhaps a relationship or a responsibility that keeps hanging over you. It may also be a bodily sensation before sleep that the dream turned into an image.

variants.q: Dreaming of a scorpion in the bed or under the covers
variants.a: A bed is a place to rest, and this dream often appears in times when even relaxing doesn't feel quite safe, such as when something is going on at home, there's friction in a relationship, or your sleep itself is unsettled.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a scorpion mean there are petty people around me?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a scorpion bad?
faq.a: A dream is not a forecast. Most of the time it just carries your daytime guardedness, tension, or an image into sleep. If this dream keeps disturbing your sleep, you can talk to a doctor.

mother.name: mother
mother.title: What does it mean to dream about your mother? Common beliefs and psychological readings
mother.lead: Dreaming of your mother is very common, from everyday time together to long stretches apart. Traditional dream readings often link a mother with care and concern. In waking life, these dreams usually relate to how you've felt about home lately, and your need to be cared for or to care for someone.
mother.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree. One kind reads dreaming of your mother as "something going on at home, and you're worried," nudging you to pay more attention to your family. Another sees the mother as a symbol of shelter, meaning there is supportive strength in your life. Some versions explain it by the mother's state in the dream, such as smiling, angry, or silent, each with a different meaning. These accounts are inconsistent, and the same dream may point in completely different directions in different versions, so treat them only as cultural reference.
mother.plain: Dreaming of your mother often happens when you "need to be cared for" or are "caring for someone." Maybe you've been more tired lately and want to go home, or want someone to ask if you've eaten. Or there may be things unsaid between you and your mother that you avoid by day and dream about at night. Some people dream of their mother at turning points, like changing jobs, moving, or a shift in a relationship, when the heart naturally returns to the most familiar person. If your mother has passed away, dreaming of her is often tied to missing her or an image you haven't let go of, and strong feelings on waking are normal. Notice what you were doing together and the mood in the dream. That usually says more about your present state than "what dreaming of your mother means."

variants.q: Dreaming of my mother being sick or unwell
variants.a: Traditionally this can worry people, but in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. Such dreams often reflect your concern for your mother, or that you yourself are tired or under stress lately, and the dream turns it into an image of family.

variants.q: Dreaming of my mother being angry or scolding me
variants.a: Often matches a daytime feeling that you "didn't do something well," or something unsaid between you and your mother. It may also be guilt about something, appearing in the dream through your mother's image.

variants.q: Dreaming of my mother passing away or leaving
variants.a: This kind of dream can wake you with a start. Traditionally it's read as worry and reluctance to let go, not as a sign that anything will happen. It tends to come up when you're afraid of losing someone or are going through a separation.

variants.q: Dreaming of a mother you haven't seen in a long time
variants.a: Often seen when you're homesick, want to be looked after, or lately lack familiar support in your life. A scene, a smell, or a holiday may also have reminded you of her.

variants.q: Dreaming of a mother who is smiling or gentle
variants.a: You usually wake up feeling warm. This kind of dream often comes when you need support, and the sense of safety in it shows that part of you already knows where you can lean a little.

faq.q: Does dreaming of my mother mean something will happen in the family?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a mother who has passed away?
faq.a: Traditionally it's read as longing and attachment, not as a sign that anything will happen. These dreams often come around holidays, anniversaries of a death, or times of change in your life, so feeling a lot afterward is normal.

father.name: father
father.title: What does it mean to dream about your father? Common views and psychological readings
father.lead: A dream about your father might be an ordinary scene, an argument, or him sitting in silence. Traditional dream lore says several different things about fathers; in waking life, these dreams often relate to how much you've been thinking about responsibility, authority, and being recognized.
father.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say the following. Some versions read dreaming of your father as "something at home needs attention," while others see it as "an elder or a person in authority is watching over you." Some also divide the meaning by your father's manner in the dream, such as a happy father, a scolding father, or a silent father, each with its own reading. Another group of versions links the father with "responsibility and rules," so that dreaming of him means you've lately been wondering whether you're doing things well. These versions differ widely, and none of them is the final word.
father.plain: Dreams of your father often appear when you're facing a situation in which you feel judged. It may be a boss or a performance review at work, or you may hold yourself to a high standard, or there may be a long-standing distance between you and your father that you don't think about by day but dream about at night. Some people dream of their father around a major decision, when a voice asking "what would he think?" rises in their mind. If your father has passed away, dreaming of him often relates to missing him or to something left unsaid. Notice whether in the dream you wanted to move closer to him or avoid him. That direction usually matches how you feel right now about responsibility or authority.

variants.q: Dreaming of my father being angry with me or scolding me
variants.a: This often matches a recent feeling of "not being good enough" or a fear of being rejected. It may also be that there's unfinished business between you and your father. The scolding in the dream is usually that harsh voice inside you.

variants.q: Dreaming of my father being sick or frail
variants.a: Traditionally this can leave you worried, but in waking life it doesn't mean it will happen. These dreams often reflect your concern for your father, or that you've been worn out lately, with the dream turning that fatigue into the image of a family member.

variants.q: Dreaming of my father dying
variants.a: This kind of dream can be unsettling. Traditionally it's read as worry and reluctance to let go, not as a sign that anything will happen. It often comes up when you're afraid of losing someone or are going through some kind of separation.

variants.q: Dreaming of arguing with my father
variants.a: Often seen when there's something you didn't say, or frustration you didn't let out, during the day. Arguing it out in the dream can actually show how much you want to state your position clearly. Whether and how to say it in waking life is still up to you.

variants.q: Dreaming of my father silent or with his back turned
variants.a: This is often tied to the feeling of getting no response. It may be about your relationship with your father, or about the same sense of loss with someone in authority or someone important to you.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a father who has passed away?
faq.a: Traditionally it's read as longing and attachment, not as a sign that anything will happen. These dreams often come around holidays, anniversaries of a death, or times of change in your life, and it's normal to wake up feeling heavy.

Another group links the grandmother with "old matters and roots," so that dreaming of her means you've lately been recalling the past. These versions don't agree with one another and are only a cultural reference.
grandmother.plain: Dreams of your grandmother often come when part of you wants to be cherished and cared for. You may have been tired lately, with nobody in your life asking how you are, or a certain smell, dish, or holiday may have reminded you of her. Some people dream of their grandmother during a move, a job change, or a shift in a relationship, when the mind naturally returns to the safest scene of childhood. If your grandmother has passed away, dreaming of her often relates to missing her, and it's normal to wake up wanting to cry. Notice what she said to you in the dream and whether you heard it clearly. That sentence is often what you most want to hear right now.

variants.q: Dreaming of my grandmother being sick or unwell

variants.q: Dreaming of my grandmother giving me instructions
variants.a: Often seen when there's something you haven't yet decided, and the dream borrows your grandmother's image to give you direction. Her words aren't necessarily a prophecy, but they may be an answer you already knew and just haven't faced yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of grandmother smiling or giving me something
variants.a: Most people wake up feeling warm inside. This kind of dream often shows up when you need support. It reflects a memory of being cared for that still lives in you, and it may be a nudge to be a little kinder to yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of time with grandmother in childhood
variants.a: This is often tied to homesickness or a longing for simpler days. It may also be that stress has been high lately, and your mind brings up its most comforting picture to balance things out.

Some people dream of him when work or family duties grow heavier, and find themselves thinking, "What would he have done?" If your grandfather has passed away, dreaming of him is often tied to missing him, or to words you never got to ask. Notice whether he was stern or gentle in the dream. That usually matches how you feel right now about rules and about yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of grandfather being angry or scolding me

child.name: children
child.title: What does it mean to dream about a child? Common scenes and psychological readings
child.lead: Dreaming of a child is mostly about "things just beginning" or "parts of you that need care." You may be busy with a new project, or a vulnerable part of you that wants looking after may be coming to the surface. Traditional views vary, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.
child.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common views on dreaming of a child. One treats a child as "new life, a beginning," linking the dream to new matters or new relationships. Another says the child stands for a younger family member or happy news to come. Some versions read a crying, fussing child as something weighing on your mind that is unfinished. The versions differ quite a bit, and even copies of the same book from different regions often disagree, so take this only as a cultural reference, not a forecast.
child.plain: If you're starting something new in daily life, such as changing jobs, learning something, or beginning a relationship, a child in your dream is common. It's as if the part of you that is "not grown yet, still tender" has been brought on stage. You may also be caring for someone, or be expected to, and feel tired and wish to be cared for yourself, so you dream of a child. Another common case: you feel responsible for something and fear you won't do it well, so the child in the dream seems naughty and hard to manage. All of this points to what matters to you now, not to what will happen. When you wake, ask yourself: what lately feels "just begun and not yet steady"? That is probably what the dream is responding to.

variants.q: Dreaming of my own child
variants.a: This is common in times of lots of parent-child interaction, or when you're worried about your child. It may also be that you're carrying something "child-like" in your mind, such as a project just getting started, which you can't stop worrying about by day and so dream of at night.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else's child
variants.a: It may reflect how you see other people's responsibilities, or that you're watching something grow nearby without being able to step in. If the child in the dream is a stranger, it may simply be that you saw related images during the day and they were carried into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of a child crying
variants.a: This is common when something is left unresolved and you can't bring yourself to say it. In dreams, crying often works like a reminder that a need is being overlooked. You might ask whether you've been holding words back lately, or putting something off.

variants.q: Dreaming of a child laughing and following you
variants.a: This dream mostly shows up when you're feeling more relaxed and things are moving forward. It may also mean you feel at ease about a relationship or a new beginning, and the dream shows it in a light, easy scene.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lot of children
variants.a: Common when many things arrive at once and you feel a bit overwhelmed. It may also be that you've been in a busy, crowded setting lately, looking after many things at once. You're busy by day, and your dreams are busy at night.

baby.name: baby
baby.title: What does it mean to dream about a baby? From tradition to daytime clues
baby.lead: Dreaming of a baby is often linked to something that has just begun to sprout, or to a fragile state that needs protecting. Some read a baby as a new beginning or joy coming to the household. Others say a baby stands for someone small and vulnerable who needs care, so holding a baby means you take a responsibility to heart. Some versions read a crying baby as something unfinished on your mind. Because the versions differ and even contradict each other, treat them as cultural reference only, not as a forecast.
baby.plain: If you're waiting on a result during the day, such as a proposal, an exam, or the next step in a relationship, dreaming of a baby is very common. It's as if that unformed, fragile thing inside you has been brought out to look at. You may also feel shaky lately, as if you don't know how to do anything yet and are afraid of breaking it, so a baby you have to hold carefully appears in the dream. Another common case is that you're caring for a person or a task and feel the weight of it, so even in sleep you're "watching over" it. These dreams usually come with concern, tension, or anticipation, and are not a preview of future events. When you wake, ask yourself: what is just beginning and still fragile for me right now? That is probably what the dream is responding to.

variants.q: Dreaming of holding a baby
variants.a: Common when you're carefully tending something, such as a new relationship or a project just getting started. Holding reflects a sense of responsibility and protectiveness. It may also simply come from having held a child or seen related images during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a baby crying
variants.a: Mostly points to a need inside you that hasn't been heard, or something that's been left unresolved. The crying works like a reminder. You might think about whether there's something you haven't said, or something you've been putting off.

variants.q: Dreaming of a baby laughing
variants.a: Often appears when you feel more relaxed and things are looking up. It may also mean you feel at ease about a new beginning, and the dream shows it in a light scene.

variants.q: Dreaming of a baby missing or not being able to find one
variants.a: Common when you're worried something is slipping out of control, or afraid you've missed something. This kind of dream reflects anxiety, not a forecast. You can look back at what has been making you especially uneasy lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else's baby
variants.a: It may reflect that you're watching something grow from the sidelines, or that you feel a responsibility toward others. If the baby is a stranger, it may simply be an image from your day carried into the dream.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a baby mean pregnancy or a new addition to the family?

faq.q: Is it bad to dream of a baby who won't stop crying?
faq.a: Crying in a dream usually points to feelings or worries left unresolved during the day. It doesn't mean anything will happen. If these dreams keep recurring and affect your sleep, it's worth talking with a doctor, and also noticing whether something has been left sitting lately.

stranger.name: stranger
stranger.title: What does it mean to dream about a stranger? How to read an unfamiliar person in a dream
stranger.lead: Dreaming of a stranger is often linked to unfamiliar situations you're facing, or to parts of yourself you haven't met yet. It could be a new environment, a new relationship, or something inside you that hasn't been seen. Traditional views come in several versions, and in waking life the dream doesn't mean anything will happen.

Some say a stranger means new contacts or news from outside. Others read an unfamiliar face as an unfamiliar part of yourself. Some versions say being chased by a stranger means something is undecided. The versions differ greatly and even contradict each other, so treat them as cultural reference only, not a forecast.
stranger.plain: If you've recently changed environments, joined a new team, or met new friends, unfamiliar faces in dreams are very common. The brain carries faces and situations you haven't finished processing into the dream. You may also be facing something unfamiliar and feel unsure, so a stranger stands in for the part you don't know yet and can't get a grip on. Another common case is that you're wary of a relationship or a decision, so the stranger in the dream feels distant or imposing. These dreams usually come with freshness, tension, or caution, and are not a preview of who you'll meet. When you wake, think about which situation lately feels strange and not yet familiar. That is probably what the dream is responding to.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a stranger
variants.a: Common when you're under stress and have been avoiding something. The chase reflects anxiety, not a forecast. You can think about what lately makes you especially want to run.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stranger smiling at you or helping you
variants.a: Mostly appears when you feel fairly at ease in a new environment, or hope someone will help. It may also be a friendly scene from your day carried into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of talking with a stranger
variants.a: Often corresponds to having to deal with people you don't know well lately, or having something you want to say to someone you don't yet know well. What's said in the dream usually reflects what's on your mind during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of many strangers
variants.a: Common when you're in a crowded, lively setting and have to deal with many faces. It may also be that you've been very social lately, so you're tired by day and your dreams are lively at night.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stranger who looks like someone you know
variants.a: This is very common. The brain mixes familiar faces with unfamiliar situations. It usually reflects your complicated feelings about a relationship or a person, not a forecast.

faq.q: Should I worry if I keep dreaming of being chased by a stranger?

celebrity.name: celebrity
celebrity.title: What does it mean to dream about a celebrity? A psychological reading of dreaming of stars and public figures
celebrity.lead: Dreaming of a celebrity often relates to how much you care about being seen, or about some ideal state. You may be paying close attention to a certain field lately, or you may want to become a certain kind of person. Tradition offers several versions, and in waking life none of them means something will happen.
celebrity.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have no single view on dreaming of a celebrity. Some read dreams of powerful or well-known people as having a helpful person or outside support. Others say it stands for fame or being noticed. Some versions remind you that such dreams reflect what you long for. The versions differ a lot, and most were written long ago, when "celebrity" meant something different from today. Take them as cultural reference, not a forecast.
celebrity.plain: If you've been watching a certain star or a popular figure in some field, it's very common for them to show up in your dreams, since the brain carries daytime images into sleep. You may also be in a stretch where you want to be seen and affirmed, and the celebrity stands for that ideal or the person you long to be. Another common case is comparison: you feel others are doing well and you're a step behind, so a "shining" person appears. These dreams usually come with attention, envy and self-expectation, and are not a sign that you'll meet someone. On waking, you can ask: whose opinion have I cared about lately? Or who do I want to become? That is probably what the dream is responding to.

variants.q: Dreaming of taking a photo or chatting with a celebrity
variants.a: Common when you badly want to be affirmed, or are putting a lot into some field. The interaction reflects what you long for, and it may also be from taking in too much related content during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a celebrity liking you
variants.a: This mostly relates to the part of you that wants to be noticed and appreciated. Such dreams are very common and reflect self-expectation, not a forecast of who will appear.

variants.q: Dreaming of a celebrity in trouble or ill
variants.a: Common when you're paying close attention to a public figure, or feeling uneasy inside. The plot reflects what you care about and doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a celebrity you know being cold to you
variants.a: It may reflect feeling overlooked or compared with others lately, in relationships or at work. The plot is a projection of feeling, not a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of many celebrities
variants.a: Common when you've been taking in a lot of one kind of content, or are in settings where you must deal with many "standout" people. You take in a lot by day, and your dreams get busy at night.

celebrity.ask: If the celebrity in your dream, or the wish to be seen, stays on your mind after you wake, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
celebrity.askQ: Will there be movement on the thing where I most want to be affirmed lately?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a celebrity mean good luck?
faq.a: Some traditional dream books link well-known people to helpful people and support, but the versions differ and none is a forecast. In waking life, this dream more often reflects the field you've been following or a wish to be seen, so it's more useful as a clue for self-observation.

faq.q: Should I worry if I dream of a celebrity in trouble?
faq.a: The plot usually matches your attention to that person or some unease inside you, and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. If such dreams keep coming back and cost you sleep, you can talk to a doctor about your sleep.

teacher.name: teacher
teacher.title: What does it mean to dream about a teacher? A reading of teachers and being taught in dreams
teacher.lead: Dreaming of a teacher is often tied to being judged, wanting to understand something, or your inner standards. You may be learning something new lately, or still unsure about a decision. Tradition offers several versions, and in waking life none of them means something will happen.
teacher.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on dreaming of a teacher. Some read teachers and elders as guidance and support. Others say being taught in a dream means something remains to be learned or clarified. Some versions read a teacher's strictness as your own self-demand. The versions differ a lot, and most don't know modern schools. Take them as cultural reference, not a forecast.
teacher.plain: If you've been learning something new, preparing for exams, or entering a setting where you're being guided, dreaming of a teacher is very common, since the brain carries daytime learning into sleep. You may also be in a stretch of fearing mistakes and judgment, and the teacher stands for the standard watching you. Another common case is being unsure about a decision and hoping someone will point the way, so a teacher appears. These dreams usually come with learning, self-demand and a wish for guidance, and are not a forecast of what will happen. On waking, you can ask: what lately makes me feel I'm still learning and not yet sure? That is probably what the dream is responding to.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scolded by a teacher
variants.a: Common when you're demanding a lot of yourself, or afraid of being judged. The scolding reflects your inner standards, not a forecast. You can think about what lately makes you especially afraid of getting it wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of a teacher being very kind to you
variants.a: Mostly appears when you long for guidance and affirmation. It may also be someone who helped you during the day, carried into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of a former teacher
variants.a: Very common. The brain often places familiar people from the past into current dreams. It usually reflects how you feel about that period or a certain standard, not a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of a teacher teaching you something
variants.a: Often matches learning something new lately, or wanting to understand something. The teaching reflects your state of learning, and it may also be daytime material replaying in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of a teacher missing or being unable to find them
variants.a: This often shows up when you're unsure about a decision and wish someone would point the way. The dream reflects a wish for guidance. It isn't a forecast.

teacher.ask: If the teacher in your dream, or that still-undecided choice, stays on your mind after you wake, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
teacher.askQ: Will there be any movement on the decision I've been unsure about lately?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about a teacher?
faq.a: The traditional dream books don't agree. Some link it to guidance and being helped along, others read it as something that still needs sorting out, and there's no settled view. In waking life, this dream more often reflects that you're learning something lately, that you hold yourself to a high standard, or that you worry about being judged. It's more useful as a clue for observing yourself.

faq.q: Is it a bad sign to dream about a teacher scolding me?
faq.a: Being scolded in a dream usually matches the standards you hold inside or your tension about making mistakes. It doesn't mean anything will happen. If these dreams keep coming back and cost you sleep, you can talk to a doctor about your sleep, and also notice which recent matter is putting you under extra pressure.

doctor.name: doctor
doctor.title: What does it mean to dream about a doctor? Common scenarios and a plain reading
doctor.lead: Dreaming of a doctor is mostly not a warning that something is wrong with your body. More often it means you're especially tuned in lately to things like checking, repairing and being cared for. You may be tired, a little worried about your health, or looking for someone to help you sort out where things stand.
doctor.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that dreaming of a doctor visiting your home means someone in your life will look in on you and offer guidance. Dreaming of going to see a doctor is often read as a reminder to watch your routine and not push through. Some versions link the doctor to a helpful benefactor, someone nearby who will give you advice. These sayings differ from book to book. Some lean toward the body, others toward relationships, and there is no single version, so take them as cultural interest.
doctor.plain: In waking life, dreaming of a doctor often follows a few kinds of moods. One is a small health matter, or you've just had a checkup or appointment and your mind keeps circling it. Another is that you've been especially tired, short on sleep and worn down, and part of you is calling out for rest. A third is that you're stuck on a problem and wish someone would just tell you what to do, or give you a diagnosis. You may also be caring for someone, or being cared for, and the question of who will handle things slips into the dream. Whether the doctor is gentle or cold often reflects whether you feel supported or scrutinized right now. Take it as a reminder to check whether you need to slow down or talk with someone.

variants.q: Dreaming of a doctor telling me I'm fine
variants.a: Common right after a checkup, when a weight has lifted. Or you've been worrying about something, and the dream reaches the conclusion that all is well, reflecting your wish to feel at ease.

variants.q: Dreaming of a doctor telling me I'm sick
variants.a: Traditionally this gets discussed, but in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. More likely you've been extra sensitive about your body or about some matter, and small things from the day get magnified.

variants.q: Dreaming of going to the hospital to see a doctor
variants.a: Often appears when you want to ask for help or find answers. In the dream, the hospital is a place where things get made clear, reflecting that you don't want to stay in the fog any longer.

variants.q: Dreaming of a doctor I know
variants.a: You may care a lot about that person's opinion lately, or hope they can give you direction. Or you may be casting yourself as the one responsible for solving the problem.

variants.q: Dreaming of many doctors
variants.a: Common when you're surrounded by lots of advice and feel a bit lost. It may also be that you're handling something that needs confirmation from several sides, and you want to ask everything at once.

doctor.ask: If a particular person appears in your dream, or something keeps weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
doctor.askQ: Will I hear any news about the matter that's been on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a doctor mean something is wrong with my health?
faq.a: Traditional sayings come in different versions, but in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. The dream more often reflects your recent tiredness and worries. If your body really feels unwell, or you keep having nightmares and sleeping badly, you can talk to a doctor.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a doctor examining me?
faq.a: It mostly relates to wanting to check where things stand, whether that's health, work or a relationship. Being examined in a dream often matches the daytime feeling of wanting reassurance while fearing that problems will be found.

police.name: police
police.title: What does it mean to dream about the police? Being chased or questioned, explained
police.lead: Dreaming of the police is usually tied to rules, responsibility and being watched. You may be afraid of making mistakes or being judged lately, or there may be something you know you should deal with but haven't.
police.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that dreaming of the police means someone will keep you in check and remind you to follow the rules. Dreaming of being chased by the police is often said to mean something is weighing on your mind. Some versions link the police to officialdom, tying the dream to paperwork, procedures or disputes. These sayings differ by version, some leaning toward relationships and others toward getting things done, so take them as cultural reference.
police.plain: In waking life, dreaming of the police often follows a few kinds of moods. One is that you're especially concerned about doing things right and not crossing a line, perhaps because work has rules or evaluations. Another is that you've been putting something off, like a message to answer or a procedure to complete, and in the dream it becomes someone coming to question you. A third is that you're in a position of being observed, such as a new environment, a new manager, or results to hand in. Whether the police are polite or stern often reflects whether you feel the outside world is reasonable or picking on you. You may also be wishing someone would come and keep order, so a chaotic situation gets an explanation. Take it as a reminder: see what's been left sitting, and deal with a little of it first. You may feel lighter.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by the police
variants.a: Common when you want to avoid something, such as a deadline, a responsibility, or a conversation that's hard to start. Getting tired from running in the dream reflects that you've been tense during the day too.

variants.q: Dreaming of the police coming to my home
variants.a: You may be especially sensitive lately about your private space being intruded on, or something at home needs attention. Or you may worry that something can't stay hidden, and your mind has rehearsed it first.

variants.q: Dreaming of the police questioning me
variants.a: Often appears when you need to explain yourself or give an account. Being questioned in the dream reflects that you've been rehearsing in your head how best to say it.

variants.q: Dreaming of the police helping me
variants.a: You may be hoping lately that someone will step in and set things right, or help you clear up a confusing situation. Or you may need a clear rule to feel at ease.

variants.q: Dreaming of a police officer as a bad person
variants.a: Traditionally this gets discussed, but in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. More likely you don't quite trust someone in a position of power, or feel the rules work against you.

police.ask: If a specific person shows up in your dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
police.askQ: What's the best way for me to handle the thing that's been weighing on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming about police mean something is going to happen?
faq.a: Traditional sayings vary from book to book, but none of them means it will happen in real life. The dream more often reflects your recent stress and sense of responsibility. If you keep having bad dreams or aren't sleeping well, it's worth talking to a doctor.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about being chased by the police?
faq.a: It's often tied to something you've been wanting to avoid lately, such as work, money, or a relationship. Being chased in a dream often matches that daytime feeling of "putting this off isn't going to work."

thief.name: thief
thief.title: What does it mean to dream about a thief? Reading things stolen and break-ins
thief.lead: Dreaming of a thief is usually linked to a fear of losing something or of being seen through. You may feel that something is slipping out of your control lately, or there's a part of you that you don't want others to touch.
thief.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this: a thief entering the house is read as a sign to watch your belongings or your relationships; having something stolen is often described as a feeling of loss inside. Some versions say the opposite, that getting something back in the dream is a good thing. The versions differ, some focusing on money and property, others on feelings, so it's best taken as cultural curiosity.
thief.plain: In waking life, dreaming of a thief often follows a few kinds of feelings. One is that your time, money, or energy keeps getting used up and you can't say who is taking it. Another is worry that something will be found out or misunderstood, a tension of being "opened up." A third is being in the middle of a change, like a new job, a move, or a shift in a relationship, when your sense of security is thinner. Whether the thief comes quietly or there's a direct confrontation often reflects whether the loss feels gradual or sudden. You may also be very aware of an opportunity someone else might get to first, and that sense of competition carries into the dream. Take it as a nudge to look at what you're guarding lately, and what you're afraid to lose.

variants.q: Dreaming of having something stolen
variants.a: This is common when something feels out of your control lately, perhaps money, time, or a relationship. The sense of loss in the dream often matches that daytime unease of "why is there less?"

variants.q: Dreaming of a thief in your home
variants.a: You may be especially sensitive about your private space lately, or something at home makes you feel intruded on. You might also be worried that a private matter will become known.

variants.q: Dreaming of catching a thief
variants.a: This often comes up when you're trying to get to the bottom of something or want an explanation. Catching someone in the dream reflects a wish to make a murky situation clear once and for all.

variants.q: Dreaming of a thief you know
variants.a: You may be wary of a certain person, or feel you give more in a relationship. It could also be that you're projecting outward a side of yourself that you don't want seen.

variants.q: Dreaming of money being stolen
variants.a: This is common when you're especially mindful of spending, income, or how your resources are divided. Money going missing in a dream often matches that daytime pressure of "no matter how I count, it's still not enough."
