thief.ask: If a specific person shows up in your dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
thief.askQ: How will the thing I've been afraid of losing develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming about a thief mean I'll lose money?
faq.a: Traditional sayings vary from book to book, but none of them means it will happen in real life. The dream more often reflects a recent sense of loss or unease. If you keep having bad dreams or aren't sleeping well, it's worth talking to a doctor.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about having something stolen?
faq.a: It's mostly tied to something that feels out of your control lately, such as time, money, or a relationship. Being robbed in a dream often matches a daytime fear of not being able to hold on.

ghost.name: ghost
ghost.title: What does it mean to dream about a ghost? Reading pressure, being chased, and faces you can't make out
ghost.lead: Dreaming of a ghost is usually linked to hard-to-name pressure and emotions you can't put down. Something may have been hanging over you lately, or there's a part of you that you don't dare touch.
ghost.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this: seeing a ghost is read as something unfinished on your mind, or surroundings that make you uneasy; being chased by a ghost is often described as pressure pushing from behind. Some versions hold that not being afraid of the ghost, or even talking with it, means you're slowly facing something inside. The versions differ, some focusing on emotions, others on surroundings, so it's best taken as cultural reference.
ghost.plain: In waking life, dreaming of a ghost often follows a few kinds of feelings. One is heavy stress and poor sleep, where the body reacts first and dreams get more jumbled. Another is something you don't want to face, like an unresolved conflict or words left unsaid. A third is being in an unfamiliar or uncertain setting, when you feel less secure. Whether the ghost is blurry or has a clear face often reflects whether you know what you're afraid of. You may also have watched a show or heard a story recently, and the images carried into the dream. Tradition tends to treat these dreams as weighty, but none of it means something will happen in real life. Take it as a nudge to see what has been keeping you from sleeping soundly, and start with what you can deal with.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased by a ghost
variants.a: This is common when you want to avoid something, perhaps pressure, a deadline, or a hard conversation. Running nonstop in the dream reflects staying tense during the day too.

variants.q: Dreaming of ghost pressing (sleep paralysis)
variants.a: This often happens with an irregular schedule, extreme tiredness, or an awkward sleeping position, when the body is half awake but can't move. Traditional explanations are many, but in real life it's mostly related to the state of your sleep. If it keeps happening, it's worth talking to a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of a ghost without being afraid
variants.a: You may be gradually getting better at facing something you used to fear. Not being afraid in the dream often matches the daytime feeling of "maybe it isn't that serious."

variants.q: Dreaming of a ghost you know
variants.a: You may have unspoken feelings toward that person, or have been thinking of them often lately. Appearing in another form in the dream reflects that the relationship still stays with you.

variants.q: Dreaming of many ghosts
variants.a: This is common when many things are weighing on you at once and you feel a bit breathless. It may also be that a lot has changed around you lately and you haven't found your footing yet.

ghost.ask: If a specific person shows up in your dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
ghost.askQ: What will happen next with the thing I can't seem to let go of lately?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a ghost mean something unclean?
faq.a: Folk sayings vary from one version to the next, and in real life they don't mean anything will happen. Dreams more often reflect your recent stress and how you're sleeping. If you keep having nightmares or can't sleep well, it can help to talk with a doctor.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of being chased by a ghost?
faq.a: It's often about something you've been wanting to avoid lately, such as stress, a responsibility, or a relationship. Being chased in a dream often matches that daytime feeling of keeping something on the back burner.

ancestor.name: ancestors
ancestor.title: What does it mean to dream of ancestors? Readings for dreams of them coming back or giving instructions
ancestor.lead: Dreaming of ancestors is usually tied to missing someone, family connection, or something on your mind that you want to settle. You may have been thinking of family a lot lately, or you may be at a moment when you need to make a decision.
ancestor.trad: In the folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common saying is that dreaming of ancestors is read as a family matter that needs discussing, or a reminder not to forget your roots. Dreaming of ancestors giving instructions is often said to mean there's something on your mind you haven't said out loud. Some versions also hold that if the ancestors look peaceful in the dream, it shows you feel more settled inside. These sayings differ from version to version, some leaning toward family, some toward mood, so take them as cultural reference only.
ancestor.plain: In waking life, dreams of ancestors often follow a few kinds of moods. One is that you've been thinking often about family, your old home, or someone who is no longer here. Another is that you're stuck at a moment when you need to decide something, and part of you hopes for an elder's strength to point the way. A third is that something is going on in the family, like a gathering, dividing up belongings, or caring for older relatives, and those thoughts carry over into the dream. Whether the ancestors seem gentle or stern often reflects whether you feel supported or expected to live up to something. It could also be that you've been sorting through old things or came across photos, and the image just connected. Tradition tends to treat this kind of dream as weighty, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. Take it as a reminder to look at who you've been caring about, and what you haven't said.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ancestor talking to you
variants.a: Often seen when there's something you want to talk over with someone but haven't brought up yet. The words in the dream are often an answer you already had in your heart.

variants.q: Dreaming of an ancestor coming back to the house
variants.a: You may have been thinking often about your old home or family, or something may be going on in the family. Coming back in a dream often matches that daytime thought of "I should go back and visit."

variants.q: Dreaming of an ancestor giving instructions
variants.a: Traditionally it gets talked about, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. More likely there's something you need to deal with, and your mind uses the figure of an elder to remind you.

variants.q: Dreaming of an unhappy ancestor
variants.a: You may feel guilty about something lately, or feel you haven't done what you should. The expression in the dream often reflects what you expect of yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of many ancestors
variants.a: Often seen around family gatherings and holidays, or when you're dealing with something family-related. It may also be that you've been longing for a sense of belonging.

ancestor.ask: If a specific person appears in your dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which coming days may bring movement.
ancestor.askQ: Will I hear news about the thing weighing on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of ancestors mean they have something to tell me?
faq.a: Folk sayings vary from one version to the next, and in real life they don't mean anything will happen. Dreams more often reflect how much you've been missing someone and what you're carrying in your heart. If you feel uneasy, it can help to talk with family.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of ancestors coming back?
faq.a: It's often about thinking of family a lot lately, or being at a moment when you have to decide something. Coming back in a dream often matches that daytime feeling of wanting something to lean on.

twins.name: twins
twins.title: What does it mean to dream of twins?
twins.lead: Dreaming of twins is usually not a forecast of anything good or bad. More often you're carrying two things of equal weight at once, or you feel pulled between two versions of yourself.
twins.trad: In the folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), twins aren't a common entry, and the sayings differ quite a bit. Some versions read a pair as good things coming in twos, or having company in your relationships. Others focus on repetition, taking it to mean the same matter keeps coming up and your attention is split. Some older sayings link dreaming of twins to the difficulty of having to look after both sides. Because the versions don't agree, take it as a cultural curiosity rather than a conclusion.
twins.plain: In waking life, you may be stuck between two choices: two jobs, two cities, two identities, or wanting to move closer to and pull back from the same person at once. You may also have been asked lately to do well on both fronts, such as family and work, or your own expectations and other people's, and feel stretched thin. Two identical people in a dream often show up when you're trying to work out which one is really you. If the twins feel close and comforting, it may reflect a wish for someone who understands you. If it feels confusing and you can't tell them apart, it may match the tiredness of too much information and too many roles during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of twin babies
variants.a: Babies are often linked to things just beginning and still fragile. You may have two new projects or relationships in the early stage, both needing care, so you feel you have to protect both at once.

variants.q: Dreaming of one twin disappearing
variants.a: Often seen when you're weighing what to give up. One missing in the dream may match having quietly dropped one option during the day, though you haven't fully let go of it yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of being one of the twins
variants.a: It may reflect a gap you've been feeling lately between "how others see me" and "what I really want," with both versions of you present at once.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to tell the twins apart
variants.a: It's often linked to confusion and overlapping roles. You may be playing too many roles during the day, so you can't tell for a moment which reaction is really yours.

variants.q: Dreaming of twins arguing
variants.a: It may match two voices inside you in conflict, such as reason versus feeling, or what you should do versus what you want to do, which the dream plays out as two people quarreling.

twins.ask: If the two figures in your dream remind you of a specific person or something you haven't decided yet, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which coming days may bring movement.
twins.askQ: Of the two choices on my mind, which one will I hear about first?

faq.q: Does dreaming about twins mean I'll have twins?
faq.a: Folk belief sometimes makes this link, but dreams aren't tied to childbirth, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. Most of the time it reflects a state of mind where you're handling two things at once.

faq.q: Should I worry if I keep dreaming about twins?
faq.a: An occasional twin dream is very common and usually fades as your routine shifts. If these dreams keep coming back, cost you sleep, or leave you unsettled during the day, it can help to talk with a doctor.

crying-person.name: person crying
crying-person.title: What does it mean to dream about a person crying?
crying-person.lead: Dreaming that someone is crying usually isn't a bad omen. More often it points to feelings you haven't said aloud about a relationship or situation, and the dream acts them out through someone else.
crying-person.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) treat crying in interesting ways. Some versions read crying as feelings easing and things turning smoother. Others say that seeing someone cry in a dream means you have something to say and have been holding it back. Some older people also say that tears in a dream don't necessarily match sadness in real life. The versions contradict one another, so it's closer to cultural association than a firm rule.
crying-person.plain: In waking life, you may be holding down some feeling: feeling wronged, guilty, missing someone, or worrying about another person. The person crying might be someone you care about, a stranger, or a face you can't place. That unfamiliar face often shows up when you aren't ready to admit you're sad. If you comfort them in the dream, it may reflect a habit of looking after others' feelings while rarely asking how you are. If you just stand and watch, it may match a real situation where you want to help but can't find a way in. Dreams of crying also often come after a goodbye, a job change, or a shift in a relationship, as the mind slowly works through it.

variants.q: Dreaming of crying yourself
variants.a: You may have been holding back all day, and the dream lets you finally release it. This is common when stress builds up to a certain point, or when you finally admit that something matters to you.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone you know crying
variants.a: This usually connects to your concern for that person, or to something unresolved between you. The tears in the dream are often feelings you're expressing on their behalf.

variants.q: Dreaming of crying and being unable to stop
variants.a: It may correspond to an emotional load that feels heavy lately, with no outlet during the day. The dream magnifies it, nudging you to notice how tired you are.

variants.q: Dreaming of comforting someone who is crying
variants.a: This is common when you've been playing the supporter lately. Comforting someone in the dream may also reflect a wish for someone to comfort you in the same way.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing after crying
variants.a: This often appears during an emotional turning point, such as finally making sense of something or feeling tension loosen. The dream strings it together with tears and laughter.

crying-person.ask: If the crying face in your dream reminds you of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what might stir in the coming days.
crying-person.askQ: Will there be any further developments with what was left unsaid between that person and me?

faq.q: Is it unlucky to dream of someone crying?
faq.a: Folk tradition has all sorts of associations, but a dream doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. Dreams of crying mostly reflect your recent mood and what's on your mind, not a forecast.

faq.q: Does dreaming of crying mean I'm under too much stress?
faq.a: It might. Dreams of crying are common when feelings have built up or life is changing. If these dreams keep coming back and affect your sleep, it can help to talk with a doctor.

laughing-person.name: person laughing loudly
laughing-person.chip: Dreaming of a person laughing loudly
laughing-person.title: What does it mean to dream about a person laughing loudly?
laughing-person.lead: Dreaming that someone is laughing loudly is mostly not an omen. It tends to point to a need to loosen up or to be seen, and it may also reflect a sense of distance in some relationship.
laughing-person.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree about laughter. Some versions read joyful laughter in a dream as harmony with others and a light heart. Others warn that laughter that is especially loud or exaggerated may match occasions in waking life where you're forcing a smile. Some also say that dreaming of others laughing means you're currently concerned with how people see you. The versions differ, so take them as a reference only.
laughing-person.plain: In waking life, you may have just come out of a tense stretch and relaxed, or the opposite: you may be in a situation where you have to laugh along and keep up appearances. Loud laughter in a dream can be pent-up feeling finding a way out, or envy of someone with unguarded ease. If the laughing person is a stranger, it may reflect a longing for lightness with no burden. If it's someone you know, it often shows that your feelings about that relationship are changing: feeling teased or compared, or simply missing the times you relaxed together. Laughter in a dream can also carry a hint of unease, which usually matches occasions where the mood was great but you didn't feel settled inside.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing loudly yourself
variants.a: You may have rarely been able to relax lately, or, on the contrary, you laughed too hard during the day. Laughter in a dream is often the mind making up for something or releasing it.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone laughing at you
variants.a: This may relate to how much you care about others' opinions. If the smile feels comfortable, it usually reflects a wish to be accepted. If it feels odd, it may match some unease you can't quite name.

variants.q: Dreaming of a group of people roaring with laughter
variants.a: This is common when you're in a lively setting but feel out of place. The dream magnifies that feeling of everyone laughing while you can't keep up.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing until you cry
variants.a: It may correspond to a time when your feelings are very full, with happiness and tiredness mixed together. The dream acts it out as laughter with tears.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughter that sounds eerie
variants.a: This mostly reflects an occasion during the day that left you vaguely uncomfortable without your being able to say why. The dream turns it into a sense of something off in the sound.

laughing-person.ask: If the smile in your dream reminds you of a certain person or something you haven't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what might stir in the coming days.
laughing-person.askQ: What will happen between me and the person who's been weighing on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of others laughing hint at something?
faq.a: Folk tradition has many associations, but a dream doesn't predict real events. Most of the time it reflects how you've been feeling about your recent dealings with people, not what someone else is actually thinking.

faq.q: If I dream of laughing happily, does that mean things will go smoothly lately?
faq.a: Dreams and fortune aren't necessarily linked. Happy dreams often show up when your mood is loosening up, so it's more realistic to treat them as a mirror of how you feel.

angry-person.name: angry person
angry-person.title: What does it mean to dream about an angry person?
angry-person.lead: Dreaming of someone who is angry usually isn't a bad omen. More often it's resentment you held back during the day, a sense that a boundary was crossed, or tension in a relationship finding a way out in your dream.
angry-person.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ quite a bit on anger. Some versions read seeing someone angry in a dream as a sign of more quarrels lately, so watch what you say. Others hold that when you play out the anger in a dream, the feeling eases in waking life. Some older sayings also link dreaming that someone is angry at you with a guilty conscience. The versions don't agree, so there's no need to treat any of them as final.
angry-person.plain: In daily life, you may be in a position where it's hard to show anger: asked to go along with things, misunderstood, or smiling along when you're uncomfortable. The angry person in the dream sometimes has someone's face and sometimes is blurry. Often that's anger you don't dare admit to yourself, appearing in someone else's form. If you're being scolded in the dream, it may relate to how much you care about someone's opinion of you lately. If you're watching someone rage at another person, it may reflect a tense atmosphere around you. These dreams are also common when your boundaries are tested again and again, such as extra work piled on or your personal time taken up.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone being angry at you
variants.a: You may be very aware of someone's opinion of you lately, or feel you've fallen short somewhere. The dream plays that pressure out as the other person's emotion.

variants.q: Dreaming of being angry yourself
variants.a: Common when you've been holding things in all day. Losing your temper in a dream often means something inside is saying, "This really bothers me."

variants.q: Dreaming of a family member losing their temper
variants.a: Usually linked to tension in the family that hasn't been talked through, or worry about a certain family member. Dreams often magnify small everyday frictions.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stranger yelling at you
variants.a: It may reflect a sense of insecurity in your surroundings, such as not yet feeling settled in a new setting or job and feeling you could be singled out at any time.

variants.q: Dreaming of making up after a fight
variants.a: Often appears when a relationship is strained but you want to mend it. The reconciliation in the dream may reflect a hope that things can be talked out.

angry-person.ask: If the anger in your dream brings to mind a person or a matter that's still stuck, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
angry-person.askQ: Will the tension between me and that person take a turn for the better soon?

faq.q: If I dream of someone angry, do I need to watch out for something?
faq.a: Folk tradition says various things, but a dream doesn't predict real events. Most of the time it reflects recent pressure in your relationships or feelings you've held down, not that anyone is actually going to do something to you.

faq.q: If I dream of losing my temper, does that mean my temper is getting worse?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Feelings in dreams are often a buildup from the day that had no outlet. If you also feel tense, irritable, and sleep badly during the day, it may help to talk with a doctor.

hugging.name: hugging
hugging.title: What does it mean to dream about a hug?
hugging.lead: Dreaming of a hug is mostly tied to a need to feel held. You may be longing for closeness, missing a past relationship, or trying to make peace with something.
hugging.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have no single view on hugging. Some versions read an embrace in a dream as harmony between people and closer ties. Others depend on who is in the dream, saying that hugging someone you haven't been in touch with for a long time means the bond is still on your mind. Another saying holds that the tighter the hug in the dream, the more it reflects a longing you couldn't put into words during the day. The versions vary, so take them as cultural associations.
hugging.plain: In daily life, you may be short on support: tired from work, carrying something on your mind with no one to tell, or in a time of change in a relationship. A hug in a dream is sometimes comfort and sometimes a goodbye. If you're hugging someone familiar, it often relates to missing that relationship or a wish to repair it. If it's a stranger or a face you can't make out, it may reflect a longing to be understood, not necessarily pointing to a specific person. How the hug feels also matters. Warm and reassuring may match finally being able to breathe out lately; so tight you can't breathe may reflect pressure or a boundary issue in some relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of hugging an ex
variants.a: Common when you're still processing that relationship. It doesn't necessarily mean you want to get back together. The hug may be your mind saying goodbye to the past or looking for closure.

variants.q: Dreaming of hugging family
variants.a: Usually linked to worry about family, or a closeness between you that's rare in daily life. Dreams often supply the words you didn't say during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of hugging a stranger
variants.a: It may reflect a longing to be understood and held, not necessarily pointing to a specific person. Common in times when loneliness weighs more heavily.

variants.q: Dreaming of a hug and then the person leaves
variants.a: Often appears during a change in a relationship or after a parting. The dream uses "holding and then letting go" to play out what you haven't yet adjusted to.

variants.q: Dreaming of being held tightly
variants.a: If it feels reassuring, it may match a time when you badly need support. If you can't breathe, it may reflect a boundary being squeezed in some relationship.

hugging.ask: If the hug in your dream brings to mind a person or a matter you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
hugging.askQ: Is there still a chance for me and the person on my mind to grow closer?

faq.q: If I dream of a hug, does it mean the other person is thinking of me?
faq.a: There's a romantic saying like that in folk tradition, but a dream can't prove what someone else is thinking. Most of the time it reflects your own longing and needs.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a hug mean the relationship will get better?
faq.a: Dreams don't announce where a relationship is headed. They're closer to your hopes or worries about it. How things actually go depends on how the two of you interact in real life.

kissing.name: kissing
kissing.title: What does it mean to dream about kissing?
kissing.lead: Dreaming of a kiss is usually not a sign of a new romance. More often it reflects a recent longing for closeness, acceptance, or being understood. The person in the dream and the mood of the moment are often worth more attention than the kiss itself.
kissing.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on dreams of kissing. One group of versions links it to harmony between people and progress in a relationship, as if a relationship you care about is drawing closer. Another group cautions that if the person is a stranger or has no clear face, the traditional reading is a passing thought that may not last. Some versions go by who the person is: kissing a partner leans toward a steady relationship, while kissing a deceased relative is mostly described as longing projected into the dream. The versions differ quite a bit, so take it as one cultural way of seeing things.
kissing.plain: This dream often shows up in a few waking situations: you've just started to care about someone, there's some ambiguity between you and another person and you're afraid to confirm it, or you've been feeling lonely lately, with no one to really hold you or listen to you. It can also appear when a relationship has grown a little distant. You kiss closely in the dream, but in real life even text replies come slowly, and that gap makes this kind of dream especially likely. Another common case is that what you really want is to be affirmed, not necessarily love, and the dream simply uses a kiss to show it. After waking, ask yourself how the person in the dream made you feel: at ease, nervous, or guilty? That feeling is usually closer to your recent mood than who the person was.

variants.q: Dreaming of kissing an ex
variants.a: Common after a breakup when you haven't fully let go, or when something recently stirred up memories. Being close in the dream doesn't mean you'll get back together. It's more like something unsaid is still sitting inside you.

variants.q: Dreaming of kissing a stranger
variants.a: It may reflect a wish for something new, for being noticed, or a feeling that life has become too routine and you want some change. A vague figure usually means you're longing for a feeling, not a particular person.

variants.q: Dreaming of kissing someone you dislike
variants.a: This dream often comes when you're having friction with someone you still have to deal with closely. The dream mixes conflict and closeness, which is mostly a mental reaction to stress.

variants.q: Dreaming of being kissed and then the person walks away
variants.a: Common when you care a lot about a relationship but feel you can't get a firm grip on it. The feeling of being left behind in the dream may match the daytime anxiety of not knowing what the other person thinks.

variants.q: Dreaming of kissing in front of many people
variants.a: It may have to do with wanting to be seen while fearing being judged. If you've had an occasion lately where you had to perform in public, this dream becomes a bit more likely.

kissing.ask: If you dreamed of a specific person, or a relationship you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring some movement.
kissing.askQ: Will things move forward between him and me soon?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a kiss mean the other person likes me too?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The person in the dream is often just the one you think about most during the day, or a stand-in for a certain feeling. It reflects how much you care, but it can't be taken as evidence of how the other person feels.

faq.q: I keep dreaming of kissing. Is something wrong?
faq.a: In most cases it just means you've been craving closeness lately, or your sleep has been lighter so you remember dreams more clearly. If these dreams recur so much that you can't sleep well or your days are affected, it's worth talking to a doctor.

fighting.name: fighting
fighting.title: What does it mean to dream about fighting?
fighting.lead: Dreaming of a fight is usually connected to anger you've been holding down, a sense of competition, or conflict left unsaid. Throwing punches in a dream is often another outlet for the times you wanted to hit back in real life but held yourself in.
fighting.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give a few common readings of dreams of fighting. One reads it as quarrels with someone and a knot in your heart, a continuation of daytime friction. Another says the opposite: fighting in a dream means a matter will succeed, seeing it as putting your strength to use. Some versions go by who wins: winning leans toward momentum going your way, losing toward unresolved pressure. These readings contradict each other and each version says its own thing, so enjoy them as cultural color.
fighting.plain: This dream often appears at certain times: when you're under pressure at work and swallow your words in meetings, when something with family or a partner hasn't been talked out and looks fine on the surface but still sticks inside, or when you're competing lately for a position, a spot, or an apology. Some people have it the other way around: too restrained and accommodating by day, so it all bursts out in the dream. Who you fight and why usually says more than who wins. Fighting someone you know is mostly tension in the relationship, while fighting a stranger may be dissatisfaction with a situation. If your heart is racing when you wake, drink some water and breathe slowly. That's just your body following the dream, not a sign that anything will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of fighting with family
variants.a: Common when something at home hasn't been talked out, or you feel your opinion isn't taken seriously. The dream magnifies built-up feelings. It doesn't necessarily mean there will be conflict in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of fighting with a partner
variants.a: It may match recent communication trouble, with small things piling up into resentment. A fierce quarrel in the dream often means that in real life things are still unsaid.

variants.q: Dreaming of being beaten
variants.a: Often appears when you feel misunderstood or singled out, or the pressure is so heavy you can't fight back. This kind of dream mostly reflects feeling wronged. It isn't a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of a fight with blood
variants.a: Traditional sayings vary, and it doesn't mean you'll be hurt in real life. A more common explanation is high emotional intensity, with something in your day that you care about deeply.

variants.q: Dreaming of breaking up a fight
variants.a: It may reflect being caught between two sides lately and wanting to play peacemaker, or working hard to hold back your own impulses. This dream often comes during stretches when mediating between people is tiring.

fighting.ask: If the person or the conflict in the dream is hard to put down, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring some movement.
fighting.askQ: Will the matter between him and me get talked out?

faq.q: Does dreaming of fighting mean I'll argue with someone?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A dream is more like a vent for emotion, where anger held in by day finds a way out at night. Whether a conflict really happens depends on how you communicate in real life.

faq.q: What does it mean to win the fight in the dream?
faq.a: Some traditional versions tell it more smoothly, but in real life it more likely reflects a recent urge to stand your ground, or a new sense that you finally have something solid under you. There's no need to treat it as a preview of an outcome.

funeral.name: funeral
funeral.title: What does it mean to dream about a funeral?
funeral.lead: Dreaming of a funeral is usually tied to endings, goodbyes, or a chapter that has passed. It doesn't necessarily have anything to do with real life and death. The mood in the dream often matches something you've been letting go of lately.
funeral.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on what a funeral dream means. One group reads it as an old matter coming to a close and a change in fortune, a stage ending. Another says that taking part in a funeral procession in a dream points to something weighing on the heart, a longing or unfinished business. Some versions split it by scene: a lively funeral leans toward changes among people, a sparse one toward loneliness. Traditionally these dreams are often described in heavy terms, but in real life they don't mean anything will happen.
funeral.plain: This dream often shows up when life is changing: a new job, a move, the end of a relationship, a child leaving home, retirement, even just dropping a habit. The dream uses a funeral to act out "ending." It can also come when you miss someone or think about days you can't go back to. Some people dream it after sorting through an elder's belongings or attending a memorial service, and then it's mostly a continuation of the day's experience. The sadness in the dream is real, but it usually points to an inner goodbye, not a forecast. If dreams like this keep coming back and cost you sleep, it may help to talk to a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of your own funeral
variants.a: This often appears during big life changes, or when you're redefining yourself. Watching your own farewell in a dream is more like saying goodbye to an older version of you.

variants.q: Dreaming of a relative's funeral
variants.a: Traditionally there are various readings, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. More commonly it reflects concern about that person's health, aging, or a change in your relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of attending a stranger's funeral
variants.a: It may reflect that you're saying goodbye to some state of things lately, or thinking more about life's big questions. When the person is vague, the focus is usually the feeling of an ending.

variants.q: Dreaming of a peaceful funeral
variants.a: This is common when you've slowly come to accept that something has ended. Feeling no grief in the dream may mean the knot inside has loosened a little.

variants.q: Dreaming of rain after a funeral
variants.a: Rain in dreams is often linked to emotions being washed through. This dream tends to appear just after you've let something go, while your feelings are still settling.

funeral.ask: If the farewell or the person in the dream is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram about that matter and see which days ahead might bring movement.
funeral.askQ: Is it time for me to let that go?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a funeral unlucky?
faq.a: Some traditional versions put it in heavy terms, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. Most of the time it reflects an ending or change you're going through.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of a funeral?
faq.a: Start by thinking about whether something recently has never really come to a close. If the dreams repeat enough to affect your sleep or daytime mood, it may help to talk to a doctor.

crying.name: crying
crying.title: What does it mean to dream about crying?
crying.lead: Dreaming of crying is often not a sign of something bad, but feelings you held back during the day finding a way out at night. If you cry hard in the dream, it often just means you've built up a lot of unspoken feelings lately.
crying.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree about crying dreams. One group says that crying in a dream actually points to happy news, seeing tears as a release of pent-up frustration. Another reads it as something unresolved in the heart and feelings piling up. Some versions split it by who is crying: crying yourself leans toward releasing stress, seeing others cry toward worrying for them. These readings contradict one another, each version saying its own thing, so take them as cultural lore.
crying.plain: This dream often comes at certain times: something recently has you saying "I'm fine" while it's still stuck inside; work or home keeps you holding on with nowhere to really cry; or you've just been through a change, like a move, a breakup, or leaving a job, and your feelings haven't caught up. Some people cry in a dream after seeing someone else upset. Crying in a dream usually leaves you feeling lighter, which is the body helping you regulate. If you wake with puffy eyes or a stuffy nose, that's just the physical effect of crying. If dreams like this keep coming back and affect your sleep, it may help to talk to a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of crying hard
variants.a: Common when stress has built up and you can't find an outlet. Crying in a dream is often closer to how you really feel than pushing through during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to cry
variants.a: It may match a state where you badly want to let it out but feel you can't cry, or that crying wouldn't solve anything. This dream often appears in times of heavy responsibility.

variants.q: Dreaming of a relative crying
variants.a: Mostly it reflects worry about that person, or a sense that something in the relationship has gone unsaid. Traditionally there are various readings, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of crying until you wake
variants.a: Often appears when your emotions are full and your sleep is light. Breathing slowly and drinking some water after waking usually helps you settle.

variants.q: Dreaming of comforting someone who is crying
variants.a: It may reflect that you've often been other people's support lately, or that part of you also wants to be comforted that way. This dream often appears for caregivers.

crying.ask: If the crying or the person in the dream is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram about that matter and see which days ahead might bring movement.
crying.askQ: When will I be able to let go of what's on my mind?

faq.q: Is dreaming of crying a bad omen?
faq.a: Traditionally there are various readings, but in real life it's more often an outlet for emotions and doesn't mean anything will happen. After waking, notice whether you've been too tired lately.

faq.q: If I cry sadly in a dream, does it mean I'm repressing things?
faq.a: It could. Many people tell themselves "it's nothing" during the day, and at night the dream plays out the feelings for them. You might think about what recent matter you haven't really processed yet.

laughing.name: laughing out loud
laughing.title: What does it mean to dream about laughing out loud?
laughing.lead: Dreaming of laughing out loud is mostly about relaxing and letting out a breath. It can also mean you've been tense for a long time during the day and the dream finally gave you an outlet. Who you're laughing at, and where, often says more about how you've been lately than the laughter itself.
laughing.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree much about laughing out loud. One common version says that laughing heartily in a dream means you're in good spirits and getting along well with people. Another version cautions that laughing too wildly, or being unable to stop, may point to something in waking life that strikes you as absurd or not quite real. Some versions also treat laughing at others and being laughed at separately, with different readings. Take it as cultural reference only.
laughing.plain: Your days may be just the opposite: lately tighter, more stifling, or spent keeping up with other people's pace. Laughing out loud in a dream often shows up when pressure eases, such as when something wraps up, the weekend is near, or you finally make a decision. If the laughter felt great, you usually wake up in a good mood. If it got a bit out of control, or had some awkwardness in it, it may point to something during the day that left you not knowing whether to laugh or cry. Some people dream of laughing with friends, which is usually about missing a more easygoing relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing out loud with a group of people
variants.a: This often appears when you've been craving company and wanting to feel close to people. It may also be that you miss a relationship where you felt at ease, and the dream brought it back.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing and not being able to stop
variants.a: This dream often matches something during the day that felt absurd, frustrating, and funny all at once. Laughing out of control is more like stress finding a strange way out.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing until you cry
variants.a: This is common in times of mixed feelings, when one situation brings both joy and reluctance to let go. The dream blends the two emotions, reflecting feelings you haven't sorted out yet during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of laughing at someone
variants.a: This is usually tied to some kind of comparing during the day, or to feeling a bit dismissive about something. Laughing in the dream doesn't mean you actually want to hurt anyone in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of others laughing at me
variants.a: This often appears when you've been a bit conscious of how others see you, or afraid of being made a fool of. The dream magnifies that discomfort. In real life, no one is necessarily laughing at you.

laughing.ask: If the laughter or the person in your dream stays on your mind after waking, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
laughing.askQ: Will the matter I've been preoccupied with lately go smoothly?

faq.q: Is dreaming of laughing out loud a good omen?
faq.a: Traditional views come in different versions, and in real life a dream doesn't mean something will happen. A more practical reading is that you may have recently felt some relief, or you need to relax, and the dream had a good laugh for you first.

faq.q: Is it normal to wake up laughing from a dream?
faq.a: It's fairly common and usually relates to brain activity during certain sleep stages, so it doesn't necessarily mean anything special. If you wake up feeling good, just treat it as a light-hearted night.

screaming.name: screaming
screaming.title: What does it mean to dream about screaming? What does constant screaming in a dream stand for?
screaming.lead: Dreaming of screaming is mostly not a mysterious forecast. It usually means some feeling during the day couldn't find a way out. It might be held-in anger, hurt you couldn't put into words, or tension you've been swallowing, and in the dream it gets amplified into a scream.
screaming.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that hearing screams in a dream is read as something on your mind left unsaid, or as a hint of gossip and quarrels around you. For dreaming of yourself screaming, some versions say pent-up emotion is about to burst, while others say you're eager to be heard. The versions differ quite a bit, some focusing on relationships and some on emotions, with no single conclusion. Tradition also links making a sound with expressing oneself, but these are associations the ancients drew, not a rule.
screaming.plain: This dream often appears when there's something you haven't said during the day. Maybe you were talked over in a meeting, couldn't get through to family, or have been putting up with someone. You may also be especially worried about how others see you, afraid you'd lose control if you spoke, so the dream screams first. Another common case is stress building to a point where your body is tense and your sleep is light, so dreams get louder and more forceful. Think back: is there something lately where you had an opinion but chose silence? The part you didn't say is often the source of the scream.

variants.q: Dreaming of screaming and not being able to stop
variants.a: This is common when feelings have built up for a long time while you keep up a normal front during the day. Not being able to stop in the dream reflects a sense that there's no outlet in real life. It doesn't necessarily mean anything will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else screaming
variants.a: This may relate to the state of someone around you, where you sense something is wrong but can't help. It may also be that you're playing out your own unspoken feelings through another person.

variants.q: Dreaming of screaming but making no sound
variants.a: This "silent scream" is very common. It mostly matches the helplessness of wanting to speak but feeling it won't help, or feeling you have no voice in some setting.

variants.q: Dreaming of screaming and waking up startled
variants.a: This is often linked to lighter sleep or too many thoughts before bed. A fast heartbeat after waking is the body's reaction. Try breathing slowly to bring yourself back to the present.

variants.q: Dreaming of many people screaming together
variants.a: This may reflect being in a tense environment, such as a team, family, or class where everyone is holding things in. It may also be that you feel uneasy about some collective situation.

screaming.ask: If the scream in your dream makes you think of someone, or of something that's never been talked through, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
screaming.askQ: Is there still a chance for me and that person to talk through what's between us?

faq.q: Does dreaming of screaming mean there will be an argument?
faq.a: Some people make that association in tradition, but in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. A more practical use is to treat it as a reminder: see whether any relationship has been making you especially tense, and find a time to talk it through.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of screaming and can't sleep well?
faq.a: If it keeps recurring and affects your sleep, you can start by adjusting your bedtime routine and cutting back on stimulation. If it goes on for a good while, you can talk to a doctor to check whether stress or sleep quality is the issue.

running.name: running
running.title: What does it mean to dream about running? What does it mean to keep running in a dream?
running.lead: Dreaming of running is usually tied to a feeling of being "in a rush" or "on the run." You may have unfinished work piling up or expectations you can't keep pace with. Or something may be making you want to get away from it, and the dream shows that as running.
running.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say a few common things. Some versions read dreaming of running as "something is moving forward and you're eager to finish it." Dreaming of being chased is often said to mean unresolved pressure on your mind. Dreaming of being unable to run, or running slowly, is linked to "having strength but not being able to use it." Some versions connect running with being busy and on the move, and take it to mean a hectic life. These accounts don't fully agree with each other, which shows that people in the past also made their own associations depending on the situation. Take them as a reference only.
running.plain: This dream shows up most often when your days move fast: work is stacking up, an exam is near, something at home needs handling, or you keep chasing a standard you can't reach. Another common case is running away. There's something you don't want to face, such as an unanswered message, a decision not yet made, or a relationship you haven't dealt with, and in the dream you keep running. Some people have the opposite dream, running smoothly and lightly. That may reflect finally having a sense of direction lately, or feeling well physically. Notice whether in the dream you were being chased, hurrying somewhere, or simply enjoying the run. The feelings behind these three are quite different.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased
variants.a: Common when you've been putting something off. You know you need to face it, but you'd rather hide for now. The person chasing you isn't necessarily a bad person. It may just be the responsibility you don't want to touch.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to run, legs feeling heavy
variants.a: Mostly matches a daytime feeling of wanting to move things forward but being stuck, such as stalled progress or effort that hasn't paid off. It may also be physical tiredness showing up in your sleep.

variants.q: Dreaming of running and running but never reaching the destination
variants.a: It may reflect anxiety about a goal, a feeling that no matter how hard you try, you're still a bit short. Or you may not really be sure where the finish line is, and you're just being pushed forward.

variants.q: Dreaming of a running race
variants.a: Often linked to comparing yourself with others, feeling that people around you are measuring their progress or results against yours. Your place in the race doesn't matter much. What matters is how tense you felt while running.

variants.q: Dreaming of running easily and happily
variants.a: This dream usually matches a better state. Perhaps you've found your rhythm lately and your body is doing fine. Traditionally it's said to mean things go smoothly, but in real life, just take it as a sign you're in a good mood.

running.ask: If the running in your dream reminds you of something you've been putting off, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
running.askQ: When should I deal with the thing I've been putting off?

faq.q: Does being chased in a dream mean something bad is coming?
faq.a: Some people think so traditionally, but it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. The more common explanation is that you have pressure or something you're avoiding during the day, and the dream simply acts out that feeling.

faq.q: What if I often dream of running and wake up tired?
faq.a: Look at whether your schedule has been too full lately, or whether you're still thinking things over before bed. If this dream keeps coming back and you aren't sleeping well, you can talk to a doctor about your sleep.

swimming.name: swimming
swimming.title: What does it mean to dream about swimming? What does it mean to swim in water in a dream?
swimming.lead: Dreaming of swimming is often tied to "adjusting to a new environment." Water usually stands for emotions or your situation. How smoothly you swim and how clean the water is often reflect whether you've felt in control lately or have been barely holding on.
swimming.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say a few common things. Some versions read dreaming of swimming in water as "things are underway and you're adapting." Swimming smoothly is linked to being in good shape. Murky water and a hard swim are said to mean "obstacles in your surroundings." Some versions connect swimming with money or romance, but the books don't agree, with some stressing your circumstances and others your relationships. These are traditional ways of making associations, not a standard to judge by.
swimming.plain: This dream often comes when you enter a new environment: changing jobs, moving to a new city, starting a relationship, or taking on an unfamiliar task. The water is that environment, and swimming in it means you're trying to adapt. If the swim is easy, you may feel you've got the hang of things lately. If it's hard, or the water is cold or murky, you may be barely holding on, or feel uneasy about the mood around you. Another common case is having a lot of feelings that surround you like water, and swimming in the dream reflects you working through them. Recall the water's temperature and color and whether you could breathe. These details usually say more about how you feel than how far you swam.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming in clear water
variants.a: Often matches feeling that your surroundings are fairly simple and that you're in control. Traditionally it's said to mean things go smoothly, but in real life, take it as a sign you've felt more at ease lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming in murky or dirty water
variants.a: It may reflect unease about a certain environment or relationship, a sense that the atmosphere is cloudy and hard to see through. Or you may be in a setting that makes you uncomfortable.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming with great effort
variants.a: Common when you're pushing through, such as a workload beyond what you can handle, or emotions you haven't worked through. The effort in the dream reflects what the day has cost you.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to breathe in the water
variants.a: It may match a feeling of being unable to catch your breath or having no space of your own. This dream often comes when your schedule is too full or you're constantly being asked for things.

variants.q: Dreaming of swimming in the sea
variants.a: The sea usually stands for a bigger situation or bigger emotions. Swimming comfortably may mean you're adapting to a big change. Swimming in fear may mean the change feels beyond your control.

swimming.ask: If the water in your dream reminds you of a situation or a person, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
swimming.askQ: Will things go smoothly for me in this new environment?

faq.q: Does dreaming of swimming mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Some versions link water with money, but they vary, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more practical view is that it reflects how you've been adjusting to some environment lately.

faq.q: What if I dream I can't swim out of the water?
faq.a: Don't rush to think the worst. Look at whether something lately has made you feel stuck, with no way out. If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you aren't sleeping well, you can talk to a doctor.

drowning.name: drowning
drowning.title: What does it mean to dream about drowning?
drowning.lead: Dreaming of drowning is often tied to a feeling of being overwhelmed: too much to handle, emotions that are too full, or a situation that leaves you short of breath. It's a picture of stress, not a forecast.
drowning.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on dreams of drowning or sinking in water. One group of versions reads it as "things beyond what you can carry, an anxious mind," a sign of worrying too much. Another group looks at the state of the water: muddy water is said to point to something stuck and tiring, while clear water is described as being trapped for a while and eventually reaching shore. Some versions also link drowning to being pulled in too deeply in a relationship or among people. The versions differ, there is no single conclusion, and none of it says what will happen in real life.
drowning.plain: This dream often shows up when you feel you can't hold on much longer: work piling up, something going on at home, several people needing you at once. Choking on water and sinking may reflect a sense that your resources aren't enough, or that no one answers when you call for help. Another common case is emotions that are too full. You hold it together by day, and at night it appears as being flooded by water. If someone rescues you in the dream, it may match a quiet wish that someone would reach out a hand. If you struggle to shore on your own, it may reflect that you're not used to asking for help. All of this is a mirror of stress and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of drowning and sinking
variants.a: Common when the load feels too heavy and you can't find a way out. Sinking in the dream reflects the feeling of not being able to hold on. It doesn't mean you're in danger in real life, but it may be worth looking at whether you can carry a little less lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else drowning
variants.a: Most often it relates to someone you care about. You may sense they're not doing well, or worry that you can't help. It may also just be an impression left by something you saw during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of being rescued after drowning
variants.a: This dream often comes when you deeply wish someone would catch you. It reflects a need for support, not an omen.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to breathe in water
variants.a: It may reflect recent anxiety or your sleep quality. Being unable to breathe in a dream is often linked to tension during the day. If you also often wake with a tight chest or sleep poorly, consider talking to a doctor.

drowning.ask: If the feeling of being overwhelmed in the dream brings to mind something weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
drowning.askQ: Will there be a turning point in what's weighing on me?

faq.q: Is dreaming of drowning a bad omen?
faq.a: Some traditional versions link drowning to worrying too much and things being stuck, but that's an old association and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. A more practical reading is to ask whether you've been carrying too much lately.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of drowning?
faq.a: Start by taking stock of whether you're carrying too much at once and whether you can hand some of it off. If the dream keeps coming back and affects your sleep or leaves you anxious during the day, consider talking to a doctor.

jumping.name: jumping
jumping.title: What does it mean to dream about jumping? What does it mean to keep jumping in a dream?
jumping.lead: Dreaming of jumping is often tied to wanting to get across something or to leave. You may be weighing a decision, wanting to shake off a situation, or feeling a little nervous about whether you can make it over this step.
jumping.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several things. Some versions read jumping as wanting to break through or change the status quo. Jumping over obstacles is associated with things moving forward. Jumping down while afraid is described as hesitation in the heart. Some versions also link jumping to "leaping up," taken to mean a change in standing or circumstances. The versions differ, some leaning toward action and some toward the inner state, so take them as a reference only.
jumping.plain: This dream often appears when you face a choice: whether to change jobs, confess your feelings, or move out. Jumping means you're standing at an edge, considering whether to step off. A light, easy jump may mean you feel more sure lately. Being afraid to jump from a height, or falling and falling after you jump, may mean you still have doubts about that decision. Another common case is wanting to get out of a state, like a dull routine or a stuck relationship, and the dream uses jumping to say "I want to leave here." You can also notice where you jump to and whether you land, which usually reflects how you imagine the outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of jumping from a high place
variants.a: Often matches a riskier decision you're considering, or wanting to get out of a situation. The fear in the dream reflects not yet being sure of the outcome, not that something will go wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of jumping over obstacles
variants.a: It may reflect that you're working through a hurdle lately and feel you're almost over it. Traditionally it's said to mean progress; in real life, take it as a sign that you have some confidence in yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of jumping but being unable to fly
variants.a: Common when you badly want change but feel unable to push. Not jumping high in the dream reflects conditions or worries in real life that still hold you back.

variants.q: Dreaming of jumping nonstop
variants.a: It may match feeling restless lately, unable to settle, or switching between things all the time. It may also be that your thoughts were very active before sleep, and the dream bounced along with them.

variants.q: Dreaming of jumping and falling endlessly
variants.a: Often linked to a feeling of losing control, like having made a decision without knowing where you'll land. This dream doesn't mean anything will happen. It mostly reflects unease about the unknown.

jumping.ask: If the jumping in your dream brings to mind a decision you're considering, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.

faq.q: Does dreaming of jumping mean a promotion?
faq.a: Some circulating versions link jumping to "leaping up," but the versions differ and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more common explanation is that you want to break out of the current situation or make a decision.

faq.q: What if I'm very afraid when I jump in a dream?
faq.a: Try not to assume the worst. See whether a decision has been making you hesitate lately. If this dream keeps coming back and you're sleeping poorly, consider talking to a doctor about your sleep.

hiding.name: hiding
hiding.title: What does it mean to dream about hiding?
hiding.lead: Dreaming of hiding mostly isn't a hint that something bad is coming. It reflects wanting to avoid certain eyes or pressures lately. The act of hiding often matches a daytime feeling of not wanting to be seen or questioned.
hiding.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on hiding. One group of versions reads it as stepping out of the spotlight for now and answering movement with stillness, a reminder to keep calm first. Other versions say that staying hidden means something on your mind hasn't been spoken. Some versions also distinguish by where you hide, such as inside a house or in a dark place, each with a different saying. These are associations within traditional culture, and the versions differ widely, so take them as a reference and not a conclusion.
hiding.plain: If you're being watched while you work, chased for progress, or asked about your private life again and again during the day, dreams of hiding come easily at night. Maybe you've also been reluctant to reply in group chats, or to be called on in meetings. This dream is common in stretches when you want to keep a little space for yourself, and it doesn't have to involve any particular person. Another possibility is that you're avoiding something you need to deal with, and the dream turns it into hiding from a person or a voice. When you wake up, ask yourself: who do I least want to be seen by lately, and what do I least want to be asked? That answer is usually more useful than the dream itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding and not being found
variants.a: Common when you want to catch your breath and step out of some situation for a while. Not being found in the dream mostly reflects a wish to keep your own pace. It doesn't mean you can avoid things forever in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding and being found
variants.a: This may match the tension of being afraid of being seen through during the day, such as being underprepared or having a private worry guessed. This dream often shows up around the time you have to hand in work or explain something.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding in a closet or under the bed
variants.a: Hiding in a tight space often has to do with wanting a completely quiet corner where no one disturbs you. It may also be that you've been sleeping badly or your surroundings are too noisy, so the dream finds an enclosed spot.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding with someone else
variants.a: This mostly reflects standing on the same side as someone and facing pressure together. The person hiding with you is often someone you feel can cover for you, and you for them, in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding for a long time and not daring to come out
variants.a: This may mean you've been avoiding something for a while and feel a bit tired. Notice what keeps you from showing up. You don't have to deal with it right away. Acknowledging it is enough for now.

hiding.ask: If the person or matter you were hiding from in the dream stays on your mind, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
hiding.askQ: How will the matter I've been trying to avoid lately develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of hiding mean trouble is coming?
faq.a: Traditional dream books have all kinds of sayings, but in real life this dream more often reflects a recent mood of avoidance. It's more useful to treat it as a nudge to ask whether you need to leave yourself some space than as a forecast.

faq.q: Should I worry if I keep dreaming of hiding?
faq.a: If it only happens now and then, it mostly relates to recent stress. If the dream keeps coming back and leaves you sleeping badly or unsettled during the day, it's worth talking with a doctor, and addressing your sleep and stress themselves.

escaping.name: running away
escaping.title: What does it mean to dream about running away?
escaping.lead: Dreaming of running away usually matches a feeling during the day of wanting to get free of some pressure, such as endless tasks or a person who is hard to deal with. How hard you run in the dream often reflects how tense you've been lately.
escaping.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about running away. Some versions say that retreating is the best move, reading it as avoiding a dispute or stepping back for now. Others hold that fleeing someone who chases you means something is unfinished in your mind. Still others distinguish by who is chasing you and whether you can run. These are traditional associations, and the versions differ quite a bit, so there's no need to treat them as predictions.
escaping.plain: If deadlines chase you and messages need replies all day, dreams of fleeing come easily at night. You may also be dodging a topic that's hard to bring up, and in the dream it becomes someone chasing you. Another common version is being unable to run, which mostly has to do with physical tiredness or light sleep and isn't a hint of anything. When you wake up, ask yourself: what do I most want to shake off lately? Is it the workload, a certain relationship, or a decision that keeps being put off? Once you can name what's chasing you, the dream usually loosens its hold.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased
variants.a: The most common running-away dream. It mostly matches something that keeps pressing you during the day, or a person who stresses you out. The one chasing you often stands for the pressure that matter brings.

variants.q: Dreaming of running away but being unable to run
variants.a: This may reflect feeling powerless or tired, or a body that's tense during sleep. The dream is common after several busy days in a row and relates to not having enough energy in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of running away and escaping
variants.a: Often appears when you've just finished dealing with something troublesome and feel relieved. Getting away in the dream reflects a wish for the matter to be over.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost while running away
variants.a: This may mean you want to leave a situation but don't yet know which way to go next. The dream is common during the hesitant period around changing jobs or surroundings.

variants.q: Dreaming of running away with a friend
variants.a: This mostly reflects facing pressure together with someone and cheering each other on. It may also be that you wish someone would leave a place you dislike together with you.

escaping.ask: If what chased you in the dream is still on your mind, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
escaping.askQ: Will there be a turn for the better in the matter I've long wanted to get away from?

faq.q: Is dreaming of running away a bad omen?
faq.a: Traditional sayings vary by version, but in real life it's more often a reflection of stress. Rather than worrying about omens, look at whether something has been chasing you lately.

faq.q: Why do I keep dreaming of being chased?
faq.a: Recurring chase dreams are common when you've been under long-term pressure to meet deadlines and demands. If it's affecting your sleep, you can talk with a doctor and start from your routine and stress.

stealing.name: stealing
stealing.title: What does it mean to dream about stealing?
stealing.lead: Dreaming of stealing mostly doesn't mean you'll do something wrong. It reflects something you want but don't dare say outright, which could be resources, attention, or a little room to breathe.
stealing.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ widely on stealing. Some versions read it as having a wish, taken to mean you want something in your heart. Others say stealing with a guilty conscience means something has been weighing on you lately. Still others distinguish by what is stolen and whether you're caught. These are associations from traditional culture, and the versions say different things, so take them as reference only.
stealing.plain: If you feel you've been given fewer resources than others, or someone else took credit for your work, you may dream of stealing at night. Or you may badly want to go after an opportunity but feel awkward asking. The tension of stealing in the dream often matches the real-life feeling of being afraid someone will notice what you want. Another possibility is that you've recently done something quietly, such as preparing to leave your job without telling coworkers or privately asking around for news, and the dream turns it into a scene of stealing. When you wake up, ask yourself: what do I want lately that I haven't said out loud?

variants.q: Dreaming of stealing money
variants.a: Money often stands for resources and a sense of security. Dreaming of stealing money may reflect a feeling that you aren't getting the return you deserve, or that you've been paying extra attention to spending and income lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting caught stealing
variants.a: This usually matches a daytime fear of being seen through, such as hiding something or not being well prepared. These dreams often show up when you feel guilty or under a lot of pressure.

variants.q: Dreaming of stealing from someone else
variants.a: It may mean you envy what someone has, whether their circumstances or their position. The person you steal from in the dream is often someone you compare yourself with in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of stealing without being noticed
variants.a: This is common when you're quietly working on a plan and don't want others to know yet. Getting away with it in the dream reflects a wish to keep things low-key for now.

variants.q: Dreaming of having something stolen
variants.a: This version often has to do with feeling taken advantage of, or feeling that your effort goes unseen. You might notice whether anyone has made you feel your rights or interests were shortchanged lately.

stealing.ask: If something you want but can't bring yourself to say is still sitting on your mind, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
stealing.askQ: Will I hear news about the opportunity I've been wanting?

faq.q: Does dreaming of stealing mean there's something wrong with my character?
faq.a: No. Dreams often turn daytime longing and comparing into symbolic pictures, and this has nothing to do with whether you'd do something wrong in real life. What matters is what you've been wanting and caring about lately.

faq.q: Should I worry if I dream of being caught stealing?
faq.a: Traditional dream books differ on this. In real life, it more often reflects guilt or the tension of fearing you'll be seen through. If you really are hiding something right now, dealing with it will help more than worrying about the dream.

lying.name: Lying
lying.title: What does it mean to dream about lying?
lying.lead: Dreaming of lying often reflects a daytime situation where some things are hard to say and you can only soften them, or something you haven't yet been honest about. The person you lie to in the dream is often someone you find hard to face in real life.
lying.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about lying. Some versions read it as a matter of gossip or quarrels and a reminder to watch your words. Others say lying in a dream means something is left unsaid in your heart. Still others give different readings depending on whether the lie is exposed. These are traditional associations, they vary widely between versions, and they needn't be taken literally.
lying.plain: If your days are full of polite talk and sharing only the good news, you may dream of lying at night. You might also be keeping something back lately, or have promised something you can't deliver, and it weighs on you. The tension after lying in the dream often matches the real-life feeling of dreading follow-up questions. Another possibility is that you aren't being honest with yourself, such as saying you're fine when you're tired. After waking, you could ask: which sentence did I say most guiltily lately? What's behind it is usually something you truly care about.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lie being exposed
variants.a: This usually matches a daytime fear of being seen through, such as being underprepared or leaving something unsaid. These dreams often come around the time you have to explain something or report on progress.

variants.q: Dreaming of lying to family
variants.a: Family often stands for the people hardest to answer to. This dream may reflect something you're keeping from home, or sharing only good news so your family won't worry.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone lying to you
variants.a: It may mean you've had some doubts about what a certain person says, or feel that information isn't transparent enough. Being deceived in a dream often matches uncertainty in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of lying very naturally
variants.a: This is common when you're in situations that call for polished wording, such as social obligations or negotiations. Lying smoothly in the dream shows you've grown used to a certain way of speaking, which isn't necessarily a bad thing.

variants.q: Dreaming of wanting to tell the truth but being unable to
variants.a: It may reflect something you want to say but are held back by timing or courage. This dream is common when there's friction in a relationship and you haven't found a chance to talk it through.

lying.ask: If the truth you couldn't say in the dream is still on your mind, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
lying.askQ: Will I get a chance to talk through what's been left unsaid between me and that person?

faq.q: Does dreaming of lying mean I'll be deceived?
faq.a: Traditional dream books offer various readings, but in real life this dream more often reflects your own awkwardness and softening of the truth. It's more practical to take it as a nudge to ask which sentence you said most guiltily lately.

faq.q: Is it a concern to dream that I keep lying?
faq.a: An occasional dream like this is usually tied to recent social pressure. If it keeps coming back and you wake up uneasy, you can talk with a doctor about your sleep and stress, and there's no need to frighten yourself.

apologizing.name: Apologizing
apologizing.title: What does it mean to dream about apologizing?
apologizing.lead: Dreaming of apologizing often reflects something you haven't let go of, or a knot in a relationship that you care about. It may also be a wish to be forgiven or to make peace. It's your feelings sorting themselves out, and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.
apologizing.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ on apologizing. Some versions read it as guilt and a wish to make amends. Others say an apology symbolizes a relationship being mended. Still others see apologizing in a dream as a reminder to talk things through. The versions disagree, so it's best treated as a cultural reference.
apologizing.plain: If you've had friction with someone that hasn't been talked through, or feel you haven't done well enough somewhere, you may dream of apologizing at night. Common feelings are self-blame, regret and wanting to be understood. You may also be waiting for the other person to bend first while finding it hard to let go. Whether the other person accepts your apology in the dream often matches whether you feel the relationship still has room to turn around. These dreams tend to come when a relationship is strained or old matters come to mind, and they don't mean real life will play out the same way.

variants.q: Dreaming of apologizing to family
variants.a: This is often tied to something unsaid at home. You may feel you haven't been dutiful enough, or that you spoke too harshly. The dream reflects what's on your mind. It doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of an apology being rejected
variants.a: You may be worried about not being forgiven, or feel a relationship is stuck. This feeling mostly comes from unease during the day. It isn't a preview of an outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone apologizing to you
