variants.a: This often matches waiting inside for a certain word, or hoping the other person will back down first. It may help to ask yourself what you really want.

variants.q: Dreaming of apologizing over and over
variants.a: You may be afraid of making mistakes lately, and used to admitting fault first. Notice whether you're taking too much responsibility onto yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of making up after an apology
variants.a: This mostly reflects how much you want to mend the relationship, and part of you is already looking for a way back. Reconciliation in a dream is an outlet for your feelings, not a promise.

apologizing.ask: If the person you apologized to in the dream stays on your mind, or there's something you've never said, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead might bring movement.
apologizing.askQ: Is there still room for things to turn around between that person and me?

faq.q: Does dreaming about an apology mean I did something wrong?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Dreams often reflect what you care about or regret. They don't mean you really did something wrong, and there's no need to keep blaming yourself.

faq.q: What if I feel heavy after dreaming about an apology?
faq.a: Start by looking at whether something during the day left you feeling in debt to someone, or left something unsaid. If you can say it, find a chance to. If not, write it down for now. If the dream keeps coming back and you're sleeping poorly, consider talking to a doctor.

quarreling.name: Arguing
quarreling.title: What does it mean to dream about arguing?
quarreling.lead: Dreaming of an argument usually isn't a sign that you're about to fall out with someone. More often it reflects a feeling you haven't let out, or a relationship that has you tense lately. Don't rush to match it to a person. Look at whether you've been holding something back during the day.
quarreling.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that quarreling with someone in a dream stands for gossip and friction between people. Some versions say that being cursed at means trouble from words, while others say the opposite: making up after a quarrel means the relationship will become clearer. Still other versions read a dream argument as an unresolved matter, with you pulled between two sides. The versions differ and even contradict each other, so take them as cultural interest and don't take them too seriously.
quarreling.plain: This dream often shows up when you're holding your feelings down during the day. You may have an opinion you haven't voiced to a coworker or family member, or you may be arguing with yourself, part of you wanting to hold back and part wanting to burst. Often you were still replaying how to answer a certain remark before bed, or worrying that conflict would damage a relationship. A fierce fight in the dream usually means you care a lot about that relationship but can't find an outlet. Notice what has made you unusually careful with your words lately, or makes your stomach tighten when you think of it. That is usually where the dream comes from.

variants.q: Dreaming of arguing with family
variants.a: Family often stands for the closest relationships, and the hardest to avoid. This dream may reflect something at home you haven't said, or a fear that saying it would hurt feelings. There are usually small frictions like that during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of arguing with a stranger
variants.a: A stranger is often a projection of some part of yourself. An argument that makes no sense may match a vague irritation during the day, or some occasion or rule you don't quite accept.

variants.q: Dreaming of making up after an argument
variants.a: This dream is common when you actually hope to repair a relationship but haven't found a way to step down. Making up in the dream is more like a wish of yours. It doesn't mean things will improve on their own.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scolded
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been demanding a lot of yourself lately and fear being rejected, or that you really were criticized during the day. The feeling of being scolded in a dream is often linked to self-criticism.

quarreling.ask: If the person or matter in the dream stays on your mind, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead might bring movement.
quarreling.askQ: Is there still a chance of resolving the knot between that person and me?

faq.q: Does dreaming of arguing mean I'm going to fall out with someone?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Dreams more often reflect your daytime feelings and what you care about. They aren't a preview. Rather than worry, think about which relationship has made you especially careful with your words lately. That's the clue.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming about arguing?
faq.a: First notice whether some feeling has had no outlet during the day. Try writing it down or talking with someone you trust. If these dreams keep coming back and affect your sleep, consider talking to a doctor.

eating.name: Eating
eating.title: What does it mean to dream about eating?
eating.lead: Dreaming of eating usually relates to what you're lacking or wanting lately. You may really be hungry, or you may want to be cared for and satisfied. It reflects your current state more than it previews anything.
eating.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several things. Some versions say dreaming of food and drink stands for good fortune at the table and social contact, others say eating symbolizes that your daily needs will be looked after, and some read being unable to eat as something weighing on your mind. The versions differ a lot on eating, some leaning material, some leaning toward human relationships, so take them as cultural reference only.
eating.plain: This dream is common when you've been too busy to eat properly during the day, or are craving comfort lately. You may also be in a stretch that calls for recharging, such as heavy work or long stretches of caring for others, and part of you wants someone to care for you too. What you eat, who you eat with, and whether you enjoy it often match how you feel about fulfillment lately. Eating with relish may mean you're more relaxed. Being unable to eat, or not getting any, may reflect a sense of too little resources or attention.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating a lot
variants.a: It may reflect a special need for compensation lately, or a desire you held down during the day. It could also be an irregular routine and real hunger, and eating too much before bed can bring this kind of dream too.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to eat
variants.a: Common when something is on your mind and your appetite is blocked by emotion. It isn't necessarily about your body. It's more that you feel unmotivated about something, or can't swallow it.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating a meal with other people
variants.a: Eating together often stands for connection and exchange. A dream like this may reflect a wish for a closer relationship, or a recent gathering or dinner that has stayed on your mind.

variants.q: Dreaming of spoiled or bad-tasting food
variants.a: It may point to an expectation that fell through, or an arrangement that doesn't quite sit right with you. Look at whether there's something during the day that you've been going along with reluctantly.

eating.ask: If the meal or the person in your dream is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
eating.askQ: Where is the sense of fulfillment I've been missing going to come from?

faq.q: Does dreaming of eating mean good luck is coming?
faq.a: Folk sayings come in many versions, but a dream is not a forecast. A more practical view is that it often reflects your recent appetite, your routine, or a wish to feel satisfied inside.

faq.q: Should I worry about dreaming of eating?
faq.a: Usually not. You might notice whether you've been too busy to eat properly, or whether you've been longing for company lately. If dreams like this keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, it's worth talking with a doctor.

drinking.name: Drinking water
drinking.title: What does it mean to dream about drinking water?
drinking.lead: Dreaming of drinking water often has to do with thirst and whether you have enough. Your body may really be short on water, or you may feel some kind of support is lacking. It's more a nudge to notice what you need right now than a prediction.
drinking.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree. Some versions treat drinking water as a sign of a steady life and needs being met. Others say drinking clear water means a clear mind, and some read being unable to find water to drink as inner longing. The versions differ a lot, even contradict each other, so enjoy them as cultural curiosities.
drinking.plain: This dream often shows up when you've drunk little water during the day, have a dry mouth, or were especially thirsty before bed. Physical sensations slip straight into dreams. Psychologically, drinking water often stands for replenishing: you may have been giving a lot and been needed for a long time, and part of you wants some nourishment and support. How easily you drink in the dream, and how clean the water is, often mirrors whether you feel you have enough resources and are being well cared for.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to get water to drink
variants.a: It may reflect a need that feels unmet lately, or a situation that's stuck and leaves you feeling powerless. It could also be that you really drank too little during the day, and your body is reminding you.

variants.q: Dreaming of drinking dirty water
variants.a: It often relates to feeling uneasy or uncertain about some environment or relationship. Look at whether there's something during the day that you've accepted reluctantly and can't quite get past.

variants.q: Dreaming of drinking and drinking but still being thirsty
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that nothing you do to recharge is enough, common when you give a lot and feel drained. It could also be hot weather or salty food making you truly thirsty.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone giving you water to drink
variants.a: This dream often comes when you long to be cared for and supported, or when someone has recently helped you out and it has stayed with you.

drinking.ask: If the glass of water or the person in your dream is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
drinking.askQ: Where is the support I've been feeling I don't have enough of?

faq.q: Does dreaming of drinking water mean something is wrong with my body?
faq.a: A dream can't be used to judge your health. More often it's simply that you drank little water during the day, have a dry mouth, or were very thirsty before bed. If you really feel unwell, do see a doctor.

faq.q: What feeling is behind dreaming of drinking water?
faq.a: It often relates to craving and replenishing. You may have been giving a lot and want to be looked after, or you may just be thirsty. More practically, notice whether you've been getting enough rest lately.

vomiting.name: Vomiting
vomiting.title: What does it mean to dream about vomiting?
vomiting.lead: Dreaming of vomiting often has to do with wanting to get something out or be rid of it. Something during the day may have turned your stomach or been uncomfortable to hold in, or your stomach may really be upset. It reflects the load you're carrying right now more than it predicts anything.
vomiting.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say a few different things. Some versions read vomiting as getting rid of something bad, so that inner knots loosen. Others say it means your body or emotions need clearing out. The versions vary, some leaning positive and some more of a reminder, so take them as cultural lore. They don't mean anything will happen in real life.
vomiting.plain: This dream often appears when you've been swallowing something reluctantly during the day: resentment, pressure, a task you didn't want, or a relationship that makes you uncomfortable but that you can't talk about. Physically, overeating, an upset stomach, or a greasy meal before bed can also bring it on. How you feel after vomiting in the dream matters. Feeling relieved may mean you actually want to let something go, while feeling miserable may reflect a sense that you can't get rid of it and it's stuck.

variants.q: Dreaming of vomiting again and again
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been carrying too much lately and want to get rid of it but can't finish. Your stomach may also really be upset, so notice what you've eaten and whether you've slept enough.

variants.q: Dreaming of vomiting on someone
variants.a: It often relates to worry that your emotions or troubles will spill onto others, or to guilt in some relationship. Look at whether there's something during the day you want to apologize for or explain.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else vomiting
variants.a: It may reflect that someone near you is releasing emotions and you're watching, unsure how to respond. It could also be that you feel uneasy about some setting.

variants.q: Dreaming of feeling good after vomiting
variants.a: This dream is common when you really want to talk something out and put it down. The relief after vomiting is more a wish inside you, and doesn't mean things will resolve on their own.

vomiting.ask: If the thing that turned your stomach in the dream is still hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
vomiting.askQ: How do I let go of something I can't swallow?

faq.q: Does dreaming about vomiting mean I'm sick?
faq.a: A dream can't tell you anything about your health. Some traditional sayings treat it as getting rid of something bad, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. If your body really feels unwell, ask a doctor.

faq.q: What feelings does dreaming about vomiting point to?
faq.a: It's often linked to forcing something down and wanting to get it out. It could be feeling wronged, under pressure, or sick of something. Notice whether there's something you've been holding back from saying lately.

bleeding.name: bleeding
bleeding.title: What does it mean to dream about bleeding?
bleeding.lead: Dreaming about bleeding is often tied to feelings of being drained, losing something, or getting hurt. You may have felt worn out lately, or something you saw or heard during the day may have stuck with you. It's more a reflection of how you're doing right now than a forecast.
bleeding.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree. Some versions read seeing blood as a flow of money or energy. Others say bleeding stands for giving of yourself or releasing emotion, and some read bleeding that won't stop as worry in the heart. The versions differ a lot, even contradict each other, so take them as cultural curiosity. In real life, they don't mean anything will happen.
bleeding.plain: This dream often shows up when you've been feeling tired or used up. Work may be draining you, you may have been caring for others for a long time, or a relationship may feel like constant giving. It could also come from seeing images of injury or medical care during the day, or from a real wound or your period working its way into the dream. How much blood there is, and whether it stops, often matches whether you feel you have enough strength and are being well supported.

variants.q: Dreaming of bleeding that won't stop
variants.a: It may reflect a sense that something keeps draining you and you feel a bit panicked. Look at whether something has been dragging on lately, leaving you feeling your energy keeps leaking away.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else bleeding
variants.a: This often matches worry about the people around you, or feelings of tenderness or guilt about a relationship. It may also be an impression left by something you saw during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of being hurt and bleeding
variants.a: It may reflect feeling hurt lately without anyone noticing. This kind of dream often comes with feeling wronged or misunderstood.

variants.q: Dreaming of just a little blood, or wiping it away
variants.a: This is common when you feel things are still manageable, or when you're trying to deal with a small wound. It may also just be a minor cut or your period showing up in the dream.

bleeding.ask: If the wound in your dream, or the person in it, is hard to let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which coming days may bring movement.
bleeding.askQ: How can I get back the energy I've lost lately?

faq.q: Is dreaming about bleeding unlucky?
faq.a: The sayings come in many versions, but a dream is not a forecast. A more practical view is that it often reflects feeling tired or drained lately, or images you saw during the day.

faq.q: Should I worry about dreaming of bleeding?
faq.a: Usually not. Notice whether you're overtired or giving too much, or whether you happen to have a wound or your period. If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you're not sleeping well, talk to a doctor.

hair-loss.name: hair falling out
hair-loss.title: What does it mean to dream about hair falling out? Common sayings and psychological clues
hair-loss.lead: Dreaming about hair falling out is mostly linked to fear of losing something, a change in image, or built-up stress. Traditional dream readings vary, but in real life it usually isn't a forecast. It reflects what's been on your mind lately.
hair-loss.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say roughly three things. One links hair loss to worry and overwork, a sign of something on your mind and too much thinking. Another looks at body and appearance, saying it may relate to recent tiredness or low energy. A few versions read it as the old falling away and the new arriving, leaning toward change. The versions don't agree: some stress emotions, some the body, and some contradict each other. So treat them only as cultural reference, not a verdict.
hair-loss.plain: If you've been paying attention to your hair or looks during the day, dreaming of hair falling out at night is very common. Something lately may also be making you feel you can't hold on: a relationship fading, an unsteady position at work, not enough time. That sense of loss easily turns into hair falling out strand by strand. Another common case is heavy stress and poor sleep, which makes dreams fragmented and repetitive. If you're tense about your image, your age, or a health checkup, the dream may simply continue your daytime thoughts. It's worth noticing how you feel on waking, anxious, calm, or relieved. That often says more about what matters to you now than the dream itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of a big clump of hair falling out
variants.a: This often appears in periods of concentrated stress, such as juggling work and family at once. A dramatic image doesn't mean anything will really happen. Mostly your mind is magnifying a feeling of not being able to hold up.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone combing my hair as it falls out
variants.a: It may relate to being cared for or being judged. You might be concerned about how an elder or coworker sees you, and in the dream it becomes someone touching your hair.

variants.q: Dreaming of hair falling out without going bald
variants.a: This dream is common in the stage of worrying but not yet having really lost anything, such as fearing things will go wrong or a relationship will change. It reminds you of what you care about more than it points to any outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of hair falling out while washing it
variants.a: Everyday actions showing up in dreams is very common, and usually ties to recent habits or physical sensations. If you really do notice hair loss during the day, it's not odd for the thought to carry into your dream.

hair-loss.ask: If you dreamed of a particular person, or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which coming days may bring movement.
hair-loss.askQ: How will the thing I've been worrying about develop?

faq.q: Does dreaming about hair falling out mean something is wrong with my body?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link hair loss to overwork, but a dream can't reflect test results. If you really are concerned about your hair or health during the day, seeing a doctor or getting checked is far more useful than interpreting a dream.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming about hair falling out?
faq.a: First see whether you've been sleeping little or under a lot of stress. If these dreams keep recurring and affect your sleep and mood, talk to a doctor, and take the chance to sort out what's been weighing on you during the day.

hair-cutting.name: cutting hair
hair-cutting.title: What does it mean to dream about cutting hair? Common beliefs and psychological readings
hair-cutting.lead: Dreaming about cutting hair is often linked to wanting a new look or wanting to cut something off. Traditional dream lore says many things, but in waking life this dream is more like your mind tidying itself up, not a forecast.
hair-cutting.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree about haircuts. Some read cutting hair as shedding worries and starting over, leaning toward sorting things out and saying goodbye. Others start from the idea that hair and skin come from your parents, and say a haircut points to tension with family or old relationships. Some versions tie it to money or changes among people around you. The same image can mean opposite things in different versions, so treat it as cultural reference, not a conclusion.
hair-cutting.plain: A haircut is already a deliberate change in waking life, so this dream often shows up when you're thinking about changing jobs, changing your look, ending a relationship, or dropping a habit. Who does the cutting and whether you wanted it makes a big difference. Cutting your own hair usually relates to taking charge; having someone else cut it may reflect feeling that things are being arranged or decided for you. If you feel light afterward, you probably look forward to the change. If you regret it, you may still be unsure about a decision.

variants.q: Dreaming of cutting your own hair
variants.a: Common when you want to take back control or tidy up your life. The image of doing it yourself usually matches a decision you're making for yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else cutting your hair
variants.a: It may reflect feeling that something is out of your hands, or being arranged by others. It may also mean you care a lot about someone's opinion.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bad haircut or hair cut too short
variants.a: Often appears when you've made a decision and then start doubting it, worried there's no going back. Traditional versions differ, and in waking life it doesn't mean something will go wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of cutting someone else's hair
variants.a: It may relate to a change in your relationship with that person, such as wanting more distance, or feeling that you're influencing them.

variants.q: Dreaming of being happy with the haircut
variants.a: This dream often comes when your mood is improving. It suggests you look forward to coming changes and are more comfortable with the new you.

hair-cutting.ask: If the person whose hair you cut in the dream is someone specific, or you're stuck on a decision about whether to change, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.

faq.q: Does dreaming of cutting hair mean losing money?
faq.a: That's what some versions say, but the versions don't agree and there's no link in waking life. Rather than worry, see whether a recent expense or decision has been on your mind.

faq.q: Does dreaming of cutting hair have to do with love?
faq.a: Some people have this dream around a change in a relationship, because cutting hair symbolizes saying goodbye and starting over. But it reflects how you feel, not how the relationship will end.

blind.name: blindness
blind.title: What does it mean to dream about going blind? Common readings and clues from your daytime mood
blind.lead: Dreaming of going blind is often linked to not seeing the way forward, fearing being kept in the dark, or feeling unsure about something. Traditional views vary, and in waking life it's usually not a warning about your body but a reflection of recent helplessness.
blind.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree about blindness. Some versions link it to not seeing a situation clearly, a sign of doubt or unclear judgment. Others read it as losing something to rely on, perhaps worry about losing a person or thing. A few read it the other way: not seeing means being undisturbed by the outside world and able to focus inward. These views differ widely, some leaning negative and some neutral, with no single conclusion, so take them as cultural reference only.
blind.plain: Not being able to see in a dream most often matches something in daytime life that leaves you unable to get your bearings: not sure what someone feels, whether work will change, or whether your choice is right. Eyes in dreams often stand for judgment and direction, so an image of blindness tends to appear when you have to decide with too little information. Another common case is feeling overlooked or misunderstood lately, as if others can't see you, and the dream flips that feeling into you not being able to see. Some people also have this dream when they're tired or have strained their eyes. After waking, ask yourself: what is something lately that you've wanted to see clearly but couldn't?

variants.q: Dreaming of suddenly not being able to see
variants.a: Common when things suddenly become uncertain, such as plans being disrupted or news arriving abruptly. A sudden image often matches a change you aren't ready to face yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of gradually going blind
variants.a: It may relate to helplessness that has built up over time, such as a relationship or job that leaves you less and less sure. A gradual change often reflects something you've noticed but haven't dealt with yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else being blind
variants.a: It may relate to wanting to be understood, or wanting to help someone see their situation. It may also be that you feel someone never sees what you put in.

variants.q: Dreaming of feeling your way in the dark
variants.a: This dream is common when you're making a choice. If the direction isn't set, images of groping along come naturally. It's more of a process than a conclusion.

blind.ask: If you dreamed about a specific person, or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
blind.askQ: Will the thing I can't see clearly right now become clear?

faq.q: Does dreaming of going blind mean something is wrong with my eyes?
faq.a: Dreams don't reflect test results. Traditional views mostly read this as not seeing clearly in a psychological sense, not a warning about your body. If your eyes truly feel unwell during the day, it's more practical to see a doctor directly.

faq.q: Does dreaming of not being able to see mean my luck has been bad lately?
faq.a: I wouldn't connect them. This kind of dream more often comes when information is lacking and direction is unsettled. It reflects your uncertainty and has no direct link to good or bad luck.

deaf.name: deafness
deaf.title: What does it mean to dream about going deaf? Dreams of not hearing and the distance inside
deaf.lead: Dreaming of being deaf often has to do with not hearing what you want to hear, feeling ignored, or wanting to shut out the noise around you. Traditional readings vary, and in waking life it mostly reflects how communication has been going for you lately.
deaf.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't say much about deafness, and what they do say is split. One strand links it to news not getting through, a sign that communication with someone is strained or that something has gone unsaid. Another reads it as "not wanting to listen", saying it may mean you're trying to avoid certain voices or advice. Some versions read it as a reminder to listen more and speak less. These accounts come from different sources and don't agree with each other, so take them as one cultural way of looking at the dream.
deaf.plain: In dreams, ears often relate to receiving messages and hearing what others say. Dreaming that you can't hear is common when someone's words have been hard to take in lately, or when you've spoken and no one has answered. It can also mean you want to switch off outside noise: family opinions, a coworker's complaints, too many voices on social media, and a need for quiet. Another common case is that there's something unsaid between you and another person. You hold it in during the day, and at night the dream plays it out as not being able to hear. Sometimes it's simply a dream that comes when you're physically tired or your ears or head feel uncomfortable. It helps to notice whether in the dream you wanted to hear and couldn't, or didn't want to hear at all. The two feelings point to different moods.

variants.q: Dreaming of suddenly not being able to hear
variants.a: This often comes when communication suddenly breaks off, such as a cold silence after an argument or a message left on read. The sudden image usually points to feelings you haven't worked through yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of being deaf without anyone knowing
variants.a: It may relate to the feeling of suffering in silence. You may feel your situation hasn't been seen lately, and in the dream that becomes others not knowing you can't hear.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to hear a certain person's voice
variants.a: This is common when there's distance between you and someone, whether you've drifted apart or you want to avoid them for a while. The dream makes that distance concrete as not being able to hear.

variants.q: Dreaming that others can't hear me speak
variants.a: It may reflect feeling that your opinions aren't being taken up or that your effort goes unanswered. This kind of dream often shows up during periods when you need to keep communicating but it only goes so far.

deaf.ask: If your dream was about a particular person, or about something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
deaf.askQ: Will there be progress on what's been left unsaid between that person and me?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being deaf mean something will go wrong with my ears?
faq.a: A dream isn't a preview of your body. Traditional accounts mostly read it as being unable to take something in, in communication or mood, not as a health verdict. If your ears really are bothering you during the day, it's better to see a doctor.

faq.q: Is dreaming of not being able to hear related to how people see me?
faq.a: I wouldn't think of it in terms of good or bad luck. This kind of dream more often reflects how communication has been going lately, such as feeling ignored or wanting some quiet for a while. It has no direct link to how others view you.

broken-bone.name: broken bone
broken-bone.title: What does it mean to dream about a broken bone? The feeling of not holding up, in traditional views
broken-bone.lead: Dreaming of a broken bone often has to do with feeling you can't hold up, feeling stuck, or something suddenly stopping. Traditional dream books offer several readings. In waking life it's usually not a warning of an accident but a reflection of the load you've been carrying.
broken-bone.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) are not consistent about dreams of broken bones. One strand links it to a support giving way, a sign that something you rely on or have arranged in life has hit trouble. Another reads it as blocked action, saying it may mean something you want to do is stuck or progress has stalled. Some versions read it as a reminder to slow down and not push through. These accounts come from different sources and have different tones, with no single conclusion. Take them as cultural reference, not as a verdict on the future.
broken-bone.plain: Bones in dreams often stand for support and structure, so an image of a broken bone is common when something that holds your life up feels loose: your work rhythm has been disrupted, there's something at home to carry, or a relationship has suddenly changed. It may also be that you've been pushing too hard and your body is telling you to rest, with the dream using bones to say so. Another common case is that something is stuck halfway, such as a delayed plan or an application with no reply, and that feeling of standstill becomes an image of being unable to move. Some people have this dream after seeing someone else get hurt, or after really twisting something themselves. When you wake, you can ask yourself which matter lately makes you feel that carrying on is getting hard.

variants.q: Dreaming of breaking my own bone
variants.a: This often appears during heavier stretches, such as looking after both work and family at once. A vivid image doesn't mean anything will happen. Usually the mind is simply magnifying the feeling of not holding up.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else breaking a bone
variants.a: It may relate to your concern for someone, such as worrying that a family member is too tired or a coworker can't hold up. It may also be that you feel the support in some relationship has loosened.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken bone that doesn't hurt much
variants.a: This kind of dream is common at a stage when you've noticed a problem but haven't really felt its impact yet. It's more of a nudge to pay attention than an outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bone breaking and being set back together
variants.a: It may reflect that you're mending something, such as clearing up a misunderstanding or catching up on progress. The image of it being put back often shows a wish to return things to how they were.

broken-bone.ask: If your dream was about a particular person, or about something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
broken-bone.askQ: The thing I'm pushing through right now: will it ease up in the coming time?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a broken bone mean something bad will happen?
faq.a: Some traditional accounts link a broken bone to a support giving way, but that is a symbolic reading, not a warning. In waking life it more often reflects the load you've been under and a sense of being stuck.

faq.q: After dreaming of a broken bone, should I rest?
faq.a: A dream can't give medical advice. But if you've really been feeling tired, sleeping poorly, or have physical discomfort, talking with a doctor and arranging some rest is more practical than interpreting dreams.

wound.name: wound
wound.title: What does it mean to dream about a wound?
wound.lead: Dreaming of a wound can leave you feeling uneasy when you wake. This kind of dream mostly reflects how you've been feeling about being hurt or vulnerable, and doesn't necessarily mean anything will go wrong in real life.
wound.trad: A common reading in the folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) is that dreaming of a wound may symbolize friction in relationships or hurt feelings you haven't dealt with. Some versions see a wound as something healing, a reminder to take better care of yourself. The versions differ quite a bit, some stressing conflict and some stressing recovery, with no single conclusion.
wound.plain: If you've just had an argument, been misunderstood, or been especially bothered by something someone said, you may easily dream of a wound at night. It can also come while you're recovering from a setback, still carrying a bit of pain but slowly getting better. The wound's location, size, and whether it bleeds often match what's on your mind. A hurt hand, for example, may relate to something you did, while a wound over the heart ties more to emotional bonds. It's more a mirror of your mood than a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bleeding wound
variants.a: Bleeding in dreams often relates to energy draining away or emotions being released. You may be tired lately, or some feelings held in for a long time may need an outlet. Notice whether you're giving too much, and rest when you can.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else getting hurt
variants.a: It may reflect worry about that person, or a feeling that you can't help. It can also mean you're projecting a part of yourself onto them. Ask yourself whether you've been overlooking your own needs lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a wound healing
variants.a: This is usually tied to a feeling of recovery: a knot inside you is loosening, or you're ready to move forward. The healing in the dream often matches how much you've let go of something in waking life.

variants.q: Dreaming of being hurt but feeling no pain
variants.a: Feeling no pain may mean you've gone numb about something, or are deliberately not feeling it. You may also be using reason to keep your emotions at a distance. Think about whether there's something lately you'd rather not face.

wound.ask: If the wound in your dream reminds you of a person or a matter you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
wound.askQ: Is the wound from that matter still hurting me?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a wound mean something is wrong with my body?
faq.a: A dream is not a medical exam and can't be used as a sign of illness. But if wound dreams keep coming back, or you still feel quite unwell after waking, it's fine to talk with a doctor, and to notice the stress in your life lately too.

faq.q: Is dreaming of a wound related to my relationships?
faq.a: It could be. Wounds often stand for friction or loss in a relationship, especially if something has felt unsettled since you last dealt with someone. The dream is just a nudge to take your feelings seriously. It doesn't mean the relationship will break.

scar.name: scar
scar.title: What does it mean to dream about a scar?
scar.lead: Dreaming of a scar usually has to do with something that's over but has left a mark. It doesn't necessarily mean you haven't healed. It's more like you're looking back at that experience and weighing how much it still matters to you now.
scar.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about scars. Some read an old mark as something that's past and can be put down; others read it as an old matter that may be raised again. Some also link a scar on the face or on the hand to reputation or to one's work. These are traditional associations, and versions often contradict each other. They don't mean anything will happen in real life.
scar.plain: A scar in a dream often matches the feeling of "I remember, but it doesn't hurt as much." During the day you may have passed a certain place, seen a photo, or heard someone mention the past, and that memory came back up. Or you may be making a decision, and past experience is what you're weighing it against. Often, people who dream of scars are less concerned with the wound itself than with whether they've really come through. Sometimes this dream even shows up when you're becoming steadier, as if to confirm that the mark is still there, but you're different now.

variants.q: Dreaming of a scar on your face
variants.a: The face is often linked to how others see me. This dream may come when you're thinking about your image or fear being judged. Traditions say various things about it, but none of them mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of your scar being seen
variants.a: This often reflects hesitation over whether to talk about a part of your past. You may be wondering whether to let someone know you better, or worrying about how they'd see you once they know.

variants.q: Dreaming of a scar disappearing
variants.a: This dream often comes with a feeling of finally being able to breathe out. It may mean something matters to you less than it did, or that you're starting to see it more evenly.

variants.q: Dreaming of many scars
variants.a: It may match a recent look back over a longer stretch of time, remembering a lot. That isn't necessarily bad. Sometimes it's a time of sorting things out, like going through an old drawer piece by piece.

scar.ask: If the scar in your dream reminds you of a stretch of your past or a certain person, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
scar.askQ: Will that part of my past still affect me now?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a scar mean something isn't resolved yet?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A scar in a dream is often a marker of memory and doesn't mean something is wrong with you now. What's more worth noticing is how you feel about that past after waking: calm, or pulled back into it.

faq.q: Why was the scar in my dream someone else's?
faq.a: You may feel for what that person has been through, or you're carrying their situation in your mind. Think about whether someone's story has touched you especially lately.

tattoo.name: tattoo
tattoo.title: What does it mean to dream about a tattoo?
tattoo.lead: Dreaming of a tattoo often has to do with wanting to leave a mark, or wanting to be seen a certain way. It may reflect a decision you're making about identity or image, or simply a version of yourself you badly want to express but haven't yet.
tattoo.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ quite a bit on tattoos. One group reads a mark on the body as a change in identity or relationships; another reads it as a call to be careful about impulsive decisions. Some versions go by the design, with animals and flowers each carrying their own associations. These are traditional associations, and versions often contradict each other. They don't mean anything will happen in real life.
tattoo.plain: A tattoo in a dream often stands for something I chose, and it stays. During the day you may be stuck on whether to make a decision: change jobs, make something public, or take a stand with someone. Or you may care a lot about how others define you and want to shake off a label. Often you remember the design clearly and wonder on waking what it means, and that usually relates to who you want to become. Another common version is a tattoo that hurts or that you regret, which may match some unease about a decision you've already made.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting a tattoo
variants.a: This often appears when you're considering a choice that will last. You may want a mark that's your own, or want to announce something to others. Traditional readings vary, and none mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else's tattoo
variants.a: It may reflect that you've noticed a change in someone, or that you're watching how others define themselves. You can also ask what about that person especially catches your attention.

variants.q: Dreaming of regretting a tattoo
variants.a: This dream often comes with the feeling of having decided but still being a little shaky. It doesn't necessarily mean you chose wrong. It's more like you're double-checking whether you really want this.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tattoo design
variants.a: Images are often clues to a feeling. An animal, a word, or a flower each carries your own associations. Ask yourself: when you saw that image, who or what was the first thing that came to mind?

tattoo.ask: If the tattoo in your dream reminds you of a decision or a certain person, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which coming days might bring movement.
tattoo.askQ: Should I say this out loud?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a tattoo mean I want to change something?
faq.a: Possibly. In dreams, a tattoo is often tied to "leaving a mark." It may reflect a wish for a fresh start lately, or a wish for something to be seen. But this is only an association. It doesn't mean you have to act.

faq.q: Why was the tattoo in my dream so painful?
faq.a: Pain is often linked to a sense that "this decision has a cost." You may already know that a certain choice isn't easy, and the dream magnifies that difficulty into pain.

giving-birth.name: giving birth
giving-birth.title: What does it mean to dream about giving birth?
giving-birth.lead: Dreaming of giving birth is often about something taking shape, and not necessarily about a real pregnancy. It may reflect a plan, a relationship, or a side of yourself that you're nurturing and haven't shared yet.
giving-birth.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say a great deal about childbirth. It is often read as "something new is about to begin" or "responsibility is coming." Some editions distinguish a boy from a girl, or an easy birth from a hard one, each with its own associations. These are traditional ways of drawing parallels, and the editions differ widely. They don't mean anything will happen in real life, and they say nothing about your health.
giving-birth.plain: This dream often shows up when you have something "unfinished but important" in your hands: a project, a relationship, a change you want to make. By day it may feel slow and not yet formed, and at night the dream acts it out as giving birth. It may also be that you're caring for someone or carrying a responsibility lately, tired but unable to let go. A common detail is that you keep wondering in the dream whether the baby has been born yet. That usually matches your expectations about some outcome. Another common version is a very hard labor, which may reflect a sense that the matter takes more effort than you imagined.

variants.q: Dreaming of being pregnant
variants.a: Often linked to a state of still preparing and not yet going public. An idea may be growing in you that you don't want others to know about yet. Traditional views vary, and none of them means something will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of painful childbirth
variants.a: This may match a feeling that something is hard to push forward, or that you're in a stage that demands effort. Pain is often stress magnified, and doesn't mean anything will actually go wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of having a boy or a girl
variants.a: Traditional editions often give different associations by gender, but they don't agree with one another. What's more worth noticing is the mood in your dream: anticipation, nervousness, or relief.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else being pregnant
variants.a: It may reflect that you're sensitive to changes in that person's life, or that you've placed one of your own hopes on them. Think about whether someone's progress has been on your mind lately.

giving-birth.ask: If the birth in your dream reminds you of something taking shape, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which coming days might bring movement.
giving-birth.askQ: When will the thing I'm working on show results?

faq.q: Does dreaming of giving birth mean I'll get pregnant?
faq.a: A dream can't tell you whether you're pregnant. The two aren't directly connected. This kind of dream is more often tied to the feeling of something taking shape.

faq.q: Why was the birth in my dream going so badly?
faq.a: It may reflect feeling stuck or worn out by how something is progressing. The dream turns that "can't push it forward" feeling into a scene. It doesn't mean things will go badly in real life.

sweating.name: sweating
sweating.title: What does it mean to dream about sweating?
sweating.lead: Dreaming of sweating is often tied to a state of working hard and almost reaching your limit. It may reflect how much you've put into something lately, or a tension in you that hasn't eased.
sweating.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about sweating. Some read it as "effort is being made and progress will follow," others as "a draining period, so rest more." Some also distinguish heavy from light sweat, or hot from cold. These are traditional ways of drawing parallels, the editions often disagree, and none of them means something will happen in real life.
sweating.plain: Sweating in a dream often matches a sense of exertion by day. Maybe your work is packed and you're always rushing, or you've been tense in a relationship, afraid of saying the wrong thing. Another common version is feeling very hot and being unable to wipe the sweat away, which may reflect a feeling that something never gets finished. This dream also tends to appear when you're trying hard but haven't seen results yet, and your body expresses the tiredness first. Notice whether you wake up feeling relieved or more tense. That is usually your real feeling about something lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of sweating heavily
variants.a: This may match having put a lot into something lately and feeling a bit overextended. Traditional views vary, and this doesn't mean your body will have problems, but it may be worth asking whether you need a pause.

variants.q: Dreaming of cold sweat
variants.a: Often linked to the feeling of being suddenly startled, with your chest tightening. Something may be unsettling you lately, or you may be waiting for news.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else sweating
variants.a: It may reflect that you feel for how hard someone is working, or that you've placed your own stress on them. Think about whether someone's situation has been on your mind lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of sweating and feeling good
variants.a: This dream often comes with the feeling of "finally getting moving and getting things done." It may mean you feel grounded about the effort you've put into a stage of life. It isn't necessarily a bad sign.

sweating.ask: If the sweat in your dream reminds you of something you've been holding up for a long time, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which coming days might bring movement.
sweating.askQ: Is the thing I'm holding up right now worth continuing?

faq.q: Does dreaming of sweating mean my health is poor?
faq.a: A dream can't be used as a basis for judging health. If you really do sweat a lot, sleep badly, or have repeated nightmares, talking to a doctor will be more helpful than interpreting dreams.

faq.q: Why do I dream I'm sweating when I'm not hot?
faq.a: What happens in a dream doesn't always have to do with temperature. More often it reflects tension in your feelings. Maybe something lately has kept you on guard.

fever.name: fever
fever.title: What does it mean to dream about a fever?
fever.lead: Dreaming of a fever is usually not a sign about your body. It's more a picture of something "burning" in your mind. It often shows up when daytime stress is high, your feelings are full, or you're worried about how something is progressing. The dream acts out that tension with the image of a rising temperature.
fever.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on bodily dreams like a fever. Some versions read it as "a fire in the heart, something left unfinished," a symbol of too much thinking and bottled-up feelings. Others link it to "shifting fortunes in money" or to gossip and quarrels, saying that dreaming of a hot body may have to do with arguments or talk behind someone's back. Still other versions lean toward a reading of liveliness and popularity. Since the versions differ so much, it's better not to treat any of them as settled. Think of it as the older generations' metaphor for inner restlessness.
fever.plain: This dream often comes when you've been especially busy or rushed, or when there's a fire in your chest with nowhere to put it. Maybe a work deadline is pressing on you, maybe there's something you haven't talked through with someone, or maybe you're expecting a lot from something and feel "fired up" all over. A fever in a dream is often your body turning the day's tension into something concrete during sleep, through images of heat, warmth and sweat. Some people have this dream when they're simply tired, the room is stuffy, or the blanket is too thick, which is even simpler. One thing to notice: is something lately keeping you from settling down? Writing it down or talking it over with someone usually helps more than going back and forth on what the dream means.

variants.q: Dreaming of a high fever and a burning body
variants.a: This is common when your feelings ran high during the day or stress has built up to a peak. The dream uses "burning hot" to magnify that tightness. Think about what lately has kept you from settling down.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else with a fever and you taking care of them
variants.a: It mostly reflects that someone has been on your mind lately, or that you tend to take other people's matters onto your own shoulders. It may also be that you've sensed someone close to you isn't doing well, and you can't let it go.

variants.q: Dreaming of a fever but being unable to take your temperature
variants.a: This "heat you can't explain" often matches a vague anxiety, a sense that something is about to happen without being able to grasp what. It usually has to do with waiting for a result or with uncertainty.

variants.q: Dreaming of the fever breaking and sweating
variants.a: This often appears just after stress has eased, when something has finally come to a close. The cooling and sweating in the dream feel more like a weight being set down.

variants.q: Dreaming of a child with a fever
variants.a: It may reflect that you care a great deal about someone or something that needs looking after (family, a team member, even a project of your own) and worry it won't hold up.

fever.ask: If the fever in your dream is tied to a particular person or something you can't put down, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what may stir in the days ahead.
fever.askQ: What will happen next with the matter that's on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a fever mean something is really wrong with my body?
faq.a: A dream isn't a medical exam and can't be used to judge your health. But if you've really been sleeping badly and keep having this kind of dream, talk with a doctor and describe your sleep clearly. That will be more reassuring than interpreting it yourself.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a fever mean I'll be very busy soon?
faq.a: A closer way to put it: it often appears alongside a "burning" state you're in during the day. How busy you'll be depends on your real schedule. The dream just plays that pace back to you.

sick.name: being sick
sick.title: What does it mean to dream about being sick?
sick.lead: Dreaming of being sick is usually not a sign about your body. It's more your mind saying "I'm tired." If you've held on too long in the day and stress has had nowhere to go, the night uses an image of illness to remind you to rest.
sick.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say this: dreaming that you are sick is read in some versions as "your body reminding you to rest," and in others as "some small worries ahead." Dreaming of someone else falling ill is often said to mean "worrying for them" or "a change in your relationship with that person." The versions differ quite a bit, and even different copies of the same book often contradict each other, so take this only as the older generations' way of making associations, not something to believe literally.
sick.plain: This dream often comes after long stretches of overtime, too little sleep, or when you've been especially mindful of your health. It may also be that you saw a family member feeling unwell or heard about an illness in the news, and the image stayed with you. The sick self in the dream often matches the side of you that keeps pushing on and doesn't dare say you're tired. Related dreams are common too: a fever, a hospital stay, someone else seriously ill. They mostly reflect your tiredness and your concern for others, not a warning that someone will get hurt. If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you're sleeping badly, talk with a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of having a high fever
variants.a: This is common when you're truly worn out or something is burning in your mind that you can't put down. The image of body heat is often a metaphor for feelings, showing you're in a state of "can't hold on, but holding on anyway."

variants.q: Dreaming of a family member falling ill
variants.a: It mostly has to do with caring about them. Have you been calling often to check in, or worrying about an elder's health? The dream magnifies that concern into an image. It doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of being in the hospital on an IV drip
variants.a: This often appears when you badly want to do nothing and be looked after for a while. Or you may have recently been to a hospital, and the scene stayed in your memory.

variants.q: Dreaming of others saying you're sick
variants.a: It may reflect a fear of being seen when you're not doing well, or a concern about how others judge your stamina and performance. During the day, give yourself a bit more room to breathe.

sick.ask: If a particular person or something you can't let go of appears in the dream, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what may stir in the days ahead.
sick.askQ: What should I pay attention to in my health and mood lately?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being sick mean something is really wrong with my body?
faq.a: Some people have traditionally made that association, but in real life a dream can't check your health. If you feel unwell, see a doctor rather than relying on a dream. A dream is more a reflection of your fatigue and mood.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming of being sick?
faq.a: First look at whether you've been sleeping too little or under too much stress. Bring your routine back in order and find chances to relax during the day, and the dreams usually change too. If they keep coming back and affect your sleep, talk with a doctor.

rain.name: rain
rain.title: What does it mean to dream about rain?
rain.lead: Dreaming of rain is often tied to the flow of emotion. You may be holding in words or feelings that are looking for a way out. It also shows up when you feel stuffy, need time to settle, or when something is slowly passing.
rain.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about dreaming of rain. Some versions read rain as nourishment and prosperity, a sign that good things are near. Others lean toward worry and tears, saying rain in a dream may relate to sorrow or parting. Still others go by how hard it rains: light rain for smooth progress, heavy rain for change. Because the versions contradict each other, tradition mostly treats it as a metaphor for feeling, not as a sign that anything will happen in real life.
rain.plain: This dream often comes when you feel a bit weighed down and some words have gone unsaid. You may have grown distant from someone lately, something may feel damp and heavy, or you may be in a transition, with one stage ending and the next not yet here. Rain in a dream often gives a shape to that need to flow and release. Some people have this dream on a rainy night, or in a damp room, and then it's simpler still. You might ask yourself: is there a feeling I've set aside and not dealt with? Talking to someone or writing it down usually helps ease it.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting soaked in heavy rain
variants.a: This often appears when you feel doused by some emotion or situation, like a sudden change or something you couldn't quite handle. It usually has to do with your rhythm being thrown off lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of sheltering from rain under an umbrella
variants.a: It may reflect that you're protecting yourself and don't want to get caught up in something. The umbrella is more like a bit of buffer space you've made for yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of light rain that won't stop
variants.a: This is common with a lingering mood, where nothing blows up but things stay unresolved. It usually relates to waiting, or to a relationship that is unclear.

variants.q: Dreaming of the sky clearing after rain
variants.a: This often appears when pressure eases and your mood lifts. The rain stopping is more like a picture of a knot inside you slowly loosening.

variants.q: Dreaming of a leak, or rain inside the house
variants.a: It may reflect a sense that your defenses have a gap, and something private or at home is leaving you uneasy. Think about where lately you haven't felt well cared for.

rain.ask: If the rain in your dream is connected to someone you can't let go of, or to something on your mind, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what may stir in the coming days.
rain.askQ: Where is this damp, heavy matter on my mind headed from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of rain mean I'll be sad?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Rain in a dream is often a picture of emotion moving. It could be sadness, or it could be relief and settling. Go by how you feel on waking, not by a fixed answer.

faq.q: Does dreaming of heavy rain mean something bad is coming?
faq.a: The traditional versions vary a lot, and none of it means something will happen in real life. A more practical reading is that it often comes along with a stretch when you feel overwhelmed, so give yourself a chance to catch your breath.

thunderstorm.name: thunder
thunderstorm.title: What does it mean to dream about thunder?
thunderstorm.lead: Dreaming of thunder is often linked to the feeling of being suddenly jolted awake. Something during the day may have shaken you, or you may be tense and waiting for news, and the dream stages that tension as thunder.
thunderstorm.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ on dreaming of thunder. Some versions read thunder as reputation and command, a sign that news is coming or things are about to stir. Others lean toward fright and quarrels, saying thunder in a dream may relate to arguments or sudden upheaval. Still others link thunder and lightning to clearing away old matters, reading it as a turning point. Because the versions contradict each other, tradition mostly treats it as a metaphor for shaking or jolting, not as a sign that anything will happen in real life.
thunderstorm.plain: This dream often comes when your nerves are wound tight. You may be waiting for a result or a reply, there may be sudden changes around you, or there may be something you've been holding back that is close to bursting out. Thunder in a dream often gives form to that sense of a coming storm, using sound and flashes to magnify the tension. Some people have this dream during a real thunderstorm, when it's noisy outside, and then it's simpler still. You might ask yourself: is something keeping me listening, waiting? Saying it plainly, or turning your attention to something else for a while, usually helps ease it.

variants.q: Dreaming of loud thunder that wakes you up in fright
variants.a: This is common when stress has built up to a point and you're on constant alert. The thunder is more like the taut line inside you being plucked.

variants.q: Dreaming of thunder and lightning with a bright sky
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been especially sensitive lately, and the slightest stir gets to you. It also appears when you're looking forward to some news and your mind is fixed on it.

variants.q: Dreaming of thunder without rain
variants.a: A dream that rumbles but never rains often matches a feeling of waiting, with a lot of noise and little result. It seems something is about to move, but hasn't actually happened yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of hiding indoors from the lightning
variants.a: It may reflect that you're avoiding a conflict or some pressure and want to protect yourself first. The house is more like a shelter you've found for yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of lightning striking nearby without hurting anyone
variants.a: This often appears right after a scare, or when something turned out all right in the end. Lightning passing close is more like a picture of lingering shakiness.

thunderstorm.ask: If the thunder in your dream is connected to someone you can't let go of, or to something on your mind, you can cast a hexagram about it and see what may stir in the coming days.
thunderstorm.askQ: The news I've been waiting for lately: what is likely to stir next?

faq.q: Does dreaming of thunder mean something bad will happen?
faq.a: The traditional versions vary a lot, and none of it means something will happen in real life. A more practical reading is that it often comes along with a stretch of tension and waiting, so try to let yourself relax a little.

faq.q: What does it mean to wake up startled by thunder in a dream?
faq.a: It mostly reflects a sense of being on call, on alert during the day. If this dream keeps coming back and you aren't sleeping well, it's worth talking to a doctor about your sleep.

earthquake.name: earthquake
earthquake.title: What does it mean to dream about an earthquake?
earthquake.lead: Dreaming of an earthquake is often tied to a feeling of unsteady ground, as if your foundation is shifting. Something in your life may have changed lately, or you may not feel sure about how stable something is. The dream acts out that unease with a shaking earth.
earthquake.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about dreaming of an earthquake. Some versions read it as change at home or a move, linked to a shift in your living situation. Others lean toward a shaken foundation and an uneasy mind, saying the tremor may reflect uncertainty in people or plans. Still others read it as an old order being renewed, seeing the shaking as a symbol of reorganizing. The versions differ from one another. Traditionally it is mostly taken as a metaphor for change, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.
earthquake.plain: This dream often shows up when something in your life is loosening. Work may be changing, your living situation may be shifting, the way you relate to someone may be changing, or your plans for the future may suddenly feel less certain. An earthquake in a dream often gives shape to that "not quite steady" feeling, through images of shaking, cracking and things falling. Some people have this kind of dream after a real earthquake, or while sleeping somewhere that sways, and then it's much simpler. You might ask yourself: is something lately making me feel the ground is moving? Steadying the parts you can control usually helps you feel more grounded.

variants.q: Dreaming of an earthquake and things falling everywhere
variants.a: This often appears when you feel your daily order has been thrown off, such as by a sudden change or by one thing after another. The falling objects are more like a picture of feeling out of control.

variants.q: Dreaming of an earthquake while standing firm
variants.a: This may reflect that, even in the middle of change, part of you is settled. It also often appears when you've already prepared yourself to face a change.

variants.q: Dreaming of a house cracking after an earthquake
variants.a: This often matches a feeling that your sense of security has a crack in it. Something at home, or a relationship you depend on, may be leaving you uneasy.

variants.q: Dreaming of fleeing to an open space after an earthquake
variants.a: This may reflect that you want to step away from some pressure and find a safe distance. The open space in the dream is more like the place where you want to catch your breath.

variants.q: Dreaming of an earthquake but feeling nothing
variants.a: This "it shook but I felt nothing" dream often appears when you've gotten used to change, or are deliberately not paying attention to something. You might ask whether some feeling has been left unattended.

earthquake.ask: If the earthquake in your dream is connected to someone you can't let go of, or to something weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
earthquake.askQ: The part of my life that is changing right now: how will it unfold from here?

faq.q: If I dream of an earthquake, will a real one happen?
faq.a: A dream is not a prediction, and traditionally it isn't taken to mean something will happen. It more often reflects how you feel about instability, and has nothing to do with real tremors.

faq.q: Does dreaming of an earthquake mean my life is about to change?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but this kind of dream often comes along with change you've been sensing lately. Rather than worrying, look at what is making you feel unsteady, and steady the parts you can control first.

tsunami.name: tsunami
tsunami.title: What does it mean to dream about a tsunami?
tsunami.lead: Dreaming of a tsunami is mostly not a warning of disaster. It more likely points to something that feels close to more than you can bear. In dreams a tsunami often stands for overwhelming emotion or pressure. After waking, consider whether something has been piling up for too long.
tsunami.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about dreams of floods and tsunamis. One school reads big water as money or opportunity on the way, seeing a strong flow as resources moving. Another reads water flooding a home as a crowded mind and pressure from household matters or relationships. Some versions say high waves hitting the shore mean a change in your surroundings is coming. Because the versions contradict each other, the traditional readings are best taken as cultural reference, not as a forecast.
tsunami.plain: This dream often comes when you're already tired in the daytime but still have to hold on, for example when your workload suddenly grows, family matters fall on you, or a relationship stirs up strong feelings. The feeling of seeing a tsunami from far off and not being able to run in time may match a sense of helplessness about something: you know it's coming, but you aren't ready. Some people have it just before a change, such as a new job, a move, or exam results. The color of the water, and whether you got to higher ground, often reflect how much in control you feel.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tsunami and escaping to high ground
variants.a: This may reflect that you've found some way to cope, or that you know you have a way out. It's common when the pressure is still there but you've started arranging a backup plan.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tsunami flooding your home
variants.a: In dreams, home often stands for security. Being flooded may match a feeling that your daily order has been disrupted, or worry about family or where you live. It isn't necessarily about any real disaster.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tsunami but feeling calm
variants.a: This may mean you're already mentally prepared for a big change, or that your feelings have been pressed down so long that you've gone numb for now. Notice whether you also tend to hold things in during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else being chased by a tsunami
variants.a: This often relates to someone you care about. You may be worried about them, or you may be projecting your own pressure onto them. Think about whether someone has been on your mind lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tsunami receding
variants.a: Receding often stands for something coming to an end or feelings slowly settling. If debris is left behind in the dream, it may mean you're still cleaning up after something.

tsunami.ask: If a particular person appears in your dream, or something is weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
tsunami.askQ: This stressful matter I've been dealing with lately: how will it develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a tsunami mean a disaster will happen?
faq.a: Traditional dream readings vary, but in real life dreams don't predict disasters. A tsunami dream more often reflects your recent stress and sense of helplessness, so it's more practical to look after your routine and your feelings first.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming of a tsunami?
faq.a: If it keeps coming back and affects your sleep, consider talking to a doctor. You can also write down the strongest image from the dream and compare it with what has been making you tense lately. A connection usually shows up.

fire.name: fire
fire.title: What does it mean to dream about a fire?
fire.lead: Dreaming of a fire is often tied to feeling "burned up" inside, or to something that has "caught fire" right in front of you. In a dream, fire can stand for anger or anxiety, but also for drive and the energy to change. A lot depends on whether you were watching from the side or being chased.
fire.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree quite a bit about fire. Some versions see fire as a sign of vigor and prosperity, and say a strong blaze means momentum in your fortunes or career. Other versions read a fire, or a burning house, as gossip and quarrels, trouble at home, or an unsettled mind. Another view takes a fire going out as heat fading away. The versions contradict one another, so treat them only as cultural reference.
fire.plain: Fire dreams often come when you have been building up a lot of feeling during the day: being misunderstood, being pushed to hurry, or friction with family or coworkers. The image of flames may match that "I can't hold it in much longer" feeling. Some people have it when life suddenly speeds up, such as a project deadline, a move, or exams coming close. Whether you fought the fire or got out often reflects how much control you feel you have. If the fire was small and went out quickly, it may just be a leftover from some minor irritation during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a fire and escaping
variants.a: It may mean that things feel tense, but you still see a way out. This kind of dream is common when you are under pressure but are already thinking about how to handle it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a house on fire
variants.a: A house often stands for your own territory or your family. A burning house may match a feeling that your living space, family relationships, or private time are being disturbed. It doesn't necessarily have anything to do with a real fire.

variants.q: Dreaming of putting out a fire
variants.a: It often reflects that you have been cleaning up other people's problems during the day, or keeping your own feelings pressed down. Ask yourself whether you have lately been the one who always "puts out the fires."

variants.q: Dreaming of a fire without being afraid
variants.a: It may mean you are actually a little hopeful about some change, or that you have already accepted that things will shift. It could also be that your feelings are held down, so the dream feels calm.

variants.q: Dreaming of thick smoke but no flames
variants.a: Smoke often stands for pressure you can't see clearly. It may match a sense that something is off, though you can't yet say what. It is common while you are waiting for a result.

fire.ask: If someone in the dream stayed on your mind, or there is something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring movement.
fire.askQ: How will this situation that has been bothering me develop from here?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a fire a bad omen?
faq.a: Traditional sayings are mixed, some good and some bad, and they vary by version. In real life, dreams don't announce disasters. A fire dream more often reflects your recent feelings and stress, so first look at whether something has been bottled up during the day.

faq.q: What should I do if I feel uneasy after dreaming of a fire?
faq.a: You can start with a few slow breaths, then write down the strongest image from the dream and compare it with what has been irritating you lately. If it keeps disturbing your sleep, consider talking with a doctor.

volcano.name: volcano
volcano.title: What does it mean to dream about a volcano?
volcano.lead: Dreaming of a volcano is often tied to feelings that have been held down for a long time and are about to burst out. In a dream, a volcano is like a symbol of stored-up energy. It may match a temper you have held back, words you haven't said, or a situation that is about to change.
volcano.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say little about volcanoes, and what they say is inconsistent. One school sees a mountain as a backer, a responsibility, or an obstacle, and reads an eruption as a change coming to something that has been building up. Another school reads fire and mountain separately: fire for gossip and quarrels, mountain for standstill, and together they stand for movement and stillness intertwined. Because there are few versions and they contradict each other, treat the traditional sayings only as cultural reference.
volcano.plain: Volcano dreams often come when things look fine on the surface but you feel full inside: you don't dare say something at work, you keep giving way in a relationship, or you have hesitated a long time over a decision. The feeling of lava churning inside may match your knowing that sooner or later you will have to take a stand. Some people have it just before a change, such as handing in a resignation, going into a negotiation, or leaving a place where they have lived a long time. Whether the volcano was quietly smoking or already erupting often reflects whether the pressure feels like "still holding it in" or "can't hold it in anymore."

variants.q: Dreaming of a volcano erupting
variants.a: It may mean you feel something has reached a breaking point, or that your emotions are close to giving way. This kind of dream is common after a long stretch of holding back, when a trigger has just appeared.

variants.q: Dreaming of a volcano smoking but not erupting
variants.a: It often matches a state of "still holding it in." You know where you stand, but haven't decided whether to speak or act, so the dream stops at the smoking stage.

variants.q: Dreaming of volcanic ash falling
variants.a: Ash often stands for the aftermath of something. It may reflect worry that a decision will affect the people around you, or that you are still sorting through earlier feelings.

variants.q: Dreaming of standing at the crater
variants.a: It may mean you are at a key point, know things will change, but haven't yet taken the step. Think about whether there is a choice lately that both excites and frightens you.

variants.q: Dreaming of a volcano in the sea
