jewelry.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say a few common things. One treats jewelry as a precious object, so dreaming of it is tied to being valued or rising in standing. Another says jewelry belongs to wealth, so it often gets linked to income or gain. Some versions say the opposite: finding or receiving jewelry in a dream is a reminder not to put all your attention on outward things. The versions differ and even contradict each other. Traditionally they were treated as a language of symbols, and they don't mean anything will happen in real life.
jewelry.plain: In dreams, jewelry is often tied to the question "Am I worth it?" You may have just been praised or compared to someone, or you may feel overlooked. Or you may be weighing whether a sum of money, a relationship, or an opportunity is worth it. Bright, expensive jewelry often shows up when you feel excited or hope to be recognized. Jewelry that is dropped or can't be found often appears when you fear losing something or not being good enough. It works more like a mirror of how you weigh your own worth than a calculation of your finances.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding jewelry
variants.a: Often comes at a time when you feel "my good luck has finally arrived," or when something recently felt like a lucky find. Finding it in a dream doesn't mean you'll receive anything in real life. What matters is where that sense of surprise comes from.

variants.q: Dreaming of lost jewelry
variants.a: Usually connected to a fear of losing something: money, a relationship, or a position you value. Common when you've felt unsettled lately and keep checking that things are still there.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone giving you jewelry
variants.a: Often reflects a wish to be recognized and treated kindly, or that someone really has been good to you lately. It may also be a question: should I accept this kindness, and is it right to take it?

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of jewelry
variants.a: A large amount usually matches a feeling of having "so much to weigh." It could be too many choices, or too much pressure. Common around the time of a major decision.

variants.q: Dreaming of jewelry being stolen
variants.a: Often shows up when you feel something has been taken or snatched ahead of you. It may not be property; it could be credit, an opportunity, or attention. After waking, think about who has left you feeling unbalanced lately.

jewelry.ask: If the jewelry in your dream made you think of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring movement.
jewelry.askQ: Will there be any movement on the matter that's been on my mind lately?

faq.q: If I dream about jewelry, am I about to get rich?
faq.a: Traditional sayings do often link jewelry with wealth, but that's symbolic language, not a prediction. A more practical reading is that you've been especially aware of money or self-worth lately, and the dream acts out that concern.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of jewelry falling on the ground?
faq.a: The usual explanation is a fear of losing something or not being good enough. Recall whether in the dream you rushed to pick it up or glanced and walked away. That's more like your habitual response to loss than a sign of any event.

ring.name: ring
ring.title: What does it mean to dream about a ring?
ring.lead: Dreaming about a ring is often tied to commitment, relationships, and settling things. It doesn't necessarily point to marriage. More often it reflects what you've been thinking about: whether to take a relationship further, or whether to finalize a decision.
ring.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say quite a bit about rings. Some treat a ring as a token of trust, so dreaming of one is linked to engagement, making friends, or being entrusted with something. Some say wearing a ring in a dream symbolizes taking on status or responsibility. Others mention a lost or broken ring, read as a promise changing. The versions differ widely, and the same scene often has opposite readings. Traditionally they were seen only as symbols, and they don't mean anything will happen in real life.
ring.plain: A ring in a dream often corresponds to the question of whether to settle down. You may be waiting for a word from someone, or hesitating over a commitment. Or a decision about work, moving, or a collaboration may be stuck at the last step. A ring that doesn't fit when you try it on often appears when an arrangement feels forced. A ring that's lost or can't be found often appears when you worry you've agreed to something you can't deliver. It helps bring the matter of commitment out into the open rather than announcing an outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of putting on a ring
variants.a: Often comes when you're considering taking on a role or responsibility, in a relationship or at work. Putting it on in a dream doesn't mean it will happen. What matters is whether you felt happy or reluctant.

variants.q: Dreaming of a ring falling off
variants.a: Usually linked to a fear of breaking a promise or losing something. Common when you've agreed to something recently but feel unsure about it. It may also be a worry that a relationship is loosening.

variants.q: Dreaming of receiving a ring
variants.a: Often reflects a hope to be recognized or chosen, or that someone really has shown you goodwill lately. It may also be a question: can I live up to this gesture?

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken ring
variants.a: Common when you feel a crack in some agreement or relationship. A break in a dream is a symbol and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. You can think about what lately has felt "not quite right."

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of rings
variants.a: A large number often matches too many choices or too many commitments. Common when you're pulled in several directions at once, or have agreed to so much that you feel breathless.

ring.ask: If the ring in your dream made you think of a certain person or something not yet settled, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days may bring movement.
ring.askQ: Will there be any further news between him and me?

faq.q: If I dream about a ring, am I going to get married?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link rings with engagement, but that's symbolic, not a prediction. A more common reading is that what's on your mind is exactly the question of whether to settle down, and the dream played it out.

faq.q: Does dreaming of a lost ring mean there's a problem in my relationship?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It more often reflects unease, such as fear that your partner will change their mind or that you can't keep a promise. It doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. You can use it to ask whether something has gone unsaid lately.

necklace.name: necklace
necklace.title: What does it mean to dream about a necklace?
necklace.lead: Dreaming of a necklace is often tied to feeling held, remembered, or looked after. It may reflect a connection you've been thinking about a lot lately, or a question like: can I carry this relationship, this responsibility?
necklace.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few readings. Some treat a necklace as a precious ornament, so dreaming of one is linked to being valued or receiving a gift. Some say anything worn around the neck stands for restraint or duty, and wearing one in a dream means being entrusted with something. Other versions say a broken or fallen necklace means a connection is loosening. The versions differ. Traditionally these are only symbolic language and don't mean anything will happen in real life.
necklace.plain: A necklace hangs around the neck, and in dreams it often points to two things: connection and burden. You may be tied to a relationship or responsibility right now, and it might feel warm, or it might feel tight. Or you may badly want someone to remember you and keep you in mind. A beautiful, shining necklace often shows up when you hope to be cherished. A broken necklace, or one you can't unclasp, often appears when a relationship or commitment is leaving you a little short of breath. It's more a reflection of how you feel about that tie.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken necklace
variants.a: This often comes up when a connection feels like it's loosening, or a responsibility feels close to more than you can hold. The break is a symbol and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. You might think about what lately has made you feel "this is about to snap."

variants.q: Dreaming of someone giving you a necklace
variants.a: This often reflects a wish to be remembered and cherished, or someone really has shown you their feelings lately. You may also be wondering whether there are strings attached to this kindness.

variants.q: Dreaming of wearing a very heavy necklace
variants.a: This mostly matches a feeling in waking life of a responsibility weighing on you, perhaps at work, in your family, or in a relationship. A heavy feeling in the dream is usually a nudge to notice how much you're carrying.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lost necklace
variants.a: This often appears when you fear losing a connection or being forgotten. It may also be that life has changed a lot lately, and something familiar feels gone.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding a necklace
variants.a: This often comes up in a period when a relationship or opportunity has come to you unexpectedly. Finding one in a dream doesn't mean you'll receive anything in real life. What matters is the feeling of "is this really mine?"

necklace.ask: If the necklace in your dream brings to mind a certain person or a connection you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
necklace.askQ: Will I hear from the person I've been thinking about lately?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a broken necklace a bad sign?
faq.a: Some traditional readings do say so, but that's symbolic language and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more practical reading is that a relationship or responsibility may be wearing you out lately.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of wearing a necklace?
faq.a: Common readings link it to being entrusted with something or being remembered. It may also mean you're in a relationship that makes you feel tied down. Think back on whether it felt comfortable or tight in the dream; that's closer to what you truly feel.

clothes.name: clothes
clothes.title: What does it mean to dream about clothes?
clothes.lead: Dreaming of clothes is often about "how I want others to see me." It may reflect that you've been caring about your appearance or how others judge you, or wondering whether the way you are now is still what you want.
clothes.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say many things about clothes. Some see new clothes as a renewed identity and a fresh look. Some say clothes stand for a person's public face and circumstances, so changing clothes in a dream is linked to a change in fortune. Other versions say torn or dirty clothes mean damaged face or private worries showing. The versions differ widely, and the same scene often gets different readings. Traditionally they're taken only as symbols and don't mean anything will happen in real life.
clothes.plain: In dreams, clothes often stand for image and protection. You may be especially concerned about how others see you, or you've just changed settings or roles and aren't sure yet whether it fits. Clothes that don't fit often show up when a role feels forced. Torn or dirty clothes often appear when you fear being seen through or embarrassed. Putting on new clothes often shows up when you want a fresh start. It's more a mirror of how you see yourself than a judgment on whether your situation is good or bad.

variants.q: Dreaming of torn clothes
variants.a: This often appears when you fear being seen through or embarrassed. You may also feel you can't keep up a certain image lately. The tear is a symbol and doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of wearing new clothes
variants.a: This often matches a wish to start over or be seen, and is common around a job change, a move, or new progress in a relationship. The new clothes reflect your hopes.

variants.q: Dreaming of clothes that don't fit
variants.a: This is mostly tied to a feeling of "this role doesn't suit me," whether a job, an identity, or a relationship. You might think about what lately has felt off.

variants.q: Dreaming of dirty clothes
variants.a: This is common when you feel your reputation or image is being affected. It may also just be that you're under stress and afraid of making mistakes. Getting dirty in a dream doesn't mean trouble in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of having nothing to wear
variants.a: This often comes up when you have to face an occasion and don't feel ready. You may also be asking yourself how you really want to show up.

clothes.ask: If the clothes in your dream bring to mind a certain occasion or something you can't put down, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
clothes.askQ: Will the thing I have to face soon go smoothly?

faq.q: Is dreaming of torn clothes unlucky?
faq.a: Some traditional readings say so, but that's symbolic language and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more common reading is that you've been afraid of being seen through lately, or that an image you keep up is tiring you.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of wearing someone else's clothes?
faq.a: This often reflects that you're playing a role that doesn't quite belong to you, or handling things the way someone else would. You might think about whether lately you've had a feeling of "this isn't like me."

shoes.name: shoes
shoes.title: What does it mean to dream about shoes?
shoes.lead: Dreaming of shoes is often about "where am I headed, and can I keep going?" It may reflect that you've been weighing a direction, worrying about whether your footing is steady, or wondering whether to continue down this road.
shoes.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. Some treat shoes as a symbol of walking and one's path, so dreaming of new shoes links to a change of setting or direction. Others say shoes stand for a partner or a companion, and a pair of shoes in a dream is tied to a relationship. Some versions say that lost or worn-out shoes mean a rough road ahead. The versions disagree, and traditionally these are only symbolic language. They don't mean anything will happen in real life.
shoes.plain: In dreams, shoes often point to direction and support. You may be standing at a crossroads right now, unsure whether to change jobs, cities, or a relationship. Or you may feel unsteady on your feet and worry about taking a wrong turn. Shoes that don't fit often show up when a choice feels forced. Lost or missing shoes often appear when you fear falling behind or being left out. New shoes often appear when you're getting ready to set out. The dream is more a reflection of how you feel about moving forward.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing a shoe
variants.a: This often shows up when you feel thrown off your stride or afraid of not keeping up. Something recent may also have caught you off guard. Losing a shoe in a dream is a symbol. It doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of wearing new shoes
variants.a: This often matches the feeling of getting ready to set out or change direction, and is common around a new job, a new school term, or a relationship moving forward. The new shoes reflect your hope and your nerves.

variants.q: Dreaming of shoes that don't fit
variants.a: This is usually tied to a sense that this choice isn't quite right for me. It could be about work, where you live, or a relationship. Think about what lately has made your steps feel stuck.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding your shoes
variants.a: This is common when you have something to face but don't feel ready. It may also be the question running in your mind: which way should I go?

variants.q: Dreaming of worn-out shoes
variants.a: This often appears when you feel you can't keep going and need to stop. It isn't necessarily a bad sign. It's more like your body or mind reminding you to rest.

shoes.ask: If the shoes in your dream remind you of a choice or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
shoes.askQ: Will there be any movement on the direction I'm considering now?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about losing a shoe?
faq.a: Some traditional readings link it to a rough road, but that is symbolic language and doesn't mean anything will happen. A more common reading is that you've felt thrown off your stride lately, or worry about keeping up with something.

faq.q: Does dreaming of new shoes mean I'm about to change jobs?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It more often reflects that you're already getting ready to set out, or looking forward to a new stage. A dream isn't a forecast, but it can help you see that part of you wants to move.

hat.name: hat
hat.title: What does it mean to dream about a hat? Common symbols and clues
hat.lead: Dreaming of a hat is mostly about identity, image, and how others see you. A hat sits on your head, so it often stands for a role, your reputation, or protection. It may also just be an image left over from tidying a closet or thinking about a new look.
hat.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about hats. One common reading says that wearing or changing to a new hat means a shift in status or surroundings. Another says a hat falling off means damaged image or losing support. Some versions see picking up a hat as taking over someone else's position. Copies and regions differ a lot, and the same thing often gets opposite readings, so traditional sayings are only a cultural reference.
hat.plain: During the day, you may well be caring about how others see you: a new job, a presentation, a new environment, or keeping up an image on social media. In a dream, a hat is often like an outer shell. Wearing it comfortably may reflect being fairly at ease in some role. A hat that's too tight, keeps falling off, or can't be found often shows up when you worry about not doing well enough or being seen through. Some people simply bought a hat or watched styling videos lately. Notice whether you wake up feeling embarrassed, relieved, or wanting to hide. That feeling is usually closer to what's on your mind than the hat itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of a hat blown away by the wind
variants.a: This often matches a worry that your image is suddenly out of your control, such as saying the wrong thing or performing poorly. It may also be that it was windy lately and you nearly lost a hat, and the leftover image carried into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of wearing someone else's hat
variants.a: It may reflect that you're taking over someone else's role or responsibility, such as covering a position or caring for family. If the hat doesn't fit in the dream, it often carries the reluctant feeling that this position doesn't seem to be mine.

variants.q: Dreaming of buying a new hat
variants.a: This is common when you want to refresh your self-image or get ready for a new stage, like just before a new haircut, job, or move. It may also simply be that you've been browsing accessories.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding your hat
variants.a: It may match a daytime fear of missing something you need to do or being absent at a key moment. If you felt rushed in the dream, it's usually tied to time pressure or a pile of to-dos.

variants.q: Dreaming of a torn or dirty hat
variants.a: This often appears when you feel your image has been damaged or you've been misunderstood. Tradition speaks of losing face, but in real life it's usually just that you've been more sensitive to others' opinions lately.

hat.ask: If the hat in your dream reminds you of someone or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
hat.askQ: Will there be any movement on the matter that's been on my mind lately?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a hat mean a promotion or a job change?
faq.a: Traditional dream books do link changing hats to a change in status, but the versions differ and it can't be used as a prediction. A more useful reading is to ask whether you're considering a change of role during the day, or worrying whether you can handle a new position.

faq.q: Is it bad to keep dreaming of a hat falling off?
faq.a: Folk sayings hold that a lost hat means losing face, but that's only a traditional association and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. If the dream keeps recurring and disturbs your sleep, you can talk with a doctor about your sleep.

mirror.name: mirror
mirror.title: What does it mean to dream about a mirror? Seeing yourself and what you care about
mirror.lead: Dreaming of a mirror is often about self-examination and caring how you look in others' eyes. A mirror shows yourself, and may also show what you keep trying to check lately: am I doing this right, and what do others think of me?
mirror.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ quite a bit on mirrors. One common reading says seeing yourself in a mirror symbolizes self-reflection and seeing your situation clearly. Another says a cracked mirror means a rift in a relationship or plan. Some versions say a blurry reflection means something on your mind isn't yet clear to you. Copies from different places disagree, even contradict each other, so treat them as cultural curiosity, not a forecast.
mirror.plain: Mirror dreams often show up when you're sizing yourself up: before an interview, when a relationship is shifting, right after a mistake, or after someone's comment. If you look good in the mirror, it may reflect that you've been more accepting of yourself lately. If the image is blurry, the glass is fogged, or the person in the mirror doesn't look like you, it often points to uncertainty, a fear that you're not quite who you imagined. Some people simply checked the mirror too often during the day, worrying about their skin or figure, and the image slipped into the dream. When you wake, ask yourself: what did you fear the mirror would show? That is often where your mind has really been lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken mirror
variants.a: Often matches a feeling that something you were sure of has developed a crack, such as a relationship, a plan, or how you see yourself. Traditionally, breaking is said to symbolize change, but in real life it doesn't mean anything bad will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming that the person in the mirror isn't you
variants.a: It may reflect feeling "not like yourself" in some setting, such as forcing yourself into a role. Or things have changed so much lately that you haven't yet adjusted to where you are now.

variants.q: Dreaming of a mirror you can't see clearly in
variants.a: Common when you haven't figured out your direction or aren't sure of your own judgment. If you've been sleeping badly or feel foggy, tiredness may simply be blurring the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of many mirrors
variants.a: May correspond to the pressure of being watched from many sides, such as facing the expectations of family, coworkers, and friends all at once. If the dream feels oppressive, it usually has to do with being judged more often lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else in the mirror
variants.a: Often appears when you keep thinking about someone, or worry about how they see you. It may also just be a photo or message from them that stayed in your mind during the day.

mirror.ask: If the mirror in your dream reminds you of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
mirror.askQ: Will I hear news about the thing I keep dwelling on lately?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a broken mirror unlucky?
faq.a: Folk belief links a broken mirror to a relationship changing, but that is only a traditional association and doesn't mean it will happen. It's more worthwhile to ask whether you've felt especially unsure about a relationship or a decision lately.

faq.q: What does it mean to see a stranger in the mirror in a dream?
faq.a: Common when life is changing and you haven't yet adjusted to a new role, such as a new job, a move, or a change in identity. If this kind of dream keeps recurring and affects your sleep, it may help to talk to a doctor.

knife.name: knife
knife.title: What does it mean to dream about a knife? Cutting, conflict, and the feeling of deciding
knife.lead: Dreaming of a knife is often tied to making decisions, cutting something off, or dealing with conflict. A knife is a tool for cutting, so one in a dream may reflect a wish to draw a line lately, or being stuck on whether to let something go.
knife.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree about knives. One common reading takes holding a knife as decisiveness and readiness to handle things. Another says being threatened with a knife means a quarrel or pressure. Some versions see a dull or broken knife as things being stuck, with no strength to push forward. Versions even contradict each other, so the traditional sayings are only a reference, not a forecast.
knife.plain: Knife dreams often come when you need to choose: whether to end a relationship, quit a job, or speak plainly. Cutting something with a knife may reflect wanting to settle things cleanly. A knife that's dull or won't cut is common when progress feels stuck and no effort seems to get you there. If the dream has a scene of conflict, it may simply be news or a show you watched, or a recent disagreement, carrying its feelings into the dream. Notice whether you woke feeling relieved or tense. That usually points to how you really feel about "cutting things off."

variants.q: Dreaming of cutting something with a knife
variants.a: Often matches a wish to sort things out and decide what to keep, such as tidying a room or ending a relationship that has dragged on. If the cutting goes smoothly, it may reflect more confidence in the decision.

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased or threatened with a knife
variants.a: May reflect stress or conflict from your day, like being pushed on a deadline or arguing with someone. Traditionally it's said to mean friction with others, but in real life it's mostly tension projected into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of a knife breaking or going dull
variants.a: Common when you feel powerless or underprepared. You may also just be very tired, which adds to the stuck feeling in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of many knives
variants.a: May correspond to having many things to handle at once, or too many options to decide among. If the dream feels oppressive, it's usually linked to a packed to-do list lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of putting a knife away
variants.a: Often appears when you've decided not to confront someone yet and to hold back for now. It may also reflect wanting to avoid conflict and slow things down.

knife.ask: If the knife in your dream reminds you of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
knife.askQ: Should I say things plainly? Will anything move in the days ahead?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a knife mean I'll argue with someone?
faq.a: Folk belief links knives to quarrels, but that is only a traditional association and doesn't mean it will happen. It's more worthwhile to ask whether there's something you haven't said lately, or a decision you're stuck on.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of holding a knife?
faq.a: Common when you want to take the initiative on something or draw a boundary. If you felt decisive in the dream, it may reflect that you already have a direction. If you felt uneasy, you may still be hesitating over the decision.

gun.name: gun
gun.title: What does it mean to dream about a gun? Feeling threatened, staying guarded, and what you want to protect
gun.lead: Dreaming of a gun is often tied to feeling threatened, being on guard, or wanting to protect something. A gun is a weapon that works at a distance, so one in a dream may reflect pressure you feel about something lately, or a state in which you need to stay alert.
gun.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say little about guns, and versions differ a lot. One common reading takes holding a gun as wanting to control the situation and being prepared. Another says being held at gunpoint means being at someone's mercy or pressure closing in. Some versions see a gunshot as a sudden change. These are mostly traditional associations that vary by place, and shouldn't be taken as a forecast.
gun.plain: Gun dreams often come when you feel that something could hurt you: being watched at work, tension in a relationship, unsettling news, or a recent tense exchange with someone. Holding a gun may reflect wanting to protect yourself and stand your ground. Being held at gunpoint is common when you feel pushed or pressed to take a stand. Some people just watched an action movie or played a game, and the images slipped into the dream. When you wake, ask yourself: what did you most want to protect in the dream? That is usually what you really care about and fear losing lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a gun pointed at you
variants.a: Often tied to pressure or feeling forced during the day, such as being rushed, questioned, or expected to go along. Tradition speaks of being under someone else's control, but in real life it is usually just tension showing up in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of firing a gun
variants.a: It may reflect an urge to strike back or say things plainly. If you felt regret in the dream, it often comes from worrying that you reacted too strongly and hurt a relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of a missing gun or one with no bullets
variants.a: Common when you feel underprepared and unable to act at the key moment. It may also simply be that you've been tired lately, and the feeling of being stuck gets magnified in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of hearing gunshots
variants.a: It may correspond to a sudden change or piece of news that startled you, such as a last-minute notice or an unexpected situation. If you recently watched news or videos about it, it may just be leftover images.

variants.q: Dreaming of putting a gun away
variants.a: Often appears when you decide to avoid conflict and hold your feelings down. It may also reflect a wish to keep things from getting out of hand and slow things down first.

gun.ask: If the gun in your dream made you think of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days might bring movement.
gun.askQ: The matter that has been stressing me lately: how will it unfold from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a gun mean something bad will happen?
faq.a: Folk tradition links guns to conflict or sudden events, but that is only a traditional association and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. What's more worth looking at is whether you've been on guard and tense lately.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of holding a gun?
faq.a: Common when you want to protect yourself or take control of a situation, such as needing to take a stand or set a boundary. If you felt uneasy in the dream, you may have doubts about whether your reaction is too strong.

rope.name: Rope
rope.title: What does it mean to dream about rope? Connection, tugging, and not letting go
rope.lead: Dreaming of rope is often linked to connection, tugging, and not being able to let go. A rope is tied at one end and loose at the other. Seeing one in a dream may reflect that you're being held by a relationship or situation, or that you're thinking about how to loosen your grip.
rope.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ on rope. One common reading takes a tied rope as being tied down by matters or having worries on your mind. Another takes untying a rope as setting down a burden and things loosening up. Some versions see a broken rope as a connection being cut or a relationship changing. Copies from different places say different things, even opposite ones, so treat this as cultural reference only.
rope.plain: Rope dreams often come when you feel "tied down" by something: a relationship, a job, a decision you keep putting off. Tying things up or pulling on a rope in the dream may reflect a wish to hold on to or organize something. A knotted rope that won't come undone is common when things feel stuck and nothing you try goes smoothly. If the rope snapped, it may reflect that you're thinking of letting go, or worry that a connection will just disappear. Some people simply tied their shoes or tidied cords during the day and the image slipped into the dream. Notice whether you wanted to pull tight or let go in the dream. That is usually closest to how you feel now.

variants.q: Dreaming of a knotted rope you can't untie
variants.a: Often corresponds to a time when things feel stuck and nothing goes smoothly, such as a communication standoff or stalled progress. It may also reflect going over a decision again and again until it only gets more tangled.

variants.q: Dreaming of a rope breaking
variants.a: It may reflect that you're considering letting go, or worry that a connection has just been severed. Tradition speaks of a connection being cut, but in real life it's usually just inner tension.

variants.q: Dreaming of being tied up with rope
variants.a: Common when you feel bound by responsibilities, relationships, or expectations. If you wanted to break free in the dream, it may reflect a wish to regain your own space. If you felt at ease, it may be a feeling of being protected.

variants.q: Dreaming of tying something with rope
variants.a: Often appears when you want to hold on to or sort something out, such as settling a matter or clearing the air in a relationship. It may also simply be that you've been packing or organizing lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of pulling a rope or tug of war
variants.a: It may correspond to a tug-of-war with someone or something, such as a disagreement or being torn between options. If it felt exhausting in the dream, it usually relates to a situation that has been draining you lately.

rope.ask: If the rope in your dream made you think of a certain person or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which coming days might bring movement.
rope.askQ: The matter I keep not being able to let go of: will there be any movement on it?

faq.q: Does dreaming of rope mean being tied down?
faq.a: Folk tradition links rope to worries and restraint, but that is only a traditional association and doesn't mean it will happen in real life. What's more worth looking at is whether you've recently felt pulled along by some matter or relationship.

faq.q: If the rope broke in my dream, does it mean a relationship will end?
faq.a: Tradition speaks of a connection being cut, but a dream is not a prediction and it doesn't mean this will happen. A more useful reading is to ask whether you're already thinking of letting go, or feeling uneasy about a certain connection.

key.name: Key
key.title: What does it mean to dream about a key? Common symbols and states of mind
key.lead: Dreaming of a key is mostly linked to finding a way and opening up a situation. It often appears when you're trying to work something out, or when you finally feel you've found a thread. It may also reflect how much you care about whether you can seize a certain opportunity.
key.trad: A common view in folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) is that keys are tied to control, opening, and authority. Getting a key in a dream is read as a way forward opening up, while a key that breaks or gets lost is said to mean things are stuck or a lead has gone cold. Some versions link keys to the home and keeping valuables, saying a ring of keys means something at home needs attention. The versions differ, some stressing relationships, others money and belongings, and there is no single standard, so take it as cultural interest only.
key.plain: In daytime you may be at a stage where you know there's a door but haven't found the key: whether to apply for a job, whether to talk things through in a relationship, whether to make a decision. In dreams a key is often the symbol of that method or permission, so you might dream of it in your hand, in your pocket, or of never being able to find it. Some people have just changed locks, moved, or handled paperwork, and everyday details go straight into the dream. Often you already have an answer inside and are only waiting for a reason that lets you feel at ease.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding a key
variants.a: Often tied to a recent feeling of unexpectedly getting a clue or an opening, like when someone's offhand remark suddenly makes things clear. Finding something in a dream mostly reflects that you're hoping a turn for the better will show up on its own.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing your keys
variants.a: Common when something is half done and you suddenly feel unsure, such as when a plan gets thrown off or you worry you've missed a key step. It may also simply be that you really did look for something during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a big bunch of keys
variants.a: This may reflect having many things to manage at once: family, work, and relationships each hold a key. Not knowing which key opens which door often matches a daytime feeling of having too much on your plate and not being able to tell what matters most.

variants.q: Dreaming of handing your keys to someone
variants.a: Often linked to handing something over and trusting someone, or to hesitating over whether to let a certain person into your private matters. How you feel as you hand them over is worth more attention than the plot.

variants.q: Dreaming of a key breaking off in a lock
variants.a: Mostly shows up when you feel you're one step from getting there but stuck. Traditional sayings read it as something being blocked; in real life it's more a projection of frustration and doesn't mean the outcome is settled.

key.ask: If the key in your dream reminds you of a certain person, or of something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
key.askQ: Is there still a chance for things to turn around between him and me?

faq.q: Does dreaming that I can't find my keys mean there's no hope?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Traditional dream reading takes it to mean a lost lead, but in real life it more often reflects your anxiety and uncertainty right now. Look at whether something has been leaving you with no clue during the day; breaking it into small steps often helps more than interpreting the dream.

faq.q: What does it mean when someone gives me a key in a dream?
faq.a: A common association is that someone is willing to help you or open a path for you. It may also be that you wish a certain person would speak up or take a position first. The other person's expression and your own feelings in the dream usually say more about what you care about than the key itself.

door.name: door
door.title: What does it mean to dream about a door? Closed, open, and won't open
door.lead: Dreaming of a door usually has to do with whether to step through: a choice, a boundary, the entrance or exit of a relationship. Whether the door is open or closed often reflects whether you feel opportunity is open to you right now or blocked.
door.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common view is that an open door is read as a way forward and people coming and going; a closed door is said to mean matters are put on hold or contact with others lessens; a broken or fallen door points to change in the household or in relationships. Some versions link walking through a door with entering a home or adding a person. The versions differ quite a bit, and the same scene can even mean opposite things in different ones, so take it as cultural reference only.
door.plain: A door in a dream is often a stand-in for a boundary: whether to join this company, whether to let this person into your life, whether to say something out loud. If you're stuck at a point where you need to take a stand, a door easily appears: you hesitate outside it, the lock won't turn, or it suddenly swings open on its own. Some people have recently moved, changed offices, or are renovating at home, and those images naturally find their way into dreams. Commonly, how easily the door opens in the dream is close to how easy it feels to move that matter forward in daytime.

variants.q: Dreaming of a door that won't open
variants.a: Often matches a daytime feeling of powerlessness, of pushing and nothing moving, perhaps stalled communication or an application with no reply. The harder you push in the dream, the more it seems to reflect putting in a lot with no response.

variants.q: Dreaming of an open door with bright light outside
variants.a: Mostly appears when you feel there may be a chance, for example when someone shows goodwill or a new direction starts to emerge. The brightness in the dream is often a projection of your own hopeful mood.

variants.q: Dreaming of knocking and knocking with no one answering
variants.a: Common when you're waiting for someone to respond: a message, an answer, a clear stance. No one answering in the dream reflects the unease of waiting; it doesn't mean the other person won't reply.

variants.q: Dreaming of closing or locking a door
variants.a: May relate to wanting to protect yourself or wrap something up. If you've recently ended a relationship or a phase, locking a door in a dream is often your mind drawing a boundary and telling you it's okay to stop.

variants.q: Dreaming of many doors and not knowing which to take
variants.a: Often appears when you have too many choices, such as several jobs or paths laid out before you. The hesitation in the dream reflects fear of choosing wrong, not that any door truly can't be taken.

door.ask: If the door in your dream reminds you of a certain person, or of a decision you haven't made yet, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
door.askQ: Should I take this step with this decision?

faq.q: Is it bad to dream that someone else shut the door on me?
faq.a: Traditional sayings point to blocked contact, but in real life it more often reflects a worry about being rejected or left out. Think about whether a relationship during the day leaves you feeling ignored; saying how you feel plainly is often more practical than interpreting the dream.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of entering an unfamiliar house with many doors?
faq.a: A common association is that you're encountering a new environment, such as a new job, circle, or relationship, and are still figuring out the rules. The doors, one after another, are like you rehearsing in your mind which path will work.

window.name: window
window.title: What does it mean to dream about a window? Looking out, being seen, a window that won't close
window.lead: Dreaming of a window mostly has to do with watching and being watched: you want to see the world outside, or worry someone is looking at you. The view outside and whether the window is open or closed often reflect how far you feel from the outside world right now.
window.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common view is that an open window is read as news coming in and smooth dealings with people; a tightly shut window is said to mean things are stuffy for now, or distance from the outside world; a broken window points to gossip or small household matters. Some versions link leaning on a window looking out with waiting for someone or hoping for news. The versions vary, some leaning toward relationships and others toward the household, so enjoy it as culture and nothing more.
window.plain: A window in a dream is often your interface with the outside world: through it you see how others are doing, and sense how others see you. If you've been scrolling social media, watching coworkers get promoted, or watching friends travel, with a touch of comparison or envy, a window easily appears. Or you may just badly need some air, feeling stifled at work or at home and wanting to see what's outside. Commonly, you feel relaxed when the window is open, and safe but a little lonely when it's shut or the curtains are drawn.

variants.q: Dreaming of looking out a window
variants.a: Often matches watching a certain circle or person's life while feeling some comparison and longing. Whether the view is clear or blurry in the dream often relates to whether you feel it's within your reach.

variants.q: Dreaming the window won't close tight and wind keeps blowing in
variants.a: This may reflect a feeling that something is hard to hold on to: your privacy being known, your emotions being pulled around, or your workload seeping into the rest of your life. Closing the window in the dream can be a way of saying you want to draw your boundaries back.

variants.q: Dreaming someone is watching you from outside the window
variants.a: This often comes up when you care a lot about how others see you, such as being judged, being noticed, or fearing you won't perform well. The pressure in the dream mostly comes from what you expect of yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of smashing a window
variants.a: This often appears when feelings have built up to the point where you want to burst out. Traditional sayings tend to talk about quarrels, but in waking life it's more like an urge to break free or to speak plainly.

variants.q: Dreaming of a beautiful view outside the window
variants.a: This mostly reflects something you long for: a place you want to go, a life you want to live. The beauty in the dream is often a reminder from yourself of what you really want lately.

window.ask: If the window in your dream brings to mind a certain person, or something you've kept putting off, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
window.askQ: Should I keep waiting to hear from him?

faq.q: Is it bad to dream that it's very dark outside the window?
faq.a: Traditional sayings tend to talk about fortune, but in waking life it more often reflects that you can't see your direction right now, or feel a little uneasy about the future. Check whether something has been left unsettled during the day, and do what you can first. That usually feels steadier.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of cleaning or fixing a window?
faq.a: A common association is wanting to tidy up a relationship or situation: clearing up a misunderstanding, smoothing out your surroundings. Doing the work in the dream often reflects that you're ready to face the problem.

stairs.name: stairs
stairs.title: What does it mean to dream about stairs? Climbing up, going down, endless steps
stairs.lead: Dreaming of stairs usually has to do with progress: whether you're going up, going down, or stuck in the middle. It often shows up when you're checking whether you're moving forward, or worried about slipping backward.
stairs.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common saying is that climbing stairs is read as things progressing and your position rising; going down stairs is said to mean things slowing down, or watching your step; broken stairs, or stairs that never reach the top, are said to mean obstacles. Some versions also say endless stairs mean something weighs on your mind. The books differ quite a bit, and the same scene is weighted differently from one version to another, so treat it as cultural reference only.
stairs.plain: In dreams, stairs symbolize process: you know exactly which step you're on and how far there is to go. If you're in a stage that calls for building up, such as studying for an exam, waiting for a promotion, or a relationship slowly warming, stairs easily appear in your dreams. Tiring climbs often match a feeling that progress is slow; going down may mean you want to relax, or worry you're slipping back. Some people are simply climbing apartment stairs every day, and the physical tiredness carries into the dream. Often, how easy the stairs are to walk is close to how smoothly you feel things are going by day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tiring climb and not reaching the top
variants.a: This often matches a feeling that the goal is still far away and your energy is running low. Stopping to catch your breath in the dream reflects a need for rest, not that you can't get there.

variants.q: Dreaming of walking down stairs
variants.a: You may be wanting to slow down, or feel something is cooling off. If going down feels easy in the dream, it often means you want to set a burden down; if it feels frightening, it's usually worry about losing something.

variants.q: Dreaming of stairs that are narrow and steep
variants.a: This is common when the road ahead feels hard: few resources, little time, few people to rely on. The tension in the dream reflects how hard you expect it to be, not that you truly can't get through.

variants.q: Dreaming of stairs breaking
variants.a: Traditional sayings tend to talk about things being interrupted, but in waking life it's more like anxiety about progress being cut off, such as a sudden change of plans. How you react in the dream is worth more attention than the break itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of an escalator or spiral staircase
variants.a: This often appears when things seem to move on their own but you can't steer them well. A spiral staircase often matches a feeling that the path winds with no end in sight, and you're a bit impatient.

stairs.ask: If the stairs in your dream bring to mind a certain person, or a goal that hasn't moved forward, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.

faq.q: Does dreaming of climbing stairs forever without reaching the top mean failure?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Traditional dream reading talks about obstacles, but in waking life it more often reflects feeling the goal is too far, or expecting too much of yourself. Breaking the goal into a few steps and finishing the one in front of you usually eases things.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of falling down stairs?
faq.a: A common association is worrying that one misstep will undo all your effort, such as in a new job or a new relationship. The feeling of slipping is mostly imagination under pressure and doesn't mean it will happen.

elevator.name: elevator
elevator.title: What does it mean to dream about an elevator? Stuck, racing, can't press the floor
elevator.lead: Dreaming of an elevator is often tied to a feeling of rising or dropping fast: you want results sooner, or worry change is coming too fast to control. An elevator that sticks or jumps floors often reflects this sense of losing control.
elevator.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common saying is that riding an elevator up is read as things moving fast and a change in position; going down is said to mean things slowing, or watching your mood swings; a broken or stuck elevator is said to mean things stalling. Some versions also say being alone in the elevator means loneliness. The books differ, and elevators are a fairly recent thing, so many of these are associations added later. Take it as cultural curiosity.
elevator.plain: In dreams, an elevator symbolizes being carried along: you hardly need to make effort, but you can't quite control the direction or speed. If you're waiting for a result by day, such as an interview call, whether a project passes, or whether a relationship goes further, elevators easily appear. Pressing a floor and not stopping, or the doors opening on the wrong floor, often match a feeling that things aren't going as you planned. Some people are under work stress and ride an elevator to and from work every day, so those images naturally enter the dream. Often, how steady the elevator is matches how much you feel you can handle the matter by day.

variants.q: Dreaming of an elevator stuck with the doors not opening
variants.a: This often matches a feeling that something is stuck and can't move, such as waiting for a reply or an approval. The stuffiness in the dream reflects waiting anxiety, not that things are fixed in place for good.

variants.q: Dreaming of an elevator racing or dropping
variants.a: Most often it shows up when things feel like they're changing too fast to keep up with, like a sudden new assignment, or a relationship that warms up or cools down overnight. The weightless feeling in the dream is often the body's response to stress.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to press the floor you want
variants.a: Common when you feel you can't get where you want to go: you want to switch teams, move a relationship forward, or change how things are. All that pressing in the dream reflects how hard you've already been trying.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crowded elevator
variants.a: It may reflect being tied up in a lot of other people's needs lately, with coworkers, family, and friends all asking at once. The crowded feeling often matches a sense that your own space is shrinking.

variants.q: Dreaming of the elevator doors opening onto an unfamiliar floor
variants.a: It often comes up when you aren't ready for a new setting, such as a new role or a new relationship. That "wrong floor" feeling is usually your mind rehearsing uncertainty.

elevator.ask: If the elevator in your dream reminds you of someone, or of something you've been waiting on for a long time, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which coming days may bring movement.

faq.q: If I dream of an elevator dropping, does it mean things will get worse?
faq.a: Traditional sayings tend to talk about ups and downs in fortune, but in real life this dream more often reflects a worry about losing control, like fearing you'll perform badly or a relationship will change. Finding the one thing during the day that feels out of your grasp usually helps you feel steadier.

faq.q: What does it mean to be alone in the elevator?
faq.a: A common association is that you're going through something on your own, like carrying a project alone or handling things at home by yourself. The quiet in the dream may be space you need, or it may be a bit of loneliness worth noticing.

bridge.name: bridge
bridge.title: What does it mean to dream about a bridge? A broken bridge, crossing a bridge, can't find a bridge
bridge.lead: Dreaming of a bridge usually has to do with transition, connection, and whether you can get across. In dreams a bridge often stands for moving from one state to another, such as changing jobs, moving, a shift in a relationship, or a hurdle inside you.
bridge.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a bridge commonly stands for coming and going, and for change. Crossing smoothly is read as having a way forward, while a broken bridge or one you can't cross is described as being stuck. Older generations also treat a bridge as the link between two sides, so crossing with someone is said to mean your relationship with them is changing. The versions differ quite a bit: some stress direction (east or west), others the bridge's material. There is no single standard version, so it's best taken as cultural interest.
bridge.plain: This dream often appears when life is about to change: a new job, a move, the end of a relationship, a new project, or hesitation over whether to cross over. A bridge may also reflect how much you care lately about balancing two sides, like family and work, or your own wishes and others' expectations. How smoothly you cross says more about how sure you feel about the matter than about any result. If what you remember on waking is the water or the height below, that usually goes along with nervousness and a fear of slipping.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken bridge
variants.a: Common when a path suddenly seems closed to you, perhaps because plans changed or a relationship has a crack in it. Your reaction in the dream is worth more attention than the bridge itself: did you freeze, find another way, or ask someone for help?

variants.q: Dreaming of crossing a very narrow bridge
variants.a: This usually relates to a situation where you can only move forward carefully, such as limited resources, few choices, or one wrong word causing trouble. It's common in stressful times that call for caution.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding a bridge to cross the river
variants.a: It may reflect an eagerness to reach the other side without finding a way, such as wanting to settle something but having no channel to do it. It may also be that you haven't yet decided whether to cross.

variants.q: Dreaming of crossing a bridge with someone
variants.a: It often comes along with a change in some relationship, perhaps in a partnership, a romance, or the distance between family members. How near or far you are from each other in the dream is more interesting than the bridge.

variants.q: Dreaming of deep water under the bridge
variants.a: Common when something weighs on your mind and you fear one slip could make things spin out of control. The bigger the water, the more it resembles the intensity of the pressure you feel by day. It doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

bridge.ask: If a particular person appears in your dream, or you can't let go of something after waking, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which coming days may bring movement.
bridge.askQ: Can a bridge still be built between him and me?

faq.q: Is a broken bridge in a dream a bad omen?
faq.a: Some people traditionally make that association, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. A more useful way to see it: it often appears when a path feels uncertain, nudging you to look for an alternative route.

faq.q: Why do I often dream of crossing a bridge?
faq.a: If you happen to be in a transition, like changing jobs, moving, or a shift in a relationship, dreaming of crossing a bridge is very common. If it keeps recurring and you're sleeping poorly, consider talking with a doctor.

tunnel.name: tunnel
tunnel.title: What does it mean to dream about a tunnel? A long tunnel, can't get out, seeing light
tunnel.lead: Dreaming of a tunnel usually has to do with going through a stretch of road with no end in sight. In dreams a tunnel is like a passage you have to go through: your view is limited and you can only move forward, but there is an exit.
tunnel.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a tunnel is commonly seen as a "passageway." Going through one is read as things passing and a new stage beginning, while a tunnel that's too long or can't be exited is described as delay. Some versions also link tunnels with secrets, things not yet out in the open. There are many versions of these sayings, some looking at length and others at light or dark, and they don't agree with each other, so take them as cultural reference.
tunnel.plain: This dream often appears when you're in a period of just holding on: a project isn't finished, exams aren't over, a relationship is still settling in, or you're tired and not resting enough. A tunnel may also reflect feeling that your choices are shrinking and your view is narrowing, so you can only take care of the next step. Whether you see light, and how long you walk, says more about how this stretch feels to you than about any outcome. Some people dream of tunnels especially around the time pressure lifts.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tunnel so long it never ends
variants.a: Common when something has dragged on with no end in sight, like a long project or repeated rounds of talking things through. The tiredness in the dream usually builds up from the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of light at the end of a tunnel
variants.a: It often comes with a feeling of "almost through this." It may be that things are nearing an end, or that you've started telling yourself to hold on a little longer. It doesn't mean things will necessarily improve right away.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost in a tunnel
variants.a: It may reflect uncertainty about direction, such as not knowing whether to keep putting yourself into something. Whether you find the exit in the dream is more like a picture of how much in control you feel right now.

variants.q: Dreaming of a tunnel collapsing
variants.a: It often shows up when you're worried that something in progress will suddenly be cut off, like a plan changing or a relationship hitting a snag. Traditionally some people read more into it, but it doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of driving through a tunnel
variants.a: It usually has to do with feeling pushed forward, such as a schedule that forces you on, or a decision already made that you can only follow through. How fast the car goes in the dream often reflects how much pressure you feel.

tunnel.ask: If someone walks with you in the dream, or you can't let go of the matter, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
tunnel.askQ: How much longer do I have to keep going down this road?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of not being able to get out of a tunnel?
faq.a: Traditionally some people say things will drag on, but it doesn't mean that will happen in real life. It more often appears when you feel stuck and can't see progress, so it may be worth asking whether to adjust your pace.

faq.q: Is it normal to dream of a very dark tunnel?
faq.a: It's very common, especially when you're tired or your view of things feels limited. If these dreams keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

road.name: Roads
road.title: What does it mean to dream about a road? A long road, getting lost, a road that ends
road.lead: Dreaming of a road is mostly about a sense of direction and which path to take. In dreams, a road is often a miniature of the choices in your life right now: wide or narrow, straight or winding, open or blocked, it reflects how you feel about moving forward.
road.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly treat a road as your future and your progress. Dreaming of a flat, wide road is read as things going smoothly, with a way forward; a rough or broken road is described as obstacles. Some versions also look at who is walking with you to judge relationships. Versions differ on a road's width and direction, and there's no single reading, so it's best taken as cultural interest.
road.plain: This dream often appears when you have a choice to make: a career direction, whether to keep studying, whether a relationship should continue, or when your routine has been disrupted. A very long road with no end is common when your goal feels far away; getting lost often comes with not knowing what you want. A road that ends or is under construction may reflect a plan that feels stuck. Most of the time these are daytime concerns replaying at night, not a preview of an outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost
variants.a: It's common when you're unsure of your direction or have too many options. Whether you ask for directions, turn back, or push on says more about how you cope during the day than the getting lost itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of a road that never ends
variants.a: It mostly relates to a goal that feels far off or progress slower than expected, such as a long-term plan or something built up slowly. The tiredness you wake with often builds up during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a road that ends abruptly
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that a path has suddenly become unworkable, such as a plan changing or a relationship getting stuck. Traditionally some people read more into it, but it doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of walking on a very narrow road
variants.a: It's common in situations with limited choices where you need to be careful, such as tight resources, little time, or one wrong word causing trouble. It may also reflect being more sensitive to risk.

variants.q: Dreaming of walking with someone
variants.a: It often goes along with the state of a relationship, perhaps the distance between partners, family members, or colleagues being adjusted. Whether you're headed the same way in the dream is worth noticing.

road.ask: If someone walks with you in the dream, or you can't let go of the matter, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
road.askQ: Which direction should I head in next?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being lost mean I chose the wrong path?
faq.a: Traditionally some people make that connection, but it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. It more often appears when you haven't thought things through yet, so it can be a nudge to write out your options.

faq.q: Should I worry about dreaming of a road that ends?
faq.a: There's no need to take it as a forecast. This dream is common when something feels stuck, so first look at whether there's a real obstacle that needs handling.

car.name: Cars
car.title: What does it mean to dream about a car? Losing control, being driven, a broken-down car
car.lead: Dreaming of a car is usually about control and where you're headed. A car in a dream often stands for how you're moving things forward right now: who is driving and how smoothly it goes reflects how much of a lead you feel you have.
car.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly treat a car as movement and status. Dreaming of driving is read as holding the direction; a car out of control or with failing brakes is described as things getting beyond your grasp. Some versions also look at who is driving to tell whether you lead or are being led. Versions differ on the type and speed of the car, so take it as cultural reference only.
car.plain: This dream often appears while you're pushing something forward: work progress, a move, a relationship developing, or when life suddenly speeds up. Driving yourself is common when you feel you have to carry it alone; being driven by someone else may reflect leaving decisions to others or going along with their plans. Failing brakes or a runaway car often come with the pressure of not being able to keep up. A broken-down car may correspond to a step that feels stuck. Most of the time these are extensions of your daytime state, not forecasts.

variants.q: Dreaming of driving with failing brakes
variants.a: It's common when things feel faster than you can control, such as a pressing schedule or growing responsibilities. The tension in the dream is mostly a magnified version of daytime pressure.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone else driving you
variants.a: It may reflect handing your direction to someone else, or going along with the plans of a team, family, or partner. Whether you feel at ease or uneasy in the dream is worth noticing.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken-down car
variants.a: Often tied to a feeling that some part of a process is stuck, such as missing tools, not enough resources, or being tired. Some people traditionally read more into it, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stolen car
variants.a: Common when you feel control has been taken from you, or something is no longer your call. It can also reflect worry about losing something important.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost while driving
variants.a: Usually about uncertain direction, such as not knowing whether to keep investing in something. Whether you stopped to ask for directions in the dream can be more telling than getting lost itself.

car.ask: If someone was sitting in the passenger seat in the dream, or you can't let go of the matter, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
car.askQ: How much of this can I still keep in my hands?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of losing control of a car?
faq.a: Some people traditionally say things will go awry, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life. It more often shows up when you feel your load is beyond what you can handle. It may be worth asking whether it's time to slow down.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of being driven?
faq.a: Common when you've handed a decision to someone else, or are going along with someone else's plans. How comfortable you felt in the dream says more about your state than who was driving.

train.name: train
train.title: What does it mean to dream about a train? Riding one, missing one, and one passing your stop
train.lead: Dreaming of a train usually has to do with following a set route and a sense of time. In dreams, a train often stands for a rhythm that's hard to change on the spot: schedules, platforms, whether you get on. It reflects how you feel about progress and choices.
train.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly treat a train as a journey and a group moving together. Catching a train is read as keeping pace, while missing one is said to mean a lost chance or bad timing. Some versions look at who is traveling with you to read relationships. Versions differ quite a bit on trains, platforms, and delays, so take it as cultural interest.
train.plain: This dream often appears in periods with a clear timetable: commuting, exams, project deadlines, moving, or before and after a trip. Missing a train is often linked to worry about falling behind others or not keeping up. Boarding without knowing where you're going may reflect following a plan without being sure why. A crowded platform where you can't get on often goes with a sense of competition or limited resources. A delayed train may match a feeling that something is being put off. These are mostly extensions of your daytime rhythm, not predictions.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing a train
variants.a: Common when you worry about falling behind or missing an opportunity, such as when a deadline is near or everyone else seems to be moving ahead. The frustration in the dream is mostly daytime anxiety turned up.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding a train without knowing where it's going
variants.a: It may reflect times when you follow the plan but aren't sure of the goal. It could also mean you're going along with someone else's plan and haven't worked out what you want.

variants.q: Dreaming of a delayed train
variants.a: Often linked to a feeling that something is being put off, such as waiting for a reply, a result, or the other person to take a position. The sense of waiting is worth comparing with where things stand in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to squeeze onto a train
variants.a: Common in situations with strong competition and limited resources, like few spots or not enough time. It can also reflect a fear of being left behind.

variants.q: Dreaming of a train passing your stop without stopping
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that an opportunity or stage has passed too quickly to react. Some people traditionally read more into it, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life.

train.ask: If someone was on the platform in the dream, or you can't let go of the matter, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
train.askQ: Have I missed my moment for something?

faq.q: Is dreaming of missing a train a bad sign?
faq.a: Some people traditionally say it means a chance slipping away, but that doesn't mean it will happen in real life. It more often shows up when you're short on time or afraid of falling behind. It may help to check whether you're really in a rush.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming I can't catch the train?
faq.a: Don't take it as a prediction. This kind of dream is common when you feel chased by time or deadlines. If it keeps coming back and you aren't sleeping well, it's worth talking to a doctor.

airplane.name: airplane
airplane.title: What does it mean to dream about an airplane? Common readings and psychological clues
airplane.lead: Dreaming of an airplane mostly relates to a recent wish to get somewhere faster, or how quickly things seem to be moving. Traditional dream readings vary, but in real life it usually reflects how much you care about direction, speed, and control.
airplane.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that a plane taking off suggests things rising, while a plane landing is often said to mean an outcome or a wrapping up. Some versions link planes to travel and news, tying them to people or matters far away. Versions differ, some leaning toward travel and others toward career, and there is no single standard, so treat it as cultural reference.
airplane.plain: During the day you may be caught between wanting things faster and knowing you can't rush: waiting for a reply or a result, racing a deadline, or getting ready to change surroundings or travel far. Planes in dreams often come with speed and height, which may reflect a wish for things to become clear soon, or worry that you can't see the whole picture. If you felt calm in the cabin, you often feel fairly settled about what's coming. If you couldn't find the gate or missed the flight, it's more like built-up time pressure and fear of missing out. The dream itself doesn't mean anything will happen. What it points to is which matter you've been watching closely lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of an airplane taking off
variants.a: Often comes with a feeling of "it's about to begin," perhaps ahead of a new job, a new relationship, or a trip. How smooth the takeoff was mostly reflects your hopes and nerves about starting, not a forecast of the outcome.

variants.q: Dreaming of a plane crash
variants.a: This dream often appears when you're under heavy stress, have been reading a lot of news, or feel you've lost control of something. Some people traditionally link it to worry, but it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. It's more like daytime anxiety carrying over.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing a flight
variants.a: Common when you fear missing a chance, letting others down, or have a packed schedule. Running and never reaching the gate mostly reflects a feeling of being behind, not an actual loss.

variants.q: Dreaming of taking a plane abroad
variants.a: It may be tied to wanting to leave a familiar setting and get a change of mood, or you may simply have been planning a trip lately. If you felt excited in the dream, it usually means you're open to change.

variants.q: Dreaming of a plane flying low or circling
variants.a: This often comes with a feeling that something is left hanging, like waiting for a notice or for someone to say where they stand. A plane that keeps circling is more like that matter in your mind that hasn't landed yet.

airplane.ask: If a particular person was on the plane in your dream, or something keeps hanging over you and you can't let it go, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
airplane.askQ: Will I hear news about the matter that's been left hanging in the next few days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a plane mean I'm going on a long trip?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Folk sayings often link planes with long journeys, but more often the dream reflects how much you've been thinking about movement, change, or getting results sooner. Whether you're actually traveling depends on your plans in waking life.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming about missing a flight?
faq.a: Start by checking whether your schedule has been too full lately, or whether you're afraid of letting something slip. Try writing out your to-do list and splitting it into "must do today" and "can wait." If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

boat.name: boat
boat.title: What does it mean to dream about a boat? Reading your mood through the voyage
boat.lead: Dreaming of a boat is often tied to the feeling that you're in the middle of a process: whether your direction is steady, who is traveling with you, and when you'll reach shore. Traditional sayings vary, but in everyday life the dream more often reflects how you feel about progress and about who or what you rely on.
boat.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that a boat moving on water is read as things moving forward, with help from a benefactor, and a boat reaching shore is often said to mean a matter will settle. Some versions link the boat to getting through hardship, as a symbol of passing a test. Others look at the water: calm water means smooth going, rushing water means more twists. The versions don't agree, so take this as cultural reference only.
boat.plain: A boat often appears in dreams at a stage of being on the way and not there yet: a project half done, a relationship still finding its footing, or a new environment you're adjusting to. You may have been asking yourself lately, "Is this the right way to go?" or "Is anyone with me?" A steady boat and nice scenery often show up when you feel fairly at ease with where things stand. A leaking, rocking boat, or one that can't find shore, is more like uncertainty that built up during the day. Some people dream of riding on someone else's boat, which may reflect relying on a person or a decision. This kind of dream isn't a verdict of good or bad. What it can show you is whether what matters most to you right now is direction or companionship.

variants.q: Dreaming of a boat sinking
variants.a: This often appears when you're under a lot of pressure and feel something is about to be too much to hold. Traditionally some people link it to setbacks, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like the load in your mind is full.

variants.q: Dreaming of taking a boat out to sea
variants.a: It may be tied to wanting to leave a familiar setting, or to putting yourself into something with no visible end. Whether the sea is calm in the dream mostly reflects your confidence in this stretch of the journey.

variants.q: Dreaming of a boat reaching shore
variants.a: This is common when something is close to a result, or when you finally feel you can catch your breath. The feeling of reaching shore is more like your heart looking forward to a chapter closing.

variants.q: Dreaming of rowing a small boat
