variants.a: This often comes with a "take it slowly, on my own" feeling, such as handling something by yourself or carrying the responsibility alone. How smoothly you row reflects whether you feel you have enough strength.

variants.q: Dreaming of many people on a boat together
variants.a: It may reflect how much you've been thinking about your team, family, or some group of people. Whether everyone is of one mind in the dream often matches how you feel during the day about how well cooperation is going.

boat.ask: If someone on the boat in your dream stood out to you, or there's a stretch of the process you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
boat.askQ: Will this relationship move forward in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a boat mean I'm going to travel?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Folk sayings often link boats with travel and crossing water, but more often the dream reflects that you're in the middle of a process and feel strongly about direction and companions. Whether you go out depends on your plans in waking life.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of a boat that can't reach shore?
faq.a: Start by thinking about whether something lately has had no conclusion and has been leaving you in suspense. Try writing down separately "what I can decide" and "what I'm waiting on others for." If this kind of dream keeps coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

bicycle.name: bicycle
bicycle.title: What does it mean to dream about a bicycle? Pedaling easily or struggling
bicycle.lead: Dreaming of a bicycle is often tied to the feeling of moving forward on your own: whether you have enough strength, whether the road is smooth, and whether anyone is pedaling with you. Traditional readings come in different versions, but in everyday life the dream mostly reflects your recent sense of pace and independence.
bicycle.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that riding a bicycle is read as making progress step by step through your own effort, while a broken bicycle or one you can't pedal is often said to mean obstacles and a need to adjust your pace. Some versions also link bicycles with youth, lightness, and everyday comings and goings. The versions differ, some stressing effort and others social contact, so take this as cultural reference only.
bicycle.plain: A bicycle often appears in dreams in everyday scenes that still take effort: commuting, rushing, carrying someone, riding uphill. You may be holding something up on your own lately, or feel progress can only come bit by bit. Riding smoothly with a pleasant breeze often shows up when you're fairly happy with your own rhythm. A chain that slips, brakes that fail, or being unable to pedal is more like powerlessness or a fear of losing control built up during the day. Some people dream of being carried, which may reflect wanting to lean on others or accepting someone's help. This kind of dream isn't a prediction. It can remind you whether you want to do it yourself or want someone to help.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding a bicycle uphill
variants.a: This often comes with the feeling that things are hard work but still moving forward, such as being stuck at work or a relationship that needs tending. Whether you can pedal in the dream mostly reflects whether you feel you still have enough strength.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken bicycle
variants.a: This is common when something suddenly feels stuck, or when tools or resources aren't enough. Traditionally some people link it to obstacles, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bicycle being stolen
variants.a: It may reflect worry about losing something you rely on, or fear that your effort will be taken by someone else. Whether you get it back in the dream often matches how much you feel you're still in control during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of giving someone a ride on a bicycle
variants.a: This often shows up when you're looking after someone else or carrying other people's expectations. Whether the ride feels steady in the dream is more about whether you feel you can keep going.

variants.q: Dreaming of brakes that fail
variants.a: It's mostly tied to feeling you can't stop, for example when there's too much on your plate or you've said yes too often. The feeling of not being able to brake is often an extension of a day that's too full.

bicycle.ask: If the bicycle in your dream was carrying someone, or something has you pedaling hard and wearing you out, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
bicycle.askQ: How much longer do I have to carry this on my own?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a bicycle mean I should exercise or travel?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Folk sayings often link bicycles with daily comings and goings and with getting by on your own effort, but more often the dream reflects your recent pace and energy. Whether to exercise or go out is still up to how you plan your day.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming that I can't pedal?
faq.a: Start by looking at whether you've taken on too much lately, or keep feeling behind. Try breaking the most draining task into smaller pieces. If these dreams keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

motorcycle.name: motorcycle
motorcycle.title: What does it mean to dream about a motorcycle? Speed, freedom and risk
motorcycle.lead: Dreaming of a motorcycle is often linked to wanting to go faster or to feel freer, and to how you weigh risk. Traditional sayings vary; in waking life, the dream more often reflects your recent drive and your worries.
motorcycle.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that riding a motorcycle points to strong initiative and things moving quickly, while a motorcycle going out of control or falling over is often read as a caution against rushing and a sign that things may change. Some versions also link motorcycles with acting alone and running about. The versions differ, some stressing speed and others stressing running around among people, so treat this as cultural reference only.
motorcycle.plain: In dreams, motorcycles often appear in scenes of rushing, weaving through traffic, carrying a passenger, or speeding: hurrying to work, to an appointment, or trying to break free of something. You may want to push things forward quickly lately, or want space of your own. A smooth ride with the wind and a sense of freedom is common when you feel in control of your situation. Being overtaken, nearly crashing, or never finding a parking spot is more like impatience and fear of mistakes built up during the day. Some people dream of being a passenger, which may reflect wanting to relax and let someone else steer. This kind of dream doesn't mean anything will happen. What it can show you is whether right now you want speed or steadiness more.

variants.q: Dreaming of falling off a motorcycle
variants.a: This often comes when you feel you're moving too fast or are afraid of making a mistake. Traditionally some people link it with things changing, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. It's more like tension from the day carrying over.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stolen motorcycle
variants.a: It may reflect worry about losing your freedom to move, or fear that someone will take an opportunity from you. Whether you find the bike in the dream often matches how you feel about still being able to make your own decisions.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding a motorcycle with a passenger
variants.a: This often appears when you're carrying other people's expectations or want to look after someone. How steady the ride feels is more about how heavy you feel your responsibility is.

variants.q: Dreaming of speeding or riding very fast
variants.a: It's mostly tied to wanting results soon or wanting to shake off pressure. The more thrilling the speed in the dream, the more you may need an outlet during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding your motorcycle
variants.a: Common when you feel unsure of your direction or have lost momentum for a while. Searching for the bike over and over is more like looking for a reason to get moving.

motorcycle.ask: If the motorcycle in your dream was carrying someone, or something has you wanting to hurry, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
motorcycle.askQ: Should I speed up or slow down on this?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a motorcycle mean I should be careful in traffic?
faq.a: Folk sayings sometimes link motorcycles with running around and speed, but a dream isn't a warning. More practically, if you've been rushing a lot lately, it's wise to take extra care when riding or driving anyway.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of losing control while riding?
faq.a: Start by checking whether your schedule has been too tight or you keep trying to finish things quickly. Try deliberately leaving a stretch of time with no rush. If these dreams keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

bus.name: bus
bus.title: What does it mean to dream about a bus? Waiting, riding and following along
bus.lead: Dreaming of a bus is often linked to the feeling of following a set arrangement: whether the bus comes, whether you can get on, who you meet aboard. Traditional readings vary; in waking life, it mostly reflects how much you care about pace and having a choice.
bus.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that riding a bus means going along with the crowd and things proceeding step by step, while a bus that never comes or one you miss is often read as the timing not being right yet and needing to wait. Some versions also link buses with groups, social contact and daily running about. The versions differ, some stressing people and others stressing timing, so treat this as cultural reference only.
bus.plain: In dreams, buses often appear in scenes where you're not the one driving and must keep to a timetable: commuting, waiting, being squeezed in, missing your stop. You may be in a stage where you need to fit in with other people or a system, such as waiting for notice, waiting in line, or following a team. A bus that comes on time and a calm ride are common when you feel fairly at ease with things. Waiting forever, not being able to squeeze on, or missing your stop is more like anxiety and fear of missing out built up during the day. Some people dream of meeting someone they know on the bus, which may reflect how much a certain relationship or circle matters to you lately. This kind of dream isn't a prediction. It may simply remind you whether you care more about timing or about having a choice.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing the bus
variants.a: Common when you fear falling behind or holding things up. The feeling of the bus pulling away is more like feeling one step slow than actually losing something.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bus that never comes
variants.a: It may reflect waiting for a reply or an opportunity while time seems to crawl. Waiting and waiting in the dream often matches the helplessness of not being able to move yet during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crowded bus
variants.a: Common when you feel your space is being squeezed and you have to accommodate many people or rules. Whether you manage to get on is more about whether you feel you still have room to breathe.

variants.q: Dreaming of riding past your stop
variants.a: It's mostly tied to being absorbed in one thing and neglecting other plans. The panic of missing your stop is often an extension of a distracted day or an overfull schedule.

variants.q: Dreaming of running into someone you know on a bus
variants.a: It may reflect a relationship, or the dynamics within a certain circle, that has been on your mind lately. Whether the conversation felt pleasant in the dream often matches how you feel about that relationship during the day.

bus.ask: If the person on the bus in your dream stays with you, or you've been waiting on news that won't come, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
bus.askQ: When will the news I'm waiting for arrive?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a bus mean I'm going to travel?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Folk sayings often link buses with coming and going and with running around, but more often the dream reflects a stage where you have to go along with other people's arrangements and wait for the right moment. Whether to go out is still up to your plans in waking life.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming that I can't catch a bus that never comes?
faq.a: Start by looking at whether something has been left hanging lately that leaves you with nothing to do but wait. List what you can do while you wait, so you feel a bit more in control. If these dreams keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

phone.name: phone
phone.title: What does it mean to dream about a phone? Common dream readings and psychological observations
phone.lead: Dreaming of a phone usually has to do with contact, being sought out, and the amount of information coming at you. You may be wondering lately whether anyone is trying to reach you, or worrying about missing some news. Dreams like this usually reflect communication pressure from the day. They don't predict anything.
phone.trad: The folk dream books passed down in Chinese tradition (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't actually include a modern object like the phone, so the usual approach is to treat it as a stand-in for a letter, a message, or a doorway. One saying is that dreaming of receiving a letter means news from far away. Another sees communication tools as a symbol of connecting with people, so in the traditional reading, trouble with a phone in a dream suggests paying attention to your dealings with others. Versions differ a lot, and some simply say such new objects have no counterpart.
phone.plain: Phones are in our hands nearly all day, so it's very common for them to show up in dreams. The dream may reflect that you've been waiting for someone to reply, afraid of missing messages in a group chat, overwhelmed by work messages, or wanting to get back in touch with someone. A dead battery, a lost phone, or one that won't stop ringing often matches the daytime feeling of being chased or of fearing you'll lose contact. For others it's the reverse: they scroll too much during the day, and at night the brain carries those images into the dream. Think of it as a mirror of your mood, with no need to think in terms of good or bad luck.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cracked phone screen
variants.a: A common association is that something has gone wrong in communication: perhaps a misunderstanding with someone lately, or a worry that a wrong word can't be taken back. It may also simply be that you dropped your phone during the day and it stuck in your mind.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lost phone or not being able to find it
variants.a: This mostly relates to a fear of losing connection, perhaps worry about being left out of a circle, or fear that someone important will stop replying. It doesn't mean you will actually lose contact in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a phone that keeps ringing but you can't answer it
variants.a: This kind of dream often appears when your schedule is too full, reflecting the pressure of too many messages and not enough time to respond. You might think about whether something has been put off and left unhandled lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dead phone battery
variants.a: It often matches tiredness during the day, a feeling that you can't hold on much longer and need rest. Traditionally some read it as a pause in comings and goings, but it doesn't mean communication will actually be cut off.

variants.q: Dreaming of using someone else's phone
variants.a: It may reflect wanting to solve something lately through someone else's perspective or resources, or caring about who takes the initiative in a certain relationship. The characters in a dream are often a projection of your mood during the day.

phone.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
phone.askQ: Is there still a chance for me to get back in touch with that person?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a broken phone mean I'll lose contact with someone?
faq.a: Traditional dream readings have no such correspondence, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. What's worth noticing is your communication stress during the day: is there a relationship that feels stuck, where you can't say what you want to say?

faq.q: Should I worry if I keep having dreams about phones?
faq.a: Dreaming of them now and then is very ordinary. If these dreams keep coming back, cost you sleep, or leave you unsettled during the day, consider talking to a doctor, or first try cutting down on phone time before bed and see if anything changes.

computer.name: computer
computer.title: What does it mean to dream about a computer? Work and mental stress in dreams
computer.lead: Dreaming of a computer usually has to do with work, to-do lists, and a mind that won't stop running. You may have a lot going on lately, or be stuck on a problem you can't solve. It's an extension of your waking state, not an omen.
computer.trad: The folk dream books passed down in Chinese tradition (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have no word for a computer. The usual analogy treats it as documents, account books, or a tool. One saying is that dreaming of writing or accounts means something needs handling. Another says that a tool breaking down symbolizes things getting stuck. Some hold that such modern objects have no counterpart and you can only look at the feeling in the dream. Versions vary, so take them as reference only.
computer.plain: A computer stands for work and thinking, so the usual background to dreaming of one is a project nearing its deadline, a report you can't finish, a hard problem you keep working on, or something you're racking your brain over. A computer that crashes, runs slowly, or loses files often matches the daytime anxiety of being stuck and afraid of making mistakes. Some people simply used a computer for too long that day, and the images carry into the dream. If you're using the computer smoothly in the dream, your brain may just be sorting out what you learned that day. Think of it as a thermometer for stress, with no need to think in terms of good or bad luck.

variants.q: Dreaming of a computer crashing or the screen freezing
variants.a: It often matches a feeling of being stuck and unable to move, perhaps work progress has stalled, or a decision just won't come. It doesn't mean you will actually mess something up in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a computer virus
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that something has been disrupted by outside forces, or a worry about being influenced by others. For some, it's just that they took in too much noise during the day and feel scattered.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing files or lost data
variants.a: This is common when you're afraid of making mistakes or of wasting effort. You might think about whether something lately makes you feel your hard work could be for nothing.

variants.q: Dreaming of buying a new computer
variants.a: It mostly relates to wanting to do things differently or start over, perhaps wanting to change how you work, or having new plans for something. New things in dreams are often a projection of your mood.

variants.q: Dreaming of chatting with someone on a computer
variants.a: This may reflect a wish to talk to someone, or things you never said out loud in waking life. Conversations in dreams are often feelings left unfinished during the day.

computer.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or something keeps weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
computer.askQ: Will this stuck situation I'm dealing with start to loosen up?

faq.q: If I dream my computer breaks down, does that mean something will go wrong at work?
faq.a: Traditional dream books have no such link, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. What's more worth looking at is your recent work stress: is there something that keeps you tense, afraid of making a mistake?

faq.q: Does dreaming about a computer mean I'm too tired?
faq.a: It could. Computer dreams often come after long stretches of mental work or screen time. If you still feel very tired or sleep badly afterward, you can talk to a doctor, or leave some time before bed to step away from screens.

television.name: television
television.title: What does it mean to dream about a television? Do you want to unwind, or be seen?
television.lead: Dreaming of a television is often linked to watching others, being watched, or wanting to zone out. You may badly need rest lately, or care a lot about how others see you. Dreams like this mostly reflect the pace of your days, not a forecast.
television.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't mention television. Common analogies are the "stage," "watching a play," and "looking on." One view says dreaming of watching a play means observing other people's affairs; another says lively scenes symbolize social dealings. Some also see a glowing screen as a symbol of "drawing attention." Versions differ a lot, and some people think modern objects simply have no counterpart.
television.plain: Television is a medium for watching, so a common background to dreaming of it is that you badly need to zone out and be entertained, or you feel watched and judged. A broken TV, no signal, or endless channel-flipping in a dream often matches a daytime feeling of not finding the point and not being able to settle. If you were absorbed in a show, your brain may just be replaying what you watched during the day. Some people dream of TV as a reflection of the mood at home, such as it being very quiet or very noisy. Treat it as a clue about the rhythm of your life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a TV with no signal or static
variants.a: Often matches a feeling of being cut off or unable to grasp the point, perhaps because there's too much going on, or you feel you can't get through to someone. It doesn't mean you will lose anything in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of a TV that keeps changing channels
variants.a: May reflect that you can't settle, or that too many choices keep you from deciding. Think about whether something lately keeps changing direction and hasn't been decided.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken TV
variants.a: Common when you want to rest but can't stop. Traditionally some read it as "the bustle pausing," but it doesn't mean trouble at home in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of yourself on TV
variants.a: Mostly linked to wanting to be seen and fearing judgment. Perhaps something is about to be laid out before others and it makes you nervous. Being watched in a dream is often a projection of caring about others' eyes during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of watching TV with family
variants.a: Often appears when you miss time with family, or the mood at home is changing. The scene usually reflects how much you care about the relationship, not a prediction.

television.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or something keeps weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
television.askQ: Will the matter on my mind lately gradually become clearer?

faq.q: If I dream the TV breaks, does that mean something will happen at home?
faq.a: Traditional dream books have no such link, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. What's more worth noticing is whether you've been resting enough and whether the mood at home is worrying you.

faq.q: Does dreaming about a TV mean I want to relax?
faq.a: It could. TV dreams often come when life is fast-paced and you need some entertainment. If you still feel tired or sleep badly afterward, you can talk to a doctor.

clock.name: clock
clock.title: What does it mean to dream about a clock? Time pressure and waiting
clock.lead: Dreaming of a clock is usually linked to not having enough time, waiting for something, or fearing you'll be too late. You may be chased by deadlines lately, or be counting down to something you look forward to. It reflects the pace of your days, not an omen.
clock.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't mention clocks. Common analogies are the "water clock," the "double-hour," and "waiting." One view says dreaming of time-related things means something is approaching; another says stopped hands symbolize a matter being put on hold. Some versions see a chime as a reminder. Versions disagree, and some people think such objects have no counterpart and only the feeling in the dream matters.
clock.plain: A clock is a symbol of time, so a common background to dreaming of one is a deadline drawing near, waiting for a reply, fearing you'll run out of time, or a life that has been very regular and tense lately. A stopped clock, spinning hands, or a clock you can't find often match a daytime feeling of not having enough time and not catching the rhythm. Some people look at the time all day and then dream of clocks at night. If time passes very slowly in the dream, you may be waiting for something and finding the days hard to get through. Treat it as a mirror of time pressure, with no need to think in terms of good or bad luck.

variants.q: Dreaming of a stopped clock
variants.a: Often matches a feeling of things being paused or stuck in place, perhaps because something hasn't progressed or you're waiting for an answer. It doesn't mean time will really stop in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of clock hands spinning wildly
variants.a: May reflect a feeling that your rhythm is off, you can't keep track of time, or things have been changing too fast. Think about whether something has caught you off guard.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding a clock or not being able to see the time
variants.a: Common when you fear being late or missing out. It may also just be that you check the time too often during the day and stay tense.

variants.q: Dreaming of a clock ringing nonstop
variants.a: Mostly linked to feeling reminded or rushed, perhaps because someone keeps pushing you lately, or you keep pushing yourself. Sounds in dreams are often a projection of daytime pressure.

variants.q: Dreaming of buying or receiving a clock
variants.a: May reflect a wish to rearrange your time and take back the rhythm of your life. Traditionally some people avoid giving clocks as gifts, but that is just a saying passed down, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

clock.ask: If a particular person showed up in the dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead might bring movement.
clock.askQ: When will I hear news about what I've been waiting for?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a stopped clock mean time is running out?
faq.a: Traditional dream interpretation has no such link, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. What's more worth looking at is the time pressure you've felt lately: is there something that keeps making you feel you're running late?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a clock mean I'm too anxious about time?
faq.a: Possibly. Clock dreams often show up when deadlines pile up and your schedule is tight. If you still feel tense after the dream and aren't sleeping well, you could talk to a doctor, or give yourself a break from your schedule before bed.

book.name: books
book.title: What does it mean to dream about a book? Book dream meaning
book.lead: Dreaming of a book is often tied to learning, answers, and things you haven't finished reading. A book can stand for what you want to understand, and also for feeling that you're not yet enough and still preparing.
book.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have a few common sayings about books. One says that dreaming of reading or studying relates to career success and exams. Another says that a book falling or getting damaged may be linked to "a change in a matter." Some versions read receiving a book as "news is coming." These sayings vary from version to version, don't always agree, and involve a fair amount of stretching, so treat them only as reference.
book.plain: In dreams, a book often stands for "what you want to understand" and "what you demand of yourself." Searching for a book and not finding it is common when you're unsure about a decision and looking for an answer. Never finishing a book, or being unprepared for an exam, often appears when you feel you're not good enough or afraid of falling behind others. A very old or thick book may reflect something that calls for patience. Someone giving you a book often matches a wish for guidance, for someone to tell you what to do. Most of these are extensions of daytime feelings, not forecasts.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding a book
variants.a: Often matches not feeling sure about something, wanting an answer and not finding it. It may also mean you're hesitating over a decision. Whether you find the book in the dream reflects how certain you feel.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finishing a book
variants.a: Very common when you feel underprepared or afraid of falling behind, especially around exams or a new job. It doesn't mean things will actually go wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of a damaged book
variants.a: May relate to fear of things being broken or of effort being wasted. It could also simply be that you were sorting old books during the day. It doesn't mean something bad will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone giving you a book
variants.a: Common when you're hoping someone will guide you or give you direction. Whether you accept the book in the dream reflects whether you're open to others' input right now.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bookstore or library
variants.a: Often matches a period of looking for direction and wanting to see more options. Whether you browse comfortably or anxiously says a lot about how you're facing a choice.

book.ask: If the book in your dream brought to mind something you've long wanted to understand, or a decision you're hesitating over, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead might bring movement.

faq.q: If I dream of a broken book, will my exam go badly?
faq.a: Traditionally there's no such link, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. More often you feel pressure about how prepared you are, and the dream acts it out.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of studying constantly?
faq.a: It may reflect that you're learning something or preparing for something lately, or that you feel you're not enough yet. If such dreams keep coming back and cost you sleep, you could talk to a doctor.

pen.name: pen
pen.title: What does it mean to dream about a pen?
pen.lead: Dreaming of a pen is mostly about wanting to express yourself, to record something, or to make things clear. It often appears when you have something to say, matters to hand over, or a plan you're preparing.
pen.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have a few common sayings. First, a pen is seen as a symbol of documents, exams, and signing contracts; dreaming of writing with a pen is traditionally linked to "something to handle, a written record to watch." Second, dreaming of a broken pen or a pen that won't write is said by older generations to relate to "words not said clearly, a matter stuck." Third, dreaming of finding a pen is often said to mean "someone will ask for your help, news is coming in." Versions differ: some stress exams and careers, others stress human relationships and talk. Take it as a cultural saying.
pen.plain: During the day you may be holding back something you want to say, or have a lot to hand over or record, and a pen appears in the dream. You may also be preparing for an exam, writing, filling out forms, or negotiating a contract, with "write it down, make it clear" running through your mind. Commonly, you're afraid of missing something or saying the wrong thing, or you want to clear something up in a relationship but haven't spoken yet. A pen dream is more a nudge to notice "what you want to express" than a forecast of what will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of a pen that won't write
variants.a: Common when you're eager to explain something but feel you can't say it, or the other person isn't listening. It may also be that you have so much going on that you feel your expression can't keep up.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken pen
variants.a: May reflect worry that a conversation will break off, or that something will stall halfway through talks. Tradition often links it to documents and talk, but in real life it's usually just that you have such concerns during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding a pen
variants.a: Often appears when you've recently received a new task or news, or someone has asked for your help. It may also be that you want to start writing or recording something.

variants.q: Dreaming of many pens
variants.a: May mean you have a lot on your plate and much to hand over, and aren't sure which to handle first. Common during especially busy periods at work or school.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone handing you a pen
variants.a: Mostly relates to someone entrusting you with something or giving you a task. It may also be that you hope someone will give you a clear answer or instruction.

pen.ask: If the pen in your dream made you think of a certain person, or something not yet said clearly, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead might bring movement.
pen.askQ: Will I hear anything about the thing he and I never talked through?

faq.q: Does dreaming about a pen mean an exam or signing a contract is coming?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link pens with documents and academic success, but that's just a cultural association. What's more worth noticing in real life is whether you're actually preparing for an exam, filling out forms, or negotiating a contract. The dream may simply be bringing up what's on your mind during the day.

faq.q: Is it bad to dream of a broken pen?
faq.a: Some versions of folk dream books read a broken pen as communication not going smoothly, but the versions differ, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. A more practical way to look at it: is there something you haven't finished saying lately, or a conversation you're afraid won't work out?

umbrella.name: umbrella
umbrella.title: What does it mean to dream about an umbrella?
umbrella.lead: Dreaming of an umbrella often has to do with wanting to protect yourself, wanting some cover, or being afraid of getting soaked. It may also be that you've been holding something up for someone else lately, or that you hope someone will shield you for a while.
umbrella.trad: Folk dream books, including the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams, say more than one thing about umbrellas. Some see an umbrella as cover and shelter. A dream of holding one up is often linked to someone helping you behind the scenes, or to you guarding against something yourself. Others play on the fact that the word for umbrella sounds like the word for "scatter" or "part ways." A dream of dropping an umbrella or lending one to someone is then read by older generations as having to do with favors between people, and with coming together and drifting apart. Still others say that closing an umbrella or finding it broken means some kind of protection is gone. The versions contradict one another, so take them as cultural lore to consult, nothing more.
umbrella.plain: During the day you may be in a state of trying to look after yourself: afraid of making mistakes, of being dragged into something, of getting caught in other people's emotions. An umbrella in a dream often shows up when you're holding up some matter or relationship, or when you really wish someone would cover for you for a moment. It could also be small things like the weather, your commute, or whether to bring an umbrella that stayed in your head. Dreaming of an umbrella is more a reflection of your sense of security and your boundaries right now than a forecast of anything.

variants.q: Dreaming of walking with an umbrella up
variants.a: This often shows up when you've been protecting yourself, wanting to stay out of the fallout, or carrying a responsibility. It may also be that you're away from home and hoping everything stays steady.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken umbrella or one that won't open
variants.a: This may reflect a feeling that some protection isn't enough, or a worry that no one will help if something suddenly goes wrong. Traditional sayings often link it to cover being lost; in real life it's usually just this unease.

variants.q: Dreaming of lending an umbrella to someone
variants.a: This often appears when you've been helping someone or covering for them lately. It may also be that you're worried something you lent, or a favor you did, won't be returned.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding an umbrella
variants.a: This may mean you've recently received someone's care, or suddenly found something to lean on. It may also be that you're looking for a way to take care of yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of forgetting your umbrella
variants.a: This mostly relates to a fear of not being ready in time or of getting drenched. It's common when you have a lot going on and worry about missing something.

umbrella.ask: If the umbrella in your dream made you think of a certain person, or a relationship you're holding up, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
umbrella.askQ: Will someone help me with the matter I'm holding up right now?

faq.q: Does dreaming of an umbrella have something to do with parting?
faq.a: That's a folk association based on the similar sounds, and the circulating versions differ. In real life it doesn't mean you'll part ways or that things will fall apart. What's more worth looking at is whether you've been worried about a relationship lately, or afraid something can't hold up.

faq.q: Is it bad to dream of a broken umbrella?
faq.a: Some traditional versions say so, but they differ from one book to another, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. You can think of it as being especially sensitive lately to whether you have enough protection, with the dream acting it out.

bag.name: bag
bag.title: What does it mean to dream about a bag?
bag.lead: Dreaming of a bag often has to do with what you carry, what you shoulder, and what you're afraid of losing. It may be a responsibility or an identity, or a personal item or relationship that you care about a lot right now.
bag.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say a few things. One treats a bag as money and belongings, or luggage: dreaming of a full bag is traditionally linked to income or gains. Another says that dreaming of a lost or stolen bag relates to things not staying with you, and to taking care of your belongings. A third says that dreaming of a new bag is often read as a change of surroundings or status. The versions weigh things differently, some stressing money and others travel, so just treat them as cultural lore.
bag.plain: During the day you may be carrying a lot: responsibilities at work, things at home, or a relationship you look after, and in the dream it turns into a bag. It may also be that you've been going out a lot or changing places, or that you're really thinking about getting a new bag or sorting out your things. Commonly, you're afraid of forgetting something, losing something, or taking on too much. Dreaming of a bag is more a reflection of what you're carrying than a forecast of what will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing your bag
variants.a: This often shows up when you fear losing something important, which could be an object, a relationship, or a position. It may also be that you really have been forgetting things lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of your bag being stolen
variants.a: This may reflect a feeling that your belongings, credit, or privacy are being taken by others. Traditional sayings often link it to money, but in real life it's usually just this unease.

variants.q: Dreaming of a new bag
variants.a: This often appears when you want to change your surroundings, job, or role. It may also be that you've been sorting out your life lately and want a fresh start.

variants.q: Dreaming of a heavy bag
variants.a: This mostly relates to taking on too much. It's common in times when you're juggling many things and don't want to trouble others.

variants.q: Dreaming of a bag full of things
variants.a: This may mean you have a lot on your plate, with much to carry and look after, and you're not sure what to deal with first.

bag.ask: If the bag in your dream made you think of something you can't let go of, or a responsibility you're carrying, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
bag.askQ: Will the thing I'm carrying right now get a little lighter?

faq.q: Is dreaming about a bag linked to money?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often tie bags to money and belongings, but versions differ, and in real life it doesn't mean money will come in or go out. What's more worth asking is whether you've been worried about money lately, or about something you're afraid of not being able to hold on to.

faq.q: If I dream my bag is missing, will I lose money?
faq.a: Some folk versions say this, but the books differ, and in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. You can think of it as being extra sensitive lately to the fear of losing things, and the dream acting that out.

wallet.name: wallet
wallet.title: What does it mean to dream about a wallet? What does a wallet stand for in a dream?
wallet.lead: Dreaming of a wallet often has to do with whether you feel secure, whether you have enough, and whether you fear losing something. It isn't necessarily about money. It can also be a resource or a sense of backing that matters a lot to you right now.
wallet.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree about wallets. First, some treat a wallet as a "treasury": a full wallet is traditionally linked to income and a comfortable hand. Second, an empty or dropped wallet is something older generations link to "watch your money, expenses are heavy." Third, finding a wallet is often said to mean an unexpected windfall or favors exchanged between people. Some versions focus on fortune with money, others on gain and loss, so take them as cultural sayings for reference only.
wallet.plain: In waking life you may be calculating about money, resources, or "whether there's enough": bills, spending, pay, or something that needs paying for. You may also feel short on backing lately and worry you can't hold up. Commonly, you keep checking how much is left, fear missing something, or fear being taken advantage of. Dreaming of a wallet is more a reflection of how much you care about what you have in hand, not a forecast of gain or loss.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing your wallet
variants.a: Often seen when you fear losing some kind of security or backing, which could be money or a sense of safety. It may also be that you've really been searching for things or worrying about misplacing them.

variants.q: Dreaming of your wallet being stolen
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that your resources, credit, or privacy are being taken by others. Traditional sayings often link it to belongings, but in real life it's mostly just this unease.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty wallet
variants.a: Mostly to do with the fear of not having enough, often when expenses are heavy or you're working out a particular cost.

variants.q: Dreaming of finding a wallet
variants.a: Often appears when you're hoping for extra income, or when there have been favors and exchanges between people lately. It may also be that part of you wants a bit of unexpected good luck.

variants.q: Dreaming of a wallet full of money
variants.a: It may mean you feel more on top of money lately, or you're expecting some income. Traditional sayings often link it to a treasury, but in real life it doesn't mean it will come true.

wallet.ask: If the wallet in your dream made you think of a certain sum of money or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
wallet.askQ: Will this money matter of mine be settled in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a wallet mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Some traditional sayings link a full wallet to income, but versions differ, and in real life it doesn't mean you'll get rich. What's more worth asking is whether you've been calculating about money lately, or caring a lot about whether you have enough on hand.

faq.q: If I dream my wallet is missing, will I lose money?
faq.a: Some folk versions say this, but the books differ, and in real life it doesn't mean it will happen. You can think of it as being extra sensitive lately to the fear of losing your security, and the dream acting that out.

food.name: food
food.title: What does it mean to dream about food? What does food stand for in a dream?
food.lead: Dreaming of food often has to do with whether you've had enough lately, whether you feel full, and whether you're being looked after. It may be physical hunger, or it may be a wish for some satisfaction and comfort.
food.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say a few things. First, food is seen as "clothing, food, and harvest": eating your fill or a rich spread is traditionally linked to a settled life and being cared for. Second, spoiled food or food you can't eat is something older generations link to "things slipping away, look after your health." Third, someone treating you to a meal is often said to mean favors exchanged or good things coming to your door. Some versions focus on the household, others on the body, so take them as cultural sayings for reference only.
food.plain: In waking life you may be troubled about "whether there's enough": enough money, enough time, whether you're being looked after properly. You may also be eating at irregular times lately, or holding back from something you want to eat. Commonly, you're so busy you forget to eat, or you feel empty inside and want some comfort. Dreaming of food is more a reflection of your needs and sense of fulfillment right now, not a forecast of what will happen.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating a lot
variants.a: Often seen when you especially need comfort lately, or you've been too busy to eat properly. It may also be a longing for "a bit more" of something.

variants.q: Dreaming of spoiled food
variants.a: It may reflect a fear that something won't last, or a feeling that your hopes have come to nothing. Traditional sayings often link it to looking after your health, but in real life it's mostly just this sense of loss.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone treating you to a meal
variants.a: Often appears when you've had social contact lately, or hope someone will be a little kinder to you. It may also be that you want to be looked after.

variants.q: Dreaming of cooking
variants.a: Mostly to do with wanting to care for people and settle your life, often when you've been tending to your home or want your days to feel steadier.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to find anything to eat
variants.a: It may mean you feel your resources aren't enough, or you feel empty inside. Common when you've been busy and tired and feel you aren't being looked after well.

food.ask: If the food in your dream made you think of a certain person or something left unfulfilled, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
food.askQ: Will this empty feeling inside me ease a bit in the coming days?

faq.q: Is dreaming about food linked to money luck?
faq.a: Traditional sayings often link food to livelihood and harvest, but versions differ, and in real life it doesn't mean money is coming in. What's more worth looking at is whether you've been worrying lately about having enough, or whether you badly need to be taken care of.

faq.q: Is dreaming of spoiled food a bad sign?
faq.a: Some versions of the folk books link it to the body or the family's fortunes, but they disagree with one another, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen. You can think of it this way: you've been especially sensitive lately to hopes falling through, and the dream is acting that out.

fruit.name: fruit
fruit.title: What does it mean to dream about fruit?
fruit.lead: Dreaming of fruit usually has to do with a feeling of being close to harvest and wanting a taste of sweetness. It often shows up when you're waiting for something to bear fruit, or, the other way around, when you feel your effort hasn't been seen yet.
fruit.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several things. One treats fruit as results and harvest, so a tree heavy with fruit leans toward things making progress. Another goes by the fruit's condition: ripe, sweet fruit is read as smooth going, while rotten or sour fruit is said to mean hopes falling through. A third links eating fruit to enjoying good food and to social contact. The versions differ quite a bit, and even the same fruit is often praised in one copy and faulted in another, so take this only as a cultural reference, not something to believe literally.
fruit.plain: This dream often appears while you're waiting for a result: a case about to close, exam results about to be posted, a relationship that's still unclear. By day you say you'll let things take their course, but inside you keep tracking progress, and at night it comes out as fruit, the image of "is it ripe yet?" It may also reflect your recent eating or physical state, or a wish to treat yourself to a good meal. Commonly, the more you care about the outcome, the more vivid the fruit in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating fruit
variants.a: It often matches a wish to enjoy the results of your effort. You may need a little sweetness and rest right now, or you may simply have been thinking about food before bed.

variants.q: Dreaming of rotten fruit
variants.a: It mostly reflects worry about whether something is dragging on too long or might go bad. It's common when a deadline is near or progress is stuck.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of fruit
variants.a: It may mean you have several things waiting on results at once, or that you have so many choices you don't know which to take first.

variants.q: Dreaming of picking fruit
variants.a: It's often tied to reaching out and taking something yourself. It may reflect that you're getting ready to go after an opportunity, or weighing whether it's worth reaching for.

variants.q: Dreaming of giving fruit to someone
variants.a: It's common when you want to keep a relationship going or express your feelings but haven't spoken yet. It may also just be that you've had more social obligations lately.

fruit.ask: If you dreamed of a particular person, or there's something on your mind you can't put down, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
fruit.askQ: Will the matter on my mind have an outcome soon?

faq.q: Does dreaming of fruit mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Folk sayings often link fruit to harvest, but that's a symbolic association. In real life, money depends on your preparation and timing, and the dream itself doesn't decide anything for you.

faq.q: Is it normal to keep dreaming of fruit?
faq.a: Dreaming of it now and then is very common, especially when you're waiting on a result or your eating has changed. If these dreams repeat enough to affect your sleep, consider talking with a doctor.

rice.name: cooked rice
rice.title: What does it mean to dream about cooked rice?
rice.lead: Dreaming of cooked rice usually circles around the basics: whether life feels steady, whether you've eaten enough, whether the household has enough. It often appears when you're working out daily expenses or longing for stability.
rice.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several things. One treats plain white rice as having enough to eat and the family's foundation, so a full pot of white rice leans toward getting by comfortably. Another links eating to relationships and reunions, and the people at the table are often read as people you care about. A third says rice that's badly cooked or not enough means feeling uneasy inside. The versions don't agree on what "eating your fill" or "leftovers" mean, and some copies say the opposite, so treat this only as a cultural reference.
rice.plain: This dream often appears when you've been counting money or time, or when your routine has been thrown off. By day you may be too busy to eat properly, and at night a pot of rice reminds you to look after yourself. It may also be real pressures coming up: something at home, an older relative's health, rent and utilities. Commonly, the less steady life feels, the more vivid the rice in the dream, down to the dishes alongside it.

variants.q: Dreaming of cooking rice
variants.a: It often reflects that you're preparing for everyday life, perhaps planning expenses, arranging things at home, or wanting life to return to a routine.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating plain rice with no side dishes
variants.a: It may match a feeling of "enough, but not satisfied": life is fine, yet something seems missing.

variants.q: Dreaming of burnt rice
variants.a: It's common when you worry you'll mess something up, or you've been rushing so much lately that something gets neglected.

variants.q: Dreaming of many people eating together
variants.a: It mostly relates to your ties with family, coworkers, or friends. It reflects a wish to be supported, or concern about something in one of those circles.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty rice jar
variants.a: It often appears when you feel unsure about income or savings. It may also be that you've really been too frugal lately.

rice.ask: If a certain person appears in the dream, or something real is weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
rice.askQ: Will the living expenses I've been worried about get better?

faq.q: Does dreaming of cooked rice mean I'll be short of money?
faq.a: Folk sayings do link not enough rice to feeling uneasy, but that's only symbolic. In real life, finances depend on how you arrange income and spending, and a dream doesn't preview your account.

faq.q: Does dreaming about eating a meal mean someone will treat you?
faq.a: Some circulating editions read sharing a table as social contact, but that is an association. Whether a meal invitation actually comes still depends on how you usually make plans.

noodles.name: noodles
noodles.title: What does it mean to dream about noodles?
noodles.lead: Dreaming of noodles is often linked to things being drawn out, connected, or taking their time. It tends to show up when you're waiting for something to slowly come together, or when a relationship or a piece of progress feels stretched long.
noodles.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. One links the length of noodles to longevity and long-lasting affection, so long noodles lean toward a relationship continuing. Another links eating noodles to how smoothly things go, with unbroken noodles said to mean things connect well. A third reads mushy or broken noodles as something on your mind or something stuck. Editions across regions disagree about broken noodles, and some even give the opposite meaning, so take it as cultural interest only.
noodles.plain: This dream often comes when you're asking yourself "why isn't this over yet?" For example, a relationship left undecided, a project revised again and again, or waiting for a reply until you're worn out. By day you tell yourself there's no rush, and at night the stretched-out noodles act it out for you. It may also be that you've simply been eating a lot of noodles lately, or that you want some simple, hot comfort. A common pattern: the more you care about when there will be a result, the longer the noodles get in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating noodles
variants.a: Often matches a wish for something simple and easy to take in. Perhaps there's a lot going on and you just want to take care of one meal first.

variants.q: Dreaming of noodles breaking
variants.a: Mostly reflects worry that something won't connect, such as communication breaking off or a plan being interrupted.

variants.q: Dreaming of noodles clumped together
variants.a: Common when things feel tangled and you can't find the thread.

variants.q: Dreaming of very long noodles
variants.a: May relate to wanting something to last, reflecting how much you care about a relationship or a commitment.

variants.q: Dreaming of cooking noodles for someone
variants.a: Often appears when you want to look after someone or show you care, but haven't found a way yet.

noodles.ask: If there's a particular person in the dream, or something dragging on is wearing on you, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
noodles.askQ: Will things between him and me move forward?

faq.q: Is dreaming of broken noodles a bad sign?
faq.a: Some folk editions link broken noodles to things on your mind, while others read them the opposite way. It's only a symbol. In real life, whether things connect depends on how you handle them.

faq.q: Does dreaming of eating noodles mean a long life?
faq.a: Linking long noodles to long life is a folk association, a cultural saying. Health depends on your routines and check-ups, not on dreams.

meat.name: meat
meat.title: What does it mean to dream about meat?
meat.lead: Dreaming of meat is often linked to wanting, striving, and being satisfied. It tends to appear when you've been craving something lately, or feel you've given a lot and deserve something back.
meat.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. One sees meat as wealth and strength, so a big piece of meat leans toward having enough to eat and having resources. Another links eating meat to desire and satisfaction, said to mean there's a lot you want. A third reads raw or spoiled meat as something not yet dealt with. Editions differ widely on dividing meat versus grabbing it, and some even contradict each other, so treat it only as a cultural reference.
meat.plain: This dream often comes when you want something badly right now. It could be money, attention, a relationship, or just a good meal. By day you hold it back, and at night it shows up as meat, an image with weight. It may also reflect feeling shortchanged and wanting a bit of fairness back. A common pattern: the more you feel there isn't enough, the more the meat stands out in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating meat
variants.a: Often matches a wish to be satisfied. Perhaps you've been holding back too much lately, or you're simply hungry.

variants.q: Dreaming of raw meat
variants.a: Mostly reflects something not yet dealt with, still "waiting to cook," such as an undecided plan or an unclear relationship.

variants.q: Dreaming of sharing meat with others
variants.a: Common when you want to look after people or share a load, or are weighing how to divide resources.

variants.q: Dreaming of spoiled meat
variants.a: May reflect worry that an opportunity will go off if left too long, common when a deadline is near.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of meat
variants.a: Often appears when desire and pressure both grow at once: there's a lot you want, and a lot to handle.

meat.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there's something you want that hasn't settled yet, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
meat.askQ: Will I hear news soon about what I want?

faq.q: Does dreaming of meat mean good things to eat are coming?
faq.a: Folk tradition often links meat to food and resources, but that is a symbolic association. Whether there's good food in real life depends on whether you have plans.

faq.q: Does dreaming of raw meat mean something won't work out?
faq.a: Some circulating editions read it this way, but versions differ. It's more a sign of your impatience over something that doesn't feel "ready" yet than a conclusion.

egg.name: eggs
egg.title: What does it mean to dream about eggs?
egg.lead: Dreaming of eggs is often tied to something that hasn't hatched yet. It tends to show up when you have a plan or an idea taking shape, or when you're carefully protecting a relationship.
egg.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give several common readings. One treats the egg as nurturing and new beginnings, so a whole egg leans toward something starting to take form. A second links picking up or collecting eggs with accumulation and small gains. A third says a broken egg, with the yolk running out, reflects a fear that things will go wrong. Versions don't agree on broken eggs, though. Some manuscripts read it as an old matter ending. Take it as cultural interest only.
egg.plain: This dream often comes when you're holding something that isn't public yet, such as a new idea, a job that isn't settled, or a relationship that's still ambiguous. By day you don't dare make much noise about it, and at night it appears as an egg, an image that is fragile and full of possibility. It may also mean you've been especially careful lately, afraid of breaking something by accident. Commonly, the more you care about a beginning, the clearer the egg in your dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of picking up eggs
variants.a: It often matches finding a small opportunity, or wanting to gather scattered ideas together.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken egg
variants.a: It mostly reflects worry that something will go wrong, often at an early stage when you haven't found your footing yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of eggs
variants.a: It may mean you're incubating several ideas at once, or that you have more to look after lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of hatching eggs
variants.a: It often appears when you're patiently waiting for something to take shape, such as a reply or for someone to state where they stand.

variants.q: Dreaming of eating eggs
variants.a: It's often linked to wanting to take something in and make it your own. It may also just be that you had eggs for breakfast lately.

egg.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there's an idea in your mind that hasn't hatched yet, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
egg.askQ: Will this plan of mine, which hasn't taken shape yet, work out?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a broken egg a bad sign?
faq.a: Some folk versions link a broken egg to worry about things going wrong, while others read it as an old matter ending. It reflects what you care about, not a forecast.

faq.q: Does dreaming of picking up eggs mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Linking picking up eggs to small gains is a folk association, a symbolic reading. In real life, money still depends on your planning and preparation.

milk.name: milk
milk.title: What does it mean to dream about milk?
milk.lead: Dreaming of milk is mostly tied to feelings of nourishment, caring, and being needed. Traditional dream readings of milk differ: some point toward a settled, steady life, while others suggest watching the balance between what you give and what comes back.
milk.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on milk. One common reading sees milk as a symbol of nourishment and a harmonious home. Dreaming of drinking milk or having plenty of it is mostly read as a life without worry and a peaceful household. Another reading links milk to giving: spilled or spoiled milk is said to mean wasted effort or things not going as expected. Some versions file milk under goods and say dreaming of milk means a little money coming in. These readings contradict one another, and the same dream often gets different explanations in different editions, so take it as cultural interest only.
milk.plain: If you're looking after others by day, such as raising children, caring for older relatives, or covering for coworkers, or if you're always the one who gives first in a relationship, you're more likely to dream of milk. In daily life milk is something that nourishes people, so its appearance may reflect how much you're wondering whether you're being looked after, or whether you're giving too much. Some people dream of milk, bottles, or pouring milk when they're running a project at work and supporting a team under pressure. Another common case is that you've been adjusting your diet, losing weight, or feeling a bit tired, so you saw or thought about milk during the day and dreamed of it at night. That's quite ordinary. If the milk in the dream is warm and plentiful, it may match feeling more settled lately. If it's sour or spilled everywhere, it may match worry that something will turn out to be wasted effort.

variants.q: Dreaming of drinking milk
variants.a: Common readings relate to replenishment and being soothed. You may need rest or support lately, or you may be accepting someone's kindness and feeling warmed by it.

variants.q: Dreaming of spilled milk
variants.a: It mostly matches frustration from the day, like effort that went unseen or a plan that hit a snag. Spilling in the dream doesn't mean something will go wrong in real life. It's more like your mind working through that sense of loss.

variants.q: Dreaming of sour or expired milk
variants.a: It may reflect worry that a relationship or situation has gone bad. It may also be that you've been more sensitive about food or health lately and thought about it during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of milking
variants.a: It's often connected with giving and producing. You may be putting steady effort into something lately and wondering whether it's worth it.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of milk
variants.a: It may match feeling you have enough resources lately, or the reverse: feeling pressure because you have to share with many people. How you felt in the dream is a better guide.

milk.ask: If the milk in your dream reminds you of a specific person, or of something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
milk.askQ: Will my relationship with that person change in the coming time?

faq.q: Does dreaming of milk mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Folk tradition does link milk with wealth, but versions differ and there's no basis for it. A more practical approach is to ask whether you've been especially concerned about money or giving lately. The dream just acts out that concern.

faq.q: Should I worry if I keep dreaming of milk?
faq.a: Dreaming of it now and then is very common. If dreams like this keep recurring and leave you sleeping badly or unsettled by day, you can talk to a doctor about your sleep. There's no need to assume the worst on your own.

wine.name: alcohol
wine.title: What does it mean to dream about alcohol?
wine.lead: Dreaming of alcohol is often linked to relaxing, socializing, and letting emotions out. It can also reflect that you want to celebrate something, or avoid something. Traditional sayings about alcohol are mixed, and the versions differ quite a bit.
wine.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) disagree quite a lot about alcohol. One common view treats it as a sign of celebration, gatherings, and lively company: dreaming of drinking or a banquet is said to mean a busy social stretch or frequent contact with people. Another view ties alcohol to drunkenness and disorder: dreaming of being drunk or of spilled wine is read as saying the wrong thing or things getting out of hand. Some versions file alcohol under wealth and desire, saying a wine jar or wine vessel means money coming in or favors exchanged. The same cup can mean cheer in one version and embarrassment in another, so take it as cultural curiosity.
wine.plain: If you've had a party, a business dinner, or a meeting with people you don't know well, or you've been thinking "maybe I should have a drink to unwind," dreaming of alcohol is very common. In a dream, alcohol is often not about alcohol itself but about the feeling of loosening up. You may have been tense lately and want an outlet, or you may have just come from a lively event and the mood hasn't faded. Another case: you're dealing with something that calls for restraint, such as drinking less, holding your temper, or saying a little less, and alcohol shows up in the dream, which may reflect that inner tug-of-war. A happy, easy drink may match fairly good relationships lately; drinking until you lose control or can't find your way home may match a worry that something is slipping beyond your grasp. All of this points to your mood during the day, not a prediction.

variants.q: Dreaming of drinking alcohol
variants.a: A common reading relates to socializing and relaxing. You may need a breather, or you may be adjusting to a new setting or a new circle of people.

variants.q: Dreaming of being drunk
variants.a: This mostly matches a worry about losing control or saying the wrong thing, or being so tired you want to zone out. Being drunk in a dream doesn't mean you'll embarrass yourself in real life. It's more a reflection of stress.

variants.q: Dreaming of spilled alcohol
variants.a: It may reflect a worry about something you can't take back, such as words already said or money already spent. Or you may be especially sensitive to waste lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of other people drinking
variants.a: This often relates to how you see a certain person. You may have noticed someone close to you seeming relaxed or indulgent lately, and you have your own opinion about it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a lot of alcohol
variants.a: It may match a stretch with many occasions and social obligations, when you feel you can't keep up. Or you may be looking forward to a celebration.

wine.ask: If the alcohol in your dream reminds you of a certain person or a gathering that isn't over yet, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
wine.askQ: How will this matter develop from here?

faq.q: Does dreaming of alcohol mean good news is coming?
faq.a: Some folk sayings link alcohol with celebration, but versions differ and it isn't a prediction. A more down-to-earth view: you may be looking forward to relaxing or being with people, and the dream acts that out.

faq.q: Is dreaming of being drunk a bad sign?
faq.a: Traditionally some people read being drunk as disorder, but it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. First consider whether you've been tired or under stress lately. What you need may be rest, not worry.

cigarette.name: cigarettes
cigarette.title: What does it mean to dream about cigarettes?
cigarette.lead: Dreaming of cigarettes is often linked to habits, stress, and wanting to quit something. It may reflect how much you've been thinking about some kind of dependence, or it may simply be an impression left by the smell or sight of smoke during the day.
cigarette.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say little about cigarettes. They are a fairly recent thing, and many versions don't have the entry at all. In the few versions that include tobacco or smoke, there are two common views. One sees smoke as the flow of qi: curling smoke is said to mean something is still brewing and unclear. The other links lighting or offering a cigarette with social exchange, saying that being offered a cigarette means someone will come to strike up a conversation. Some versions link smoke with depletion, saying that smoking nonstop in a dream means your energy is being drained. These sayings come from scattered sources and differ a lot between versions, so take them as a curiosity.
cigarette.plain: If you smoke, dreaming of cigarettes may just be an extension of everyday scenes, especially if you've been thinking about cutting back or quitting. The more you think about it by day, the easier it is to dream of at night. If you don't smoke, cigarettes in a dream may relate to stress: in daily life a cigarette is often a symbol for catching your breath, and you may badly need a reason to stop and pause. Another common case is that someone around you smokes, or you've recently smelled smoke or seen related images, and the dream just pieces these together. If the cigarette won't light or keeps going out, it may match a feeling that something is stuck and you can't get any leverage. If someone hands you a cigarette, it may match going along passively with something in your relationships lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of smoking
variants.a: It may reflect that you need to relax lately, or that you're in a tug-of-war with a habit. If you don't normally smoke, smoking in a dream is mostly a symbol of stress, not a prediction.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone handing you a cigarette
variants.a: This is often related to relationships. You may be passively accepting someone's kindness or request lately, and feel unsure whether to take it.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cigarette that won't light
variants.a: This mostly matches a feeling of being stuck during the day, like things that won't move or words you can't say. A cigarette that won't light in a dream doesn't mean failure in real life. It's more a reflection of that stuffy feeling.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cigarette going out or throwing one away
variants.a: It may match wanting to end a habit or a relationship. Change is already brewing inside you, but you haven't acted on it yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of lots of cigarettes or smoke
variants.a: It may reflect that you have a lot on your mind lately and can't see which way to go. Or your surroundings may truly feel stuffy, and you want some fresh air.

cigarette.ask: If the cigarette in your dream reminds you of a habit or a person, you can cast a hexagram on that matter and see which days ahead may bring movement.
cigarette.askQ: Will I be able to break this habit?

faq.q: Does dreaming of cigarettes mean something is wrong with my health?
faq.a: No. Dreams don't predict health. If you've been coughing a lot, sleeping badly, or worrying about your body, it's more practical to talk to a doctor directly. You don't need to look for answers in a dream.

faq.q: What does it mean for a non-smoker to dream of cigarettes?
faq.a: Common readings relate to stress and wanting to relax, or to having come across the smell of smoke or related images during the day. Thinking about whether you've been especially tense lately will help more than analyzing the dream's details.

medicine.name: medicine
medicine.title: What does it mean to dream about medicine?
medicine.lead: Dreaming of medicine is often tied to wanting to be fixed, or wanting a problem solved. It may reflect something you've been dealing with lately, or a sense that you could use a little help or a small adjustment.
medicine.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on medicine. Some versions read taking medicine as a matter getting resolved, or someone helping. Others read bitter or hard-to-swallow medicine as a process that isn't easy. Others read searching for medicine, or running out of it, as feeling unsettled inside. The books differ, so treat all of this as folk reference only.
medicine.plain: In dreams, medicine is often a symbol of mending: when your body feels off you take medicine, and when something weighs on your mind you look for a way to fix it. So this dream often shows up when you're dealing with some trouble, at work, at home, or in a relationship, and you want it to get better soon. It may also be that you're really taking medicine or seeing a doctor, or someone close to you is unwell, and your daytime worry carries into the night. Whether you take the medicine smoothly, can't find it, or find it bitter often mirrors how solvable the matter feels to you in the daytime.

variants.q: Dreaming of taking medicine
variants.a: Common when you're dealing with something and hoping it improves soon. You may also really be taking medication, and the daytime routine carries into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to find medicine
variants.a: Usually tied to feeling unsettled or afraid of running out of time, for example worrying that something hasn't been handled well. It may also just be that you spent a long time looking for something during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of medicine that's bitter and hard to swallow
variants.a: Often appears when you feel you know what you should do about something, but doing it is hard. It may also be that you've been resisting taking medicine or seeing a doctor lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone giving you medicine
variants.a: It may reflect that you badly need someone to lend a hand or give you direction lately. It may also be that people around you keep caring for you, and you can feel it.

variants.q: Dreaming of dropped or spilled medicine
variants.a: Common when you worry that a fix won't work, or that your effort will be wasted. It may also simply be that you knocked something over during the day and the image stayed with you.

medicine.ask: If the medicine in your dream reminds you of a person or a matter you're dealing with, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
medicine.askQ: Will this matter be resolved smoothly in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of medicine mean something is wrong with my health?
faq.a: A dream can't be used as a health assessment, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. If this kind of dream keeps recurring and you're sleeping poorly, it's worth talking to a doctor.

faq.q: Does dreaming of taking medicine mean things will get resolved?
faq.a: Some traditional versions read it as a resolution or help arriving, but the books differ, and it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. A more practical view: notice whether you've been waiting for something to get better.

coffin.name: coffin
coffin.title: What does it mean to dream about a coffin?
