coffin.lead: Dreaming of a coffin often gives people a start, but it's usually about endings, closing a chapter, or transition, not a warning. Traditional readings of coffins are surprisingly varied, too.
coffin.trad: What the folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say about coffins differs from most people's instinct. One common reading links the word for coffin to the words for official post and wealth, so a coffin means a turn for the better or money coming in. Another sees the coffin as a wrapping-up: something is ending, or a stage is passing. Some versions say an open, empty coffin means you've let go of a worry. The versions differ a lot, and the same coffin can be read completely differently from one to the next. Take it as cultural color; it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.
coffin.plain: Many people wake up unsettled after dreaming of a coffin, but this dream isn't rare. It often comes when life is changing stages: a handover at work, a relationship coming to a close, moving, graduating, leaving a place you've been for a long time. In a dream, a coffin is more like a period at the end of a sentence than the end of everything. Another possibility is that you recently attended a funeral, saw related images, or are worried about an elder in the family, and it carried into your sleep. If you weren't afraid in the dream, it may reflect that you've already accepted something has ended. If you were very afraid and kept running, it may reflect that you aren't ready to face a change. Some traditions read coffins in a positive way, but that's a cultural reading and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of an open coffin
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been sorting through something old lately, and a worry is slowly loosening. An open coffin in a dream doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. It's more like you're letting go.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty coffin
variants.a: Often tied to something being over but not as frightening as you imagined. Maybe you've just finished dealing with something and feel lighter for it.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone in a coffin
variants.a: Usually tied to your concern for a particular person, especially if an elder, relative, or friend has been on your mind lately. The dream just acts out that concern.

variants.q: Dreaming of carrying a coffin
variants.a: It may reflect that you're taking part in wrapping something up, or that you feel a responsibility is heavy and shared. Whether you were a bystander or doing the carrying in the dream can change how it feels.

variants.q: Dreaming of many coffins
variants.a: It may reflect that you're facing more than one ending lately, one after another. It could also be that a certain occasion left a deep impression on you and carried into the dream.

coffin.ask: If the coffin in your dream reminds you of a person or something that has already ended, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
coffin.askQ: Do I still need to deal with this matter that has already ended?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a coffin unlucky?
faq.a: Traditional readings of coffins actually vary a lot, and some versions lean positive, but these are all cultural readings. In real life, dreaming of a coffin doesn't mean anything will happen, so try not to frighten yourself.

faq.q: Is dreaming of a coffin connected to death?
faq.a: No. Dreams don't foretell death. This kind of dream is usually about endings, transitions, or worry for someone. If it keeps disturbing your sleep or leaves you very uneasy during the day, you can talk to a doctor.

tomb.name: grave
tomb.title: What does it mean to dream about a grave? Common beliefs and a plain reading
tomb.lead: Dreaming about a grave is usually not a sign of anything bad. Traditional dream lore links it with endings, wrapping up, and letting go. In plain terms, it often reflects that you are saying goodbye to a stage of life, or that something in your heart hasn't really been put down yet.
tomb.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give a few common readings. First, seeing a grave means "a matter comes to an end": a relationship, a job, or a knot in the heart is wrapping up. Second, dreaming of paying respects at a grave is read as missing and caring about people or things that have gone far away. Third, a grave that cracks open or caves in is explained differently from version to version: some say it concerns an elder in the family, others say it is only a reminder to pay attention to small matters around you. The versions differ a lot, and even different copies of the same book often contradict each other, so treat this as cultural background, not a final answer.
tomb.plain: In plain terms, grave dreams often come right after something has ended: leaving a job, moving, a breakup, graduating, or a relationship slowly fading. It may also be that you've been thinking of someone who is no longer around, or of a "if only I had..." You have no time for it during the day, so it surfaces at night. It is more like tidying a drawer in your mind and putting old things away. It doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. If you weren't afraid in the dream, or even felt quiet, your feelings are usually just settling. If you panicked, you may be resisting the idea of an ending itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of being inside a grave
variants.a: A common reading is feeling trapped in some situation, such as being stuck in a relationship or a job, wanting to move but unable to. It may also be that you're very tired and long for quiet rest.

variants.q: Dreaming of visiting or paying respects at a grave
variants.a: This usually has to do with missing someone. It may be a relative who has passed away, or a time you can't return to. It's more likely to happen if an anniversary or related news came up during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of many graves, a whole field of them
variants.a: This often appears when you're under pressure and things are wrapping up one after another, and you feel there is "so much to deal with." It may also be that you've recently come across a lot of information about life, death, or aging.

variants.q: Dreaming of a grave cracking open or collapsing
variants.a: Traditional versions differ, and it doesn't mean anything will go wrong in real life. In plain terms, you may be worried that something already in the past will be dug up again, or feel uneasy about a coming change.

variants.q: Dreaming of crying beside a grave
variants.a: This often happens when feelings have built up for a long time and finally find a way out. Crying in a dream usually brings some relief. It shows you need a good release, not that something is being foretold.

tomb.ask: If a particular person appeared in the dream, or something in your heart keeps weighing on you, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
tomb.askQ: Am I still unable to let go of what has already ended?

faq.q: Is dreaming about a grave unlucky?
faq.a: Some people do link it that way traditionally, but that is only a cultural saying and doesn't mean anything will happen in real life. Most of the time it reflects that you are saying goodbye, wrapping something up, or missing someone or something.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming about graves?
faq.a: First, look at whether something has recently ended, or whether there has been a parting or someone you miss. If these dreams keep coming back and cost you sleep, you can talk with a doctor or someone you trust. They usually fade gradually.

temple.name: temple
temple.title: What does it mean to dream about a temple? Common readings of worshiping and entering a temple
temple.lead: Dreaming of a temple is traditionally linked with seeking peace of mind and finding direction. In plain terms, it often reflects that you have something on your mind to ask about, want something to lean on, or are hesitating over a decision. It has no direct connection to good or bad luck.
temple.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give a few common readings. First, entering a temple to worship is read as having a wish you hope to fulfill. Second, a solemn, bright temple is said to mean your mood will settle. Third, a closed temple gate or an empty temple is explained differently from version to version: some link it to distance from others, others say only that you've been lonelier lately. Different versions often explain the same scene in opposite ways, so take this only as cultural background.
temple.plain: This dream often comes when you "need an answer": whether to change jobs, whether to continue a relationship, whether to clear the air with family. In a dream, a temple is like a place where you can set judgment aside for a while, so you may dream of worshiping, lighting incense, drawing a temple lot, or just sitting in the temple courtyard, spacing out. Or you may have passed a temple often lately, or an elder at home mentioned going to worship, so it's on your mind. If you felt calm in the dream, your mind is usually just looking for a way out. If you were anxious and couldn't find the temple, you may not yet be clear about what you want to ask.

variants.q: Dreaming of entering a temple to worship, holding incense
variants.a: This is common when you have a wish or a worry and want reassurance. You may also actually be thinking of visiting a temple, so you thought of it by day and dreamed of it at night.

variants.q: Dreaming of the temple deity looking at you
variants.a: This usually reflects guilt or an uneasy conscience about something lately, a feeling of being watched. Traditional versions differ, and it doesn't mean anything will happen. What matters is what you care about inside.

variants.q: Dreaming of a temple festival or a lively temple
variants.a: This often appears when you long for liveliness and want to connect with people. You may also have recently attended a similar event or seen related images, and the dream replayed them.

variants.q: Dreaming of a run-down or empty temple
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that something you relied on is no longer reliable, such as a person or place you trusted having changed. Or you may be feeling lonelier lately and looking for a corner where you feel at ease.

variants.q: Dreaming of drawing a temple lot or asking about something
variants.a: This is common when you're stuck on a choice and wish someone would decide for you. Don't take what you drew in the dream seriously. The point is that you probably already lean one way and just haven't had the courage to admit it.

temple.ask: If what you asked about in the temple is also troubling you in real life, you can cast a hexagram about it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
temple.askQ: Which direction should I go with the decision on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a temple mean a deity is giving guidance?
faq.a: Some people think so traditionally, but that is a matter of personal belief and nothing is certain. In plain terms, it is more like your mind looking for direction and reassurance. The dream reflects what you yourself care about.

faq.q: Do I need to do anything after dreaming of worshiping at a temple?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If you already have a habit of worshiping, going for a visit does no harm. If not, there's no need to do anything special. It may help to think about what you were hoping to ask for in the dream. That is the real point.

church.name: church
church.title: What does it mean to dream about a church? Common readings of entering a church and weddings
church.lead: Dreaming of a church is traditionally linked with commitment, faith, and seeking forgiveness. In plain terms, it often reflects that you've been thinking about a commitment in a relationship lately, or that part of you wants a quiet place where you feel accepted.
church.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say relatively little about churches. Most of what circulates comes from Western dream traditions retold. First, dreaming of a church is read as seeking peace or forgiveness. Second, dreaming of getting married in a church is said to relate to commitment and responsibility. Third, dreaming of an empty church varies by version: some link it to loneliness, others say it's simply a wish to be alone. These views differ a lot, so treat them as cultural reference only.
church.plain: Church dreams often show up when you're facing the question of whether to commit: you've been together a while and are thinking about the next step, you're deciding whether to sign a long contract, or you agreed to something and now feel a little regret. In a dream, a church is a quiet, solemn space, so you may find yourself walking in, sitting down, hearing bells, or seeing stained glass. You may also have been to a wedding recently, watched a show about one, or have a practice of faith yourself. If the dream feels warm, it's usually just a wish to be held. If it feels stressful, it may reflect that you aren't ready for some commitment yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting married in a church
variants.a: This is common when you're thinking about the next step in a relationship, or when the idea of commitment is on your mind. It isn't necessarily about your current partner; it may be your own picture of, or worry about, marriage itself.

variants.q: Dreaming of church bells
variants.a: This mostly reflects a wish for a reminder or a rhythm, such as wanting a more regular routine. It may also be that you heard bells or saw related images recently and they showed up in the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of a church full of people
variants.a: This often appears when you long for a sense of belonging and want to be accepted by a group. It may also be that you recently attended a gathering or ceremony, and the lively crowd stayed in your mind.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dark, empty church
variants.a: It may reflect a feeling that something you relied on has drifted away, or that you've been lonelier lately. It could also be that you actually need time alone, and the dream clears a quiet place for you.

variants.q: Dreaming of confessing or praying in a church
variants.a: This is common when something weighs on your conscience and you want to tell someone. Speaking up in a dream usually brings some relief. It reflects a need to be understood, not a forecast of anything.

church.ask: If in the dream you were thinking of a certain person or commitment, you can cast a hexagram about it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
church.askQ: Does the promise between him and me still stand?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a church mean I'm going to get married?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Some people traditionally link churches with commitment, but a dream isn't a forecast. In plain terms, it's more likely that you've been thinking about a relationship or a responsibility, which may not be directly about marriage.

faq.q: Why dream of a church if I'm not religious?
faq.a: It's very common and doesn't mean you should take up a faith. You may have watched a show about one, passed a church, or wanted a quiet place where you feel accepted, and the dream borrowed that setting.

hospital.name: hospital
hospital.title: What does it mean to dream about a hospital?
hospital.lead: Dreaming of a hospital is mostly about wanting to be cared for or wanting to stop and rest. A hospital is a place of repair, and walking into one in a dream often means some part of you needs rest, or that you're worried about someone's condition.
hospital.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say that dreaming of a hospital is read in some versions as "pay attention to your health lately," and in others as "something needs handling or mending." Waiting for someone or visiting a patient in a hospital is often said to relate to worrying about that person. Versions differ: some stress health reminders, others stress concern for people. These are just the older generation's way of making associations.
hospital.plain: This dream often comes when you're too busy to catch your breath, or when you've recently accompanied someone to the hospital. It may also be that something "needs handling but keeps getting put off," and the dream uses a hospital to remind you. A hospital in a dream often matches the side of you in waking life that wants care and a break. Other common versions are waiting in line at a hospital, visiting a patient, or being the patient yourself. They mostly reflect tiredness and concern, not a forecast that someone will be in trouble. If such dreams keep recurring and you're not sleeping well, consider talking to a doctor.

variants.q: Dreaming of waiting in line at a hospital
variants.a: This often appears when you feel that everything involves waiting and progress is stuck. The image of a queue reflects a sense of waiting and powerlessness; it doesn't mean anything will happen in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of visiting someone in the hospital
variants.a: This mostly relates to worrying about someone. Have you been thinking about a family member or friend lately? The dream turns that care into a hospital visit.

variants.q: Dreaming of lying in a hospital bed
variants.a: This is common when you're really tired and wish you could let everything go and be looked after. It may also be that your body has been showing signs of fatigue, so remember to let yourself rest.

variants.q: Dreaming of a quiet, empty hospital
variants.a: It may reflect a recent feeling of having no one around and having to hold on by yourself. This dream often comes in stressful times when you don't want to trouble others.

hospital.ask: If the hospital in your dream made you think of someone, or something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram about it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
hospital.askQ: What should I deal with first right now?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a hospital mean something is wrong with my health?
faq.a: Some people traditionally make that association, but a dream can't give you a checkup. If you feel unwell, see a doctor. A dream is more likely reflecting your tiredness, your concern for someone, or a wish to rest.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of visiting someone else in the hospital?
faq.a: Folk reading usually takes it as worrying about that person; it doesn't mean they will get into trouble. More practically, ask yourself whether you've been thinking of them lately. A phone call to check in may settle your mind.

school.name: school
school.title: What does it mean to dream about school? Common readings of going back to school and taking exams
school.lead: Dreaming of school is traditionally linked with learning and being evaluated. In plain terms, it often reflects that you're facing some kind of test or comparison, or that you wish to return to a simpler state. It has nothing to do with good or bad luck.
school.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give several common views. First, dreaming of going back to school is read as having unfinished business on your mind. Second, dreaming of an exam is said to mean facing an evaluation and wanting to prove yourself. Third, dreaming of not finding the classroom or being late varies by version: some link it to anxiety, others say only that you've been tense lately. Versions often interpret the same scene differently, so treat them as cultural reference only.
school.plain: School dreams often appear when you're being evaluated: a review at a new job, a presentation coming up, or someone at home who has expectations of you. In the dream you may be looking for a classroom, rushing to an exam, or forgetting your textbook, all of which seem to reflect a fear of not doing well enough. It may also be that you recently visited your old school, met a former classmate, or that a child has started the school year, so it was on your mind by day. If the dream feels nostalgic, it's usually just missing simpler days. If it feels urgent, it may reflect that you've been under more pressure lately and worry about missing something.

variants.q: Dreaming of taking an exam or writing a test paper
variants.a: This often shows up when you're facing some kind of evaluation or comparison, like a work review or being closely examined. It can also be that you hold yourself to a high standard, and the dream gets nervous on your behalf.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding the classroom or being late
variants.a: Most often it reflects a fear of not keeping up or being left behind, such as falling behind on progress or not matching others. It can also be that your schedule has been packed lately and you feel constant time pressure.

variants.q: Dreaming of going back to your old school
variants.a: This often appears when you miss a certain period of your life or think back on who you were then. It can also be that you recently ran into an old classmate or passed your old school, and the image surfaced.

variants.q: Dreaming of attending class with classmates
variants.a: It may reflect a wish for companionship, for someone to work hard alongside. It can also be that you've been on a team lately, with lots of daytime interaction, so a similar scene turns up at night.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scolded or called on by a teacher
variants.a: This is common when you feel watched by someone or fear being rejected. Traditional sayings vary by version and don't mean anything will happen in real life. The point is whose opinion you care about.

school.ask: If the dream centers on a review or on how a certain person sees you, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
school.askQ: Will my performance this time be recognized?

faq.q: What does it mean to dream about taking an exam?
faq.a: Traditionally it's linked with evaluation and pressure, but a dream is not a forecast. In plain terms, it mostly reflects that you're facing some kind of test or comparison lately and feeling a bit tense.

faq.q: Why do I still dream about school long after graduating?
faq.a: It's very common and doesn't mean you want to go back to studying. You may miss simpler days, or you've recently met a similar "being judged" situation, and the dream borrowed school as its setting.

classroom.name: classroom
classroom.title: What does it mean to dream about a classroom? Common situations and psychological readings
classroom.lead: Dreaming of a classroom is mostly tied to the feeling of being watched and judged. You may be at a stage where you have to hand in results or be examined, and daytime tension carries into the dream, played out in a classroom setting.
classroom.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) say several things. One: the classroom stands for study and assessment, and dreaming of sitting in one is often read as something coming up that needs careful preparation. Two: dreaming of an empty classroom is said by some to mean you feel something is missing, like companions. Three: dreaming of not finding the classroom or going to the wrong one is often said to mean you're unsure of your direction. Versions differ, some stressing exams and others relationships. There is no single answer, so treat it as a reference only.
classroom.plain: A classroom is a classic "being examined" scene: someone is watching how you perform, whether it's a work presentation, an interview, an exam, or just being quizzed at a family gathering. The panic in the dream of "not ready yet," "can't find my seat," or "the teacher is about to arrive" is common when you have deadlines and grading standards in waking life. You may also be learning something new or have just moved into an unfamiliar environment and are still adjusting. Another common case is that you care a lot about someone's opinion, and the classroom simply stages that concern.

variants.q: Dreaming of not knowing how to answer the exam
variants.a: This is common when you have a clear deadline and feel underprepared. The panic of handing in a blank paper mostly reflects a fear of being compared, and doesn't mean anything will go wrong in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty classroom
variants.a: It may be linked to loneliness, or to feeling that no one around you understands what you're busy with. It can also be that you're in a phase where everyone is busy on their own with little interaction.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding the classroom
variants.a: Common when you've just changed environments or taken on a new task and don't yet have a clear sense of where to go or what to do. It's a normal reaction during an adjustment period.

variants.q: Dreaming of being called on by a teacher
variants.a: Mostly it relates to fear of being singled out or examined in public. There may be a meeting, a presentation, or a time you have to speak that's on your mind during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of being back in your school days
variants.a: Common when life is changing and you want to regain a simple sense of order. It can also be that you recently met an old classmate and old memories were stirred.

classroom.ask: If a certain classmate, a teacher, or that classroom keeps lingering with you, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
classroom.askQ: Will the matter on my mind lately start to move in the days ahead?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a classroom mean an exam or something is going to happen?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A classroom is just a ready-made scene the brain uses to act out "being examined," common in times with deadlines and grading. Take it as a nudge to check on your preparation.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of a classroom and can't sleep well?
faq.a: First look at whether something has been sitting unresolved during the day. If the dreams keep repeating and your sleep stays poor for a while, you can talk to a doctor. There's no need to scare yourself.

office.name: office
office.title: What does it mean to dream about an office? Overtime, coworkers, and stress in dreams
office.lead: Dreaming of an office usually relates to three things: responsibility, relationships, and boundaries. Work pressure, how you get along with coworkers, and that one thing you can't let go of after hours all easily replay in the dream as an office.
office.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ on workplaces. Some read the office as "position and responsibility," and dreaming of being busy at your desk is often said to mean you have something to shoulder soon. Others say an empty office symbolizes feeling unable to make an impact. Another saying is that dreaming of a conflict with a coworker means to watch your words. Versions emphasize different things, some career and some relationships, with no firm conclusion, so use it as a reference only.
office.plain: Office dreams most often appear in three situations: your workload suddenly increases and you keep thinking about work after hours; there's something unspoken between you and a coworker or manager; or you're considering a change of environment. Common dream scenes like "can't find the meeting room," "the computer crashes," or "being called into a small room" mostly match the daytime tension of "afraid of missing something" or "afraid of being singled out." It may also be that you've let your boundaries slip lately, replying to messages even during rest time, so naturally you're still at the office in your dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of working overtime until very late
variants.a: Common when your workdays run long, or when your mind won't switch off after you leave. The tiredness of working overtime in a dream is often your body reminding you to leave some room for yourself.

variants.q: Dreaming of arguing with a coworker
variants.a: It may relate to something you didn't say during the day, or a feeling of being misunderstood. Feeling lighter after the argument in the dream is common when a bit of resentment has built up inside.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scolded by your boss
variants.a: Often reflects how much you care about your performance, or a recent situation where you were being reviewed. It doesn't mean it will happen in real life. It's more a projection of the standards you hold yourself to.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty office
variants.a: Common when you feel you're carrying things alone, or the mood on your team feels cold and quiet. You may also be in a period of handover or switching teams.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to find your seat
variants.a: May relate to an unclear role, such as a new position or a new project you haven't got the hang of yet. A common dream during an adjustment period.

office.ask: If a certain coworker, boss, or work matter from the dream stays on your mind, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
office.askQ: How will things develop between me and that coworker?

faq.q: Does dreaming of the office mean something will go wrong at work?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The office is a ready-made setting, and the brain often uses it to act out daytime stress. Feeling tense in the dream usually just means you care a lot about how you're doing at work lately.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of being fired?
faq.a: Traditional sayings vary, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more common reading is that you feel insecure about your place, or you've been under pressure from being evaluated lately.

toilet.name: bathroom
toilet.title: What does it mean to dream about a bathroom? Readings for dreams of looking for a bathroom or a dirty bathroom
toilet.lead: Dreaming of a bathroom is often linked to wanting to relax, to clear things out, or to have a private space. Feelings you held in during the day, unfinished matters, or never finding time to catch your breath can turn into scenes like searching for a bathroom or finding one that's filthy.
toilet.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. First, the bathroom stands for release and cleaning out, so dreaming of cleaning one is often read as wanting to sort out the clutter in your mind. Second, dreaming of not finding a bathroom is said by some to mean something urgent is on your mind with nowhere to express it. Third, dreaming of a dirty bathroom is often read as feeling that something is unclean and wanting to avoid it. Versions differ a lot, some focusing on money and others on emotions, and there is no single reading, so take it as a reference only.
toilet.plain: Bathroom dreams often show up when you're holding things in: holding in urine, words, or feelings, or going several days without time to yourself. Not finding a bathroom, a broken lock, or a filthy room usually matches that daytime feeling of wanting to deal with something but being stuck. You may also have something you want to say clearly, but you haven't found the right time or person. Another common case is being in a stage where you need privacy, such as living with family or sitting in a very open office, and part of you wants a space where you can close the door.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to find a bathroom
variants.a: Common when you're really holding something in, or you have something urgent to say and no chance to say it. It may also be that your schedule has been so full you can't find a moment to breathe.

variants.q: Dreaming of a dirty bathroom
variants.a: May relate to wanting to avoid something, or feeling that a certain relationship is uncomfortable. Finding it disgusting in the dream often reflects wanting a bit more distance.

variants.q: Dreaming of a broken bathroom door lock
variants.a: Mostly relates to a sense of privacy and safety, such as feeling your space has been intruded on. It may also be that stress is high lately and even rest doesn't feel settled.

variants.q: Dreaming of being seen in the bathroom
variants.a: Common when you're afraid of being seen through, or of your private matters being discussed. Someone may have asked you a question during the day that you didn't want to answer.

variants.q: Dreaming of cleaning a bathroom
variants.a: Often read as wanting to tidy things up and start fresh. In real life you may be about to sort out a room, a relationship, or your state of mind.

toilet.ask: If the stuck, can't-clear-it feeling from the dream stays with you, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
toilet.askQ: When will that stuck matter on my mind start to loosen?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a bathroom mean I'll lose money?
faq.a: Traditional sayings vary, and it doesn't mean it will happen in real life. A more common reading is that you've recently felt a need to clear things out and relax, which may have nothing to do with money.

faq.q: Does dreaming of not finding a bathroom mean something is wrong with my body?
faq.a: A dream itself can't be used as a health judgment. But if you often dream of looking for a bathroom, check whether you're drinking a lot of water before bed or really holding it in often during the day, and talk to a doctor if needed.

kitchen.name: kitchen
kitchen.title: What does it mean to dream about a kitchen? Readings for dreams of cooking or a messy kitchen
kitchen.lead: Dreaming of a kitchen is often linked to caring, providing, and getting things ready. You may be busy looking after others and handling all kinds of tasks, or the reverse: you want someone to feed you a good meal and take care of you for a change.
kitchen.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) offer a few common readings. First, the kitchen stands for household livelihood and having enough to eat, so dreaming of lighting the stove and cooking is often read as something at home needing to be arranged. Second, dreaming of a messy kitchen is said by some to mean the clutter in your mind is piling up unsorted. Third, dreaming of an empty kitchen with empty pots is often read as the home feeling cold and quiet. Versions differ, some focusing on family and others on money and belongings, and there is no firm conclusion, so take it as a reference only.
kitchen.plain: Kitchen dreams often show up during a period of constantly giving: caring for family, raising children, organizing gatherings, or finishing up other people's work. Endless cooking, a messy kitchen, or not finding a pot usually matches that daytime feeling of things keep coming and I never get to sit down and eat. Another common case is that you've been wanting to be cared for lately but feel awkward asking, so in the dream someone cooks a whole table of food, or you keep waiting for a meal. Life may also be shifting, such as moving or changing homes, and the kitchen becomes a symbol of feeling settled.

variants.q: Dreaming of cooking for a lot of people
variants.a: Common when you're looking after a group of people, or tend to take everything on yourself. Bustling around in the dream may reflect that you're a bit tired but not good at saying stop.

variants.q: Dreaming of a messy kitchen
variants.a: This may have to do with having too many small tasks on your plate, or a living space that needs tidying. It can also mean several things are sitting in your mind at once, with no order set yet.

variants.q: Dreaming of a kitchen on fire
variants.a: Traditional sources give different versions, and none of them means something will actually happen. A more common reading is that your mood or schedule has been too full lately, and you feel an urgency, as if things are about to catch fire.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone cooking a meal for you
variants.a: This often shows up when you want to be taken care of or need a rest. It may also be that you recently accepted someone's help and felt warmed by it.

variants.q: Dreaming of an empty kitchen
variants.a: This may relate to feeling that home is quiet and cold, or that life has lost some warmth. It could also be that you just moved or changed surroundings and haven't settled in yet.

kitchen.ask: If the meal or the kitchen in your dream reminded you of a certain person or matter, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
kitchen.askQ: Will there be a turn for the better in that matter between me and my family?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a kitchen mean something is going on at home?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The kitchen is a ready-made setting for care and provision. A busy, chaotic kitchen in a dream usually just means you've been juggling a lot lately, not that anything will go wrong at home.

faq.q: Is dreaming of a kitchen fire a bad omen?
faq.a: Traditional sources offer various versions, and none of them means it will happen in real life. A more common reading is that your schedule or emotions are too full, and the dream is a reminder to leave some room to breathe.

bedroom.name: bedroom
bedroom.title: What does it mean to dream about a bedroom? Readings for rooms, beds and private spaces
bedroom.lead: Dreaming of a bedroom often relates to rest, privacy and intimacy. You may need a space where you can close the door, or something on your mind may only surface in your most private moments.
bedroom.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say a few things. First, the bedroom stands for privacy and security, and a tidy room is often read as feeling more settled inside. Second, a very messy room is said by some to mean worries piled up and left unsorted. Third, someone entering the room is often taken to mean you feel a boundary has been crossed. Versions differ, some focusing on relationships and others on family fortunes, and there is no settled answer, so treat it as a reference only.
bedroom.plain: Bedroom dreams often come when you want to rest but can't: scrolling before sleep, a mind that won't stop, or people constantly coming and going in your life. A room that gets broken into, a bed you can't find, or a room that feels strange usually matches a daytime feeling of having your boundaries crossed or of a space not feeling like yours. Another common case is that you're working through an intimate relationship or adjusting to a new living arrangement, such as moving in together, living apart or moving house, and the bedroom becomes a symbol of how settled you feel inside.

variants.q: Dreaming of a messy room
variants.a: This may relate to having too much going on, or a few things on your mind left unsorted. It may also be that your living space really does need tidying, and the dream simply brings the picture out.

variants.q: Dreaming of someone breaking into your room
variants.a: This is common when you feel your privacy is being invaded, or someone keeps asking about things you don't want to answer. Being intruded on in a dream usually reflects a wish to draw your boundaries more clearly.

variants.q: Dreaming of not being able to find your room
variants.a: This may relate to a sense of belonging, for example after a recent move or change of surroundings, or when a place no longer feels like home. It's a common dream during a period of adjustment.

variants.q: Dreaming of a room that feels strange
variants.a: This is common when life is changing or you're getting to know yourself again. A strange room in a dream doesn't mean you will lose anything in real life.

variants.q: Dreaming of lying in bed unable to sleep
variants.a: This usually reflects a head that's too full during the day and can't switch off before bed. It may also be that something has been left hanging lately, so your body has lain down but your mind hasn't.

bedroom.ask: If the room or the bed in your dream reminded you of a certain person or matter, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring some movement.
bedroom.askQ: Will there be any movement in that relationship on my mind?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a bedroom mean a change in my love life?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The bedroom often stands for privacy and a sense of being settled. What happens in the dream mostly reflects how you've been feeling about boundaries, rest or close relationships, and it isn't a forecast.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming that someone breaks into my room?
faq.a: First, see whether someone's behavior has made you uncomfortable during the day, or whether your space has felt too open and lacking in privacy lately. If the dream keeps repeating and you've slept poorly for a while, it's a good idea to talk with a doctor.

old-house.name: old house
old-house.title: What does it mean to dream about an old house? Common readings and how they match your feelings
old-house.lead: Dreaming of an old house mostly relates to familiarity, people and things from the past, and a sense of belonging. It often appears when you've been thinking about old times or when life is shifting, and it doesn't mean anything will happen.
old-house.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) commonly say a few things. First, the old house is seen as old people and old matters, and dreaming of it is often read as being reminded lately of past relationships or unfinished feelings. Second, the old home is seen as a foundation, suggesting thoughts about family, home or elders are surfacing. Third, some versions link a damaged old house with needing to tidy up your life. Versions differ and even contradict each other, so take it as cultural reference only.
old-house.plain: This dream often comes after you've come across old photos, passed the place you lived as a child, or talked with family about the past. It may also be that life is changing, such as a move, a new job or a shift in a relationship, and part of you is moving forward while another part looks back to check where you came from. A warm old house may reflect how much you value feeling settled. A dark, unfamiliar one, or one where you can't find the room, is common when you're a bit tired and feel some things are still unfinished. It's more like your mind sorting old files than a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of an old house that is run-down and about to collapse
variants.a: This often comes with a sense that some old matter or old relationship has loosened. You may be realizing that a part of the past needs to be let go, or that a habit no longer fits, and it doesn't necessarily have anything to do with an actual house.

variants.q: Dreaming of going back to your childhood home
variants.a: Most often it shows up when you're thinking about childhood or family, or when you've recently needed a sense of safety. The familiar smells and furniture in the dream are often the mind looking for a place to catch its breath.

variants.q: Dreaming of strangers in an old house
variants.a: Common when a familiar place has changed in ways you didn't expect, like a new member in an old circle of friends or a change at your family home, and you're still adjusting.

variants.q: Dreaming of looking for something in an old house
variants.a: Often reflects a search for answers or memories, or a wish to understand how an old matter came about. It can also be something from the day that you haven't been able to put down.

variants.q: Dreaming of buying or moving into an old house
variants.a: May be tied to a feeling of accepting a part of your past again, or of taking on a responsibility. It can also mean you're thinking about going back to a familiar place or circle.

old-house.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or an old matter keeps coming back, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
old-house.askQ: Will I hear anything about that old matter on my mind in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of an old house mean I'm going to move?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Dreams often reflect daytime moods and thoughts, so thoughts of moving or changing your surroundings can show up in them. But a dream isn't a schedule, so go by your actual plans.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of the same old house?
faq.a: Notice whether something has been coming up again and again in your thoughts lately. If the dream is keeping you from sleeping well or affecting your days, it's worth talking with a doctor, and writing down what's on your mind can help you sort it out.

new-house.name: New house
new-house.title: What does it mean to dream about a new house? Dreams of moving into a new home
new-house.lead: Dreaming of a new house is often linked to new beginnings, a wish for a change of scene, or hopes for the future. It usually reflects a change you've been planning or imagining lately. It doesn't predict wealth or a move.
new-house.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give several common readings of a new house. Some read a "new home" as a fresh look to life, or changes in your relationships or living situation. Others link it to family members, or to thoughts of settling down and building a career. Some versions connect a house being finished and moved into with things making progress. The versions differ quite a bit, so treat them as cultural reference only.
new-house.plain: This dream often comes when you're thinking about changing jobs, moving, renovating, or starting a new project, or when your relationship or family is entering a new stage. A bright, spacious new house may reflect your hopes for the future. An empty one that isn't finished yet is common when something is just beginning and you don't know how to arrange it. Some people dream of a new home when stress is high, as if the mind were finding a more comfortable space for itself. It's more like rehearsing a change than a guarantee.

variants.q: Dreaming of moving into a new house
variants.a: Often appears alongside the thought that life is about to look different. It could be a new setting, a new routine, or feeling ready for a new stage.

variants.q: Dreaming of a new house that's big and empty
variants.a: Common when you've just started something new and haven't found your footing. You feel hopeful, yet things still seem unsettled and need some time to take shape.

variants.q: Dreaming of a new house that leaks or isn't finished
variants.a: May reflect lingering doubts about a new decision, a feeling that the details haven't been handled well. In the daytime, you could go back and check the parts that make you uneasy.

variants.q: Dreaming of buying a new house
variants.a: Mostly linked to wanting stability and a space of your own. It may also be that you really are looking at homes or working out a budget, and the thought carried into the dream.

variants.q: Dreaming of other people in a new house
variants.a: Often comes when someone new has entered your life, such as a new colleague or relationship, and you're adjusting to the feeling that this space is no longer only yours.

new-house.ask: If the new house in your dream brings to mind a specific plan or person, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring some movement.
new-house.askQ: Will the new project I've been working on lately make progress in the coming days?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a new house mean I'll get rich?
faq.a: Some folk sayings make that link, but dreams aren't an indicator of fortune. A more practical clue is whether you're planning something new during the day, since that's where dreams often draw from.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a new house I can't move into?
faq.a: Common when you want a change but are held back by some condition, such as time, budget, or a relationship that isn't ready yet. You might think about which part makes you feel you can't get in.

ruins.name: Ruins
ruins.title: What does it mean to dream about ruins? Dreams of crumbling walls and wreckage
ruins.lead: Dreaming of ruins is often linked to feelings of endings, loss, and starting to sort things out again. It usually reflects something you're facing the end of or a change you're going through. It doesn't mean anything bad will happen.
ruins.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) don't agree on ruins. Some read crumbling walls as the past being over and a time to begin again. Others link them to thoughts of changes in people or surroundings. Some versions connect walking through ruins with sorting through the past. The versions differ from one another, so treat them as cultural reference only. They don't mean anything will happen in real life.
ruins.plain: This dream often comes right after a relationship, a job, or a stage of life has ended, or when you've recently heard that a place or a person has changed. Ruins in a dream are like a scene that has passed but is still standing there, and you may feel a pang of regret while knowing you can't go back. If you're searching for something in the ruins, it's common when you want to find something in past experience. If you're walking through calmly, it may reflect that you're slowly accepting a change. It's more like the mind tidying up than a prediction.

variants.q: Dreaming of searching for something in ruins
variants.a: Often reflects a recent wish to find answers or lessons in the past. It may also be that something old was never settled, and you keep looking back at it.

variants.q: Dreaming of people still living in ruins
variants.a: May be linked to some part of the past that you're still attached to, such as people or things in an old relationship or place that you can't quite let go of.

variants.q: Dreaming of ruins being rebuilt
variants.a: Often appears when you're putting something back in order and want it to work again, with the thought of repairing it in the back of your mind.

variants.q: Dreaming of frightening ruins and wanting to run
variants.a: Mostly shows up when you've been under more pressure lately and want to avoid certain old matters. Your reaction in the dream is often the same urge to get away that you feel during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of ruins turning into a lively place
variants.a: May reflect your hope that "there's still a turn for the better," or that you've recently seen a place or a relationship take on a new shape.

ruins.ask: If the ruins in your dream remind you of something that has ended but that you still can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which coming days may bring some movement.
ruins.askQ: Will anything change around the matter I can't let go of?

faq.q: Is dreaming of ruins unlucky?
faq.a: Some folk sayings make that association, but a dream is not a forecast. Ruins are often just a picture of daytime feelings about endings and change, and they don't mean anything will happen in real life.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of ruins over and over?
faq.a: Notice whether something has been left unfinished lately. If these dreams keep you from sleeping well or leave you uneasy during the day, you can talk with a doctor, and it may also help to write down what's on your mind.

market.name: market
market.title: What does it mean to dream about a market? Reading dreams of a street market and busy shopping crowds
market.lead: Dreaming of a market is often linked to dealings with people, choices, and everyday errands. It mostly reflects that you've been dealing with others, making decisions, or juggling many things in daily life lately. It doesn't mean anything special will happen.
market.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) give a few common readings of markets. Some read a market as lively relationships and lots of news. Others link it to buying and selling, gain and loss, and exchanging with people. Some versions connect getting lost in a market, or not finding what you're looking for, with having too many choices and feeling unsure. Versions differ, so take it as a cultural reference.
market.plain: This dream often comes when you've been more social lately, have a lot to coordinate, or are making a choice, such as comparing prices, picking something out, or deciding whether to agree to something. The noise and the vendors' calls are often an extension of too much information during the day. If you keep searching for a stall or can't find what you want to buy, it may reflect that you're not yet sure about a decision. Some people dream of a market when life is very routine and a bit monotonous, as if part of them wants to join the bustle. It's more a snapshot of everyday feelings.

variants.q: Dreaming of shopping at a market
variants.a: Often tied to a recent mood of making choices and weighing options, or to small matters in life that need your decision one by one.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crowded, packed market
variants.a: May reflect that you feel there's too much social contact or information lately, that you're being pushed along, and that you'd like somewhere to catch your breath.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost in a market
variants.a: Common when there are too many options and you don't know which way to go. During the day, try picking out the one thing you care about most and looking at that first.

variants.q: Dreaming of a market closing up, empty
variants.a: May be connected to a feeling that the bustle has passed and life has quieted down, or you may simply want more time alone lately.

variants.q: Dreaming of running into someone you know at a market
variants.a: Often appears when you're thinking of a friend, or may have a chance to reconnect soon. It may also be that you have something you want to say to someone.

market.ask: If the market in your dream brings to mind a specific person or a decision you haven't made yet, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which coming days may bring some movement.
market.askQ: Will I hear anything about that decision I've been facing?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a market mean losing money?
faq.a: Some folk sayings make that association, but a dream is not a financial forecast. More likely you had shopping, price comparing, or money on your mind during the day, and a market appeared in the dream.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a noisy market?
faq.a: It often reflects a stretch of more information or social contact, leaving you feeling a bit full. Notice whether too many things are running at once and need to be put in order.

station.name: train station
station.title: What does it mean to dream about a train station?
station.lead: Dreaming of a train station is often linked to being in a transition: about to set out, about to leave, or waiting for something to be settled. A station stands for change and waiting, and the scene mostly reflects how you feel about your next step.
station.trad: In folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams), a common view is that dreaming of a station or platform is read in some versions as travel or a journey far away, in others as linked to waiting or parting, and one version sees it as a sign that things are about to turn. Versions differ, some stressing the journey and some people and affairs, so it can't be taken as a verdict.
station.plain: A station often appears in dreams when life is about to change or you're waiting for news: a job change, a move, a shift in a relationship, or just a wish to get moving. If the station is bright and trains run smoothly, it often means you're looking forward to your next step. If trains are delayed or you can't find the platform, it may reflect a feeling that progress is stuck and you're a little anxious. This kind of dream is more a way of sorting out where you're headed than a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of waiting a very long time for a train at the station
variants.a: Common when you're waiting for a result lately, or feel that things aren't moving forward. The waiting in the dream is mostly something left hanging during the day, and doesn't mean real life will keep dragging on.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing the train
variants.a: May reflect worry that you're a step behind, or fear of losing an opportunity. Missing it in the dream doesn't mean you'll miss it in real life; it's just anxiety coming out.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost at a station and not finding the platform
variants.a: This often shows up when you haven't settled on a decision, or when there's so much information that you don't know which way to go. Being lost in a dream often looks like the hesitation you feel during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of seeing someone off at a train station
variants.a: Usually it has to do with parting or letting go. It may also be that you're getting used to someone not being around lately. Saying goodbye in a dream often reflects how reluctant you feel inside.

variants.q: Dreaming of a crowded, packed train station
variants.a: It may reflect that you've been pushed along by a lot of things lately and feel you have little say. A crowd in a dream is often what pressure looks like. It doesn't mean real life will get messier.

station.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or you're waiting on the outcome of something, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
station.askQ: Will there be any movement on the thing I'm waiting for in the days ahead?

faq.q: Does dreaming of a train station mean I'm going on a long trip?
faq.a: Not necessarily. In dreams, a station mostly stands for transition and waiting, and has no direct link to whether you actually travel. If you really are planning a trip, the dream is just playing the thought through.

faq.q: Does dreaming of missing a train mean I'll lose an opportunity?
faq.a: A dream can't predict real life. Dreams of missing a train often reflect the anxiety of fearing you'll be a step too slow. You might think about whether something lately makes you feel you're short on time.

airport.name: airport
airport.title: What does it mean to dream about an airport? Common symbols and states of mind
airport.lead: Dreaming of an airport usually has to do with standing at the doorway of a new stage: you're getting ready to set out, waiting for a result, or facing a time of change whose direction isn't settled yet. It reflects anticipation and unease side by side. It doesn't predict anything that will happen.
airport.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have no old entries for a modern setting like an airport. Later readers mostly compared it to "travel," "relay stations," or "ferry crossings." There are a few common readings. One is that being at an airport symbolizes change ahead, a long journey, or a new environment. Another is that missing a flight is read as obstacles or plans changing. A third is that a crowded airport symbolizes a busy social life and mixed opportunities. The versions differ a lot. Some stress "travel," others "waiting," and there is no single conclusion.
airport.plain: An airport is a place where you haven't really left yet, so this dream often appears when you're stuck in a transition: perhaps you've just handed in your resignation, are waiting for exam results or an interview call, are preparing to move, or have a relationship that hasn't been talked through. The announcements, boarding gates, and weight of luggage often match the daytime tension of fearing you'll miss something or pick the wrong gate. Some people experience the reverse: life has been very comfortable lately, yet in the dream they keep wanting to fly, reflecting an itch to move that hasn't been acted on. Commonly people dream of getting lost in an airport, not finding the gate, or losing a passport. These mostly come with self-doubt about being unprepared, and don't suggest that anything will really go wrong.

variants.q: Dreaming of missing a flight
variants.a: This is common when you're worried an opportunity is slipping away, or a deadline is close. Missing it in the dream reflects the daytime anxiety of running out of time. In real life there is usually still room to make up for it.

variants.q: Dreaming of being lost in an airport and unable to find the gate
variants.a: Mostly this matches a choice in front of you when you don't yet have the full picture. It may be about work direction, school, or moving. The dream makes the feeling of not knowing which way to go concrete.

variants.q: Dreaming of losing your passport or ticket
variants.a: Often it relates to fearing you aren't qualified enough or forgot something key, such as before an interview or a presentation. It reflects tension while preparing, and doesn't predict failure.

variants.q: Dreaming of a major airport delay and waiting and waiting
variants.a: This is common when you've already worked hard but are still waiting on a result. The waiting in the dream matches the daytime helplessness of being stuck and unable to move.

variants.q: Dreaming of seeing someone off on a plane
variants.a: Mostly it relates to separation. It may be a friend going far away, a relationship cooling, or you leaving a stage of life behind. The dream is helping you work through the reluctance to let go.

airport.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there's something you can't let go of, you can cast a hexagram on that matter to see which days ahead may bring movement.
airport.askQ: Will the matter I'm stuck on make progress in the days ahead?

faq.q: Does dreaming of an airport mean I'm going on a long trip?
faq.a: Not necessarily. In dreams an airport is more a symbol of transition and doesn't necessarily match real travel. Most of the time it reflects that you're in a period of change, not that a trip is coming.

faq.q: What if I keep dreaming of rushing for a flight or missing it?
faq.a: Dreams like this are often tied to deadline pressure, so first look at whether something lately makes you feel you can't put it off. If it keeps recurring and you aren't sleeping well, you can talk with a doctor. There's no need to frighten yourself.

prison.name: prison
prison.title: What does it mean to dream about prison? Where the feeling of being locked in comes from
prison.lead: Dreaming of prison is usually not a mysterious omen. It's more that during the day you feel restricted: perhaps work ties you down, a relationship does, or you've set too many rules for yourself. The dream turns that feeling of being unable to move into images of iron bars and a cell.
prison.trad: The folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have quite a few entries on "prison," but the versions contradict one another. Common readings include: dreaming of being locked in a cell symbolizes being trapped or controlled by others, or something weighing on your mind; dreaming of being released after serving time is read as pressure lifting and a turn for the better; dreaming of visiting a prisoner or bringing prison meals symbolizes concern for someone in a difficult situation. Some versions read prison as "self-restraint," stressing that it's a reminder rather than a prediction. Accounts differ, so treat them only as cultural reference.
prison.plain: Prison dreams most often appear when you feel you have few options: responsibilities at work weigh on you, family expectations do, you don't dare speak honestly in a relationship, or money leaves your hands tied. Some people lock themselves up: they could refuse but keep saying yes, and in the dream that becomes a cell. Common images are an iron door closing, no way out, or looking outside through bars. These mostly match the daytime stuffy feeling of wanting to move but being unable to. On the other hand, dreaming of escaping or being released often comes when you're trying to loosen things up, or have finally decided to change. These dreams have most to do with the feeling of freedom. They don't suggest you will really run into trouble.

variants.q: Dreaming of being locked in prison
variants.a: This is common when you're tied down by some responsibility or relationship and feel you have no choice. The dream reflects a sense of being restricted, and in real life there is usually room you haven't seen.

variants.q: Dreaming of a prison break or escaping from prison
variants.a: Mostly it matches that you want to break free of a situation, or are already weighing a change. The dream acts out the wish to be free. It doesn't mean you will do something impulsive.

variants.q: Dreaming of visiting someone in prison
variants.a: It often has to do with concern. You may be worried about a friend or family member, or part of your own feelings may be locked away and unspoken.

variants.q: Dreaming of being wrongly accused and locked up
variants.a: Often seen when you feel misunderstood or treated unfairly. Protesting your innocence in the dream reflects the hurt of having "no way to say what's weighing on you" during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a prison that is bright and not frightening
variants.a: Sometimes it reflects that you have actually accepted a certain limit, and may even find routine reassuring. The dream shows your mixed feelings about "structure."

prison.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there is something you can't let go of because it's stuck, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
prison.askQ: When will the thing I'm stuck on start to loosen?

faq.q: Does dreaming of prison mean trouble is coming soon?
faq.a: It's not a forecast. Prison in a dream mostly stands for the feeling of being restricted, which relates to your daytime stress or the demands you place on yourself, not to something that will happen in real life.

faq.q: If I dream of being locked up, is something wrong with me?
faq.a: There's no need to think that way. These dreams are common and usually tied to recent stress or a strong sense of responsibility. If it keeps coming back and affects your sleep, you can talk to a doctor.

graveyard.name: cemetery
graveyard.title: What does it mean to dream about a cemetery? Endings, remembering and starting over
graveyard.lead: Dreaming of a cemetery is mostly about "endings" and "remembering": a relationship has come to a close, a stage of life has passed, or you are still holding someone in your heart. These dreams often appear around times of transition and reflect a mood of sorting things out and saying goodbye. They are not a forecast.
graveyard.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) differ quite a lot on cemeteries and graves. Common versions: first, walking into a cemetery stands for old matters being settled and it being time to look ahead; second, sweeping a grave or making offerings stands for remembrance, care, or family ties; third, a quiet, sunny graveyard is read as a settled state of mind. Some versions read a cemetery as "something hidden," a reminder to watch for old business left unresolved. Tradition has a great deal to say about dreams of the dead and of graves, but in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen, and the versions often contradict each other.
graveyard.plain: Cemetery dreams often come right after something has ended: graduating, leaving a job, a breakup, a move, or a long relationship slowly fading. You may not have had time to feel sad during the day, so at night the dream walks you to the graveyard and plays out the feeling of "it's over." Some people have been missing someone who is no longer near, and headstones, photos or old belongings appear in the dream. That reflects longing, not something bad. It's also common to dream of getting lost in a cemetery or being chased, which usually matches old feelings from the day that haven't been dealt with. On the other hand, a cemetery full of flowers and calm often shows up when you are gradually letting go and getting ready to move on.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting lost in a cemetery
variants.a: Often matches a time when an old stage has ended and the new direction isn't clear yet. Being lost in the dream reflects the uncertainty of the in-between.

variants.q: Dreaming of sweeping a grave or making offerings to a relative
variants.a: Mostly tied to remembrance and care, especially if someone important has recently left or a relationship has changed. The dream helps you express longing you didn't voice during the day.

variants.q: Dreaming of a grave being opened or moved
variants.a: Often seen when you are going back over an old memory, or something you thought was past has been brought up again. It reflects "facing it again," not a forecast.

variants.q: Dreaming of a cemetery that is beautiful and quiet
variants.a: Often appears when your mind is settling and you are slowly accepting something. The calm in the dream matches the daytime feeling of "finally being able to let go."

variants.q: Dreaming of being chased into a cemetery
variants.a: Mostly tied to unresolved stress or old feelings; the dream gives shape to the feeling of "can't escape." In real life there is usually still time to face it at your own pace.

graveyard.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or there is something you haven't been able to let go of, you can cast a hexagram on it to see which days ahead may bring movement.
graveyard.askQ: Should I keep waiting for the person I can't let go of?

faq.q: Is dreaming of a cemetery unlucky?
faq.a: Tradition has many sayings about cemeteries, but in real life they don't mean anything will happen. Most of the time the dream reflects the mood of an ending, missing someone, or a transition. It's not a forecast.

faq.q: What does it mean to dream of a late relative standing beside a grave?
faq.a: Often seen when you have been missing that person lately, or are going through a change connected to them. The dream is an extension of longing. Traditional sayings vary, and in real life it doesn't mean anything will happen.

being-late.name: being late
being-late.title: What does it mean to dream about being late? The anxiety of missing out and running out of time
being-late.lead: Dreaming of being late is almost always about "fear of not making it": fear of missing a chance, letting people down, or not keeping up. It reflects time pressure and a sense of responsibility built up during the day. It doesn't predict that you will really drop the ball.
being-late.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating versions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have no very old entry specifically for "being late." It is mostly filed under "travel blocked" or "rushing on the road." Common versions: first, missing a ride or being late stands for obstacles and falling behind; second, being late with nobody blaming you is read as the pressure not being as heavy as it seems; third, being late because you can't find the way stands for an unclear direction. Versions differ quite a bit, some stressing "obstacles," others "a reminder," so take them only as cultural reference.
being-late.plain: Dreams of being late most often come when your schedule has been too full: clocking in, meetings, school pickups, deadlines. You rush all day, and at night the dream keeps rushing. There may also be someone you "can't be late for," such as a strict boss or family expectations, and in the dream you keep checking your watch or can't find the way. Common scenes are being unable to run, losing your shoes, or an elevator that won't come. These mostly match the daytime helplessness of "being in a hurry but stuck." On the other hand, dreaming of being late but arriving in the end often shows up when you actually know you can cope. These dreams relate most to your sense of time and responsibility.

variants.q: Dreaming of being late for work or school
variants.a: Often seen when you have been tense about a regular responsibility and worry you aren't doing enough. The dream reflects stress, not a forecast that you will slip up.

variants.q: Dreaming of rushing for a train or plane and never making it
variants.a: Mostly matches a worry about missing an opportunity or deadline. The "one step short" feeling in the dream is daytime anxiety turned up.

variants.q: Dreaming of being late and nobody noticing
variants.a: Sometimes it reflects that something is weighing on you more than you think, and people around you haven't noticed. It may also be saying it's not as serious as you imagine.

variants.q: Dreaming of being unable to run, legs feeling heavy
variants.a: Often shows up when you feel behind and can't do much about it. The dream turns that frustration of wanting to go faster and not being able to into a picture.

variants.q: Dreaming of being scolded after being late
variants.a: Usually has to do with a fear of letting someone down, maybe a boss, family member, or partner. The dream shows how much you care about being judged. It doesn't predict a scolding.

being-late.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or you can't put down the thing you're afraid you won't finish in time, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
being-late.askQ: Is there still time for the thing I'm most worried about missing right now?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being late mean I'll make a mistake soon?
faq.a: No, it isn't a warning. Dreams about being late mostly reflect worry about time and responsibility. They point to pressure during the day, not to something that will happen.

faq.q: What should I do if I keep dreaming of missing a ride?
faq.a: Start by checking whether your schedule has been too full or you haven't been resting enough. These dreams are common. If they keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, you can talk to a doctor.

missing-exam.name: being late to an exam
missing-exam.chip: Dreaming of being late to an exam
missing-exam.title: What does it mean to dream about being late to an exam? The feeling of being judged
missing-exam.lead: Dreaming of being late to an exam usually has to do with a fear of being tested: fear of not being prepared enough, of doing badly, of slipping up at a key moment. It reflects how much you care about evaluation and results. It doesn't predict that something will go wrong with an exam or at work.
missing-exam.trad: Folk dream books (such as the many circulating editions of the Duke of Zhou's Book of Dreams) have entries on exam scenes from the imperial examination era, mostly pointing to status and competition. Common sayings include: dreaming of being late to an exam or missing it stands for being underprepared or having opportunities blocked; dreaming of not finding your seat in the exam hall stands for an unsettled position or unclear direction; dreaming of not being able to answer the questions is read as insecurity or heavy pressure. Some versions also read exam dreams as a reminder that you hold yourself to high standards. Versions differ, and none of this means anything will happen in real life.
missing-exam.plain: Exam dreams are special: many people still have them years after leaving school. They often appear when you face some kind of grading situation: a performance review, an interview, a proposal, meeting someone's parents, or even just your own expectations of yourself. Being late, not finding the exam room, or losing your admission ticket in the dream mostly matches the daytime tension of being afraid you're not good enough. Some people have just taken on a new task and feel they're about to be tested even though no one is pushing them. Other common versions are a blank exam paper, or the bell ringing before you've finished. These reflect worry during the preparation period, not a hint about the outcome. On the other hand, dreaming of being late but getting into the room in the end often comes when you actually feel confident.

variants.q: Dreaming of being late to an exam and missing the entry
variants.a: Common when you're worried about performing badly at a key moment, such as an interview or a presentation. The dream reflects a fear of missing out, and in real life there is usually still time to prepare.

variants.q: Dreaming of not finding the exam room or your seat
variants.a: Usually matches facing a new role or task where you haven't found your footing yet. The dream acts out the feeling of not knowing where you are.

variants.q: Dreaming of getting the exam paper and finding it blank
variants.a: Often connected to a fear of being underprepared, especially when you have something important to deliver soon. The dream magnifies the worry of going blank on the spot.

variants.q: Dreaming of still looking for a pen as the exam is about to start
variants.a: Common when you feel a key resource or support is lacking, such as people, time, or information. It reflects the feeling of being stuck during preparation.

variants.q: Dreaming of realizing after the exam that you took the wrong subject
variants.a: Usually has to do with a fear of putting effort in the wrong direction, and you may be hesitating over whether a choice is right. The dream shows that worry of having worked for nothing.

missing-exam.ask: If a particular person appears in the dream, or you can't put down the test you're afraid of not doing well on, you can cast a hexagram on it and see which days ahead may bring movement.
missing-exam.askQ: Will the challenge I'm about to face go smoothly?

faq.q: Does dreaming of being late to an exam mean I'll do badly?
faq.a: No, it isn't a warning. Exam dreams mostly reflect how much you care about being evaluated. They point to pressure during the day, not to a real-life result.

faq.q: Is it normal to dream of being late to an exam long after graduating?
faq.a: Very common. In dreams, exams often stand for situations where you feel tested, and work or relationships can trigger them. If they keep coming back and you're not sleeping well, you can talk to a doctor.
